product_outlooks.label: ATM & cash automation / recycling
product_outlooks.scope: ATM fleet conversion: dispense-only machines becoming deposit machines
product_outlooks.summary:
This line is growing, but almost none of the growth is in the number of machines. ATM fleets across Printec's markets are flat or shrinking. The spending is going into the machines that already exist. Banks are turning cash-out-only ATMs into recyclers, which are machines that re-use the notes customers have just paid in.

Two dated requirements drive the next twelve months. First, every bank directly supervised by the European Central Bank must give its supervisor a plan by 31 October 2026. That plan must name the “legacy, unsupported or end-of-life” technology the bank will replace, which covers ATMs still running unsupported operating systems ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)). Second, Hungary has passed a law under which ATMs may be replaced but never removed ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The pool of machines to convert is no longer an estimate. It is a count taken from the banks' own data feeds. Two thirds of BCR's 1,668 Romanian devices cannot take a deposit. Roughly 1,840 to 1,950 dispense-only sites sit across Bulgaria's four largest banks ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec should aim this line at those named fleets and at the two contests that are already open, in Austria and Ukraine. It should sell device telemetry, meaning remote machine monitoring, and cash-cycle software together with the hardware rather than afterwards.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, and the timing is unusually easy to date. The firmest trigger anywhere in Printec's markets is the European Central Bank's supervisory letter SSM-2026-0301, signed 7 July 2026. It tells every significant institution to send an artificial-intelligence and cyber action plan to its Joint Supervisory Team by 31 October 2026. Focus area 5 requires the replacement of legacy, unsupported and end-of-life technology. Focus area 1 requires an accurate inventory of information-technology assets. On 31 July 2026 the three European supervisory authorities extended the same expectation to nationally supervised mid-market banks, which is where most of Printec's estate sits ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Hungary is the second dated force. Since 14 May 2026, Act XIV of 2026 has banned a bank from shutting down any ATM that existed when the Act came into force. It expressly allows replacement instead. The law itself expects that the replacement machine may not fit the old opening, because of its size and security requirements. That is exactly what happens when a through-the-wall dispenser is swapped for a deposit or recycling machine. Alongside it, Act XVIII still requires ATM cash withdrawal in every settlement above 500 inhabitants by 31 December 2026, across 1,039 named settlements allocated to nine banks ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Two contests are open now rather than expected later. Geldservice Austria's EUR 9.1m banknote and coin recycler framework was checked again on 31 August 2026 and was still unawarded. The recorded contract start is 2 November 2026, and call-off deliveries under it can reach Slovenia, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)). PrivatBank's recycler renewal closed stage-one qualification on 25 August 2026. The commercial round is the next step, on a specification written to a Diebold Nixdorf software baseline ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Croatia adds a structural deadline of 1 January 2027. By then the banks must set up a national shared ATM network, or let any consumer withdraw free twice a month at any bank ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

Where to aim: at the counted conversion populations rather than the market totals.

- Romania: BCR's 1,100 dispense-only machines, and CEC Bank's roughly 350 branches marked for operating-model redesign.
- Hungary: MBH's 1,029 cash-out-only machines, of which the 803 inherited from Takarékbank take no deposits at all, plus OTP Hungary's 1,220.
- Bulgaria: the 1,840 to 1,950 dispense-only sites across UBB, Postbank, DSK and UniCredit Bulbank.
- Croatia: Zagrebačka banka's 562, ahead of the shared-network decision.
- Serbia: AikBank's 457 of 570. The bank refits a branch roughly every two weeks to a published standard specification, so the target is the standard rather than the site.
- Czechia: the 944 cash-out-only machines in the four-bank pool, worst at MONETA and Air Bank.
- Slovakia: the retrofit tail, where cash desks have gone from only 25 of 121 VÚB branches and 16 of 47 at UniCredit.

([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

In short: run this line as a conversion programme driven by supervisory deadlines, aimed at named machine populations. Attach device telemetry, cash forecasting and multivendor ATM software to every machine.
drivers: The European Central Bank's letter SSM-2026-0301 of 7 July 2026 sets a deadline of 31 October 2026. By then every significant institution must name its legacy, unsupported and end-of-life technology in a plan that a supervisor reads. The same expectation was pushed down to nationally supervised banks on 31 July 2026. An ageing ATM on an unsupported operating system falls squarely inside that wording ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Hungary has turned a shrinking fleet into a guaranteed replacement market. Act XIV of 2026 bans the removal of any existing machine from 14 May 2026, but allows replacement. Act XVIII requires cash withdrawal in 1,039 named settlements by 31 December 2026. A hand-over of ATM operation cannot be contracted for less than five years ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

The white space is now counted rather than estimated. Croatia's central bank publishes a machine-readable national cash-point registry. It returned 6,852 records on 27 August 2026, of which 3,841 are cash-out-only ATMs. Zagrebačka banka is the weakest of the big four, with a 19.6% deposit share. The same matching-date method gives Bulgaria's four largest banks roughly 1,840 to 1,950 dispense-only sites, and BCR exactly 1,100 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Two contests are open inside the horizon. Geldservice Austria's EUR 9.1m recycler and coin framework was still unawarded on 31 August 2026. It has a 2 November 2026 contract start and delivery reach into four further Printec countries. PrivatBank's recycler renewal closed stage-one qualification on 25 August 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Branch cash desks are being removed faster than machines are being added, which pushes the cash into the lobby. Across Slovakia's five largest banks, 93 of 128 Slovenská sporiteľňa branches now have no cash desk. The same is true at 48 of 69 Tatra branches and at 47 of 120 ČSOB branches. The banks name security rules, staff training and vault equipment as the costs they are escaping ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec's main ATM supplier, NCR Atleos, is being bought by Brink's, a direct competitor in managed services. The UK Competition and Markets Authority opened a Phase 1 inquiry on 26 August 2026, with a decision deadline of 22 October 2026. Completion has been brought forward to early Q1 2027. That is a supply-channel question to settle before signing any multi-year fleet commitment.

Deposit volume is growing far faster than the fleet that carries it. Bulgaria's national fleet fell to 5,031 ATMs at end-2025 from a peak of 5,751. At the same time, ATM deposits reached 12.53m transactions worth EUR 7.2bn, up about 50% by value. Fewer machines doing much more cash-in work is the recycler business case in plain numbers ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
What changed this cycle is that the case for conversion stopped being an argument and became an inventory. In the four weeks to 31 August 2026, the banks' own ATM locator feeds and two central-bank registries were pulled on matching dates. The dispense-only population can now be addressed machine by machine and provider by provider, rather than estimated from market totals ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The supervisory calendar also became firm. An ATM running an unsupported operating system used to be quiet technical debt. The 31 October 2026 filing turns it into a fix-list item that a supervisor will read and then track. The annual information-technology risk questionnaire moving to February 2027 lengthens the evidence window rather than closing it ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The two largest single contests in the line, Austria and Ukraine, both reached their decision stage in the last weeks of August 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

By opportunity value this is the largest of Printec's six lines, at EUR 377.8m. But it is a replacement and conversion cycle inside fleets that are not growing, not an expansion. It should be planned that way.
cite_ungrounded: The NCR Atleos / Brink's transaction in its entirety — the acquisition itself, Brink's status as a managed-services competitor, the UK Competition and Markets Authority Phase 1 inquiry opened 26/08/2026, the 22/10/2026 decision deadline and the early-Q1-2027 completion date. None of it appears in any signal tagged to this line; it was supplied as briefing context and must be re-sourced before it is put in front of a customer.
The characterisation of atm_recycling as the largest of the six lines by opportunity value rests on comparing the six `m` figures supplied with this task, not on any signal.

product_outlooks.label: Self-service, kiosks & branch transformation
product_outlooks.scope: Branch counter closures and the move of counter work to lobby machines
product_outlooks.summary:
This line grows because banks are removing the teller, not the branch. Across Printec's markets, the counter is being taken out of buildings that stay open. The cash and paperwork it used to handle has to go somewhere. The usual replacements are a lobby recycler, a business cash-deposit machine, a bill-payment kiosk or a video-advisory pod.

The volumes make the case on their own. Albania's branch counters took in ALL 783.7bn of cash deposits in the first half of 2026. That is roughly eleven times what the whole national ATM estate took in ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)). In Cyprus almost nine in ten deposits already arrive at a machine ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The largest named pipelines are in Romania and at NLB. CEC Bank has marked roughly 350 Romanian branches for operating-model redesign, against only 46 that have a 24/7 zone today. NLB has committed to a group-wide cash-deposit upgrade across six markets ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec should sell a repeatable per-site package: counter recycler, deposit machine, kiosk, queueing and accessible fit-out. The aim is to win the template rather than the individual branch.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, driven by banks cutting counter staff rather than by network expansion. The branch estates being kept open matter most.

CEC Bank's 2025 audited report names an Operational Model Redesign Program covering roughly 350 rural and urban branches, built around self-service equipment and remote advice. The measured base today is only 46 of 1,011 units with a 24/7 self-service zone. Its Cash2Card launch on 4 August 2026 lets anyone deposit cash onto any Romanian bank's Visa or Mastercard debit card, on a fleet of over 270 multifunction machines. This justifies the spend, because each new deposit point now serves the whole national card base ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

In Cyprus, Eurobank Limited disclosed on 6 August 2026 that 95% of withdrawals and almost 90% of deposits now happen at machines rather than counters. It has two legacy estates to standardise before an April 2027 core-banking cutover ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

NLB has put a named group programme behind the same idea. It is an ATM and cash-deposit-system upgrade that moves cash out of branches. Branch cash transactions fell from 32% at end-2023 to 13.5% in March 2026, against a target below 10%. Three cash-light branches opened in Slovenia in the first half of 2026, and a EUR 160–200m technology budget sits behind Strategy 2030 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Two Greek programmes carry hard dates. Comments on ELTA's EUR 6m retail and delivery transformation specification close on 10 September 2026 through the ESIDIS platform. That is the only moment its scope can still be shaped. ODAP's EUR 30.0m visitor-services procurement closed for tenders on 23 July 2026, with no award published as at 27 August 2026. Its classification set explicitly includes ticket-issuing machines ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Where to aim:

- CEC Bank and BCR in Romania, where 211 of BCR's 282 branches already run with no cash desk and depend on lobby machines staying up.
- Eurobank Limited in Cyprus, before the April 2027 cutover.
- NLB group procurement in Ljubljana rather than any single subsidiary.
- Komercijalna banka in North Macedonia, which has now repeated the same modernised-branch template at five or more sites.
- VÚB and UniCredit in Slovakia, as the counter estates least converted so far.
- DSK in Bulgaria, where exactly one site in 777 has a kiosk device and coin deposit is entirely manual. That is the entry point with the least competition in that market.
- The Greek consortium routes into ELTA and ODAP, where Printec's realistic position is under a systems integrator rather than as a prime contractor.

([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md))

In short: turn one per-site package into a product and sell the branch standard. At CEC, Komercijalna and AikBank the specification is copied site by site rather than re-tendered.
drivers: Counters are being removed from branches that stay open. Across Slovakia's five largest banks the cash desk has already gone from 93 of 128 Slovenská sporiteľňa branches, 48 of 69 at Tatra and 47 of 120 at ČSOB. That leaves VÚB at 25 of 121 and UniCredit at 16 of 47 as the largest remaining refit pipelines ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

CEC Bank has published its own pipeline. Roughly 350 branches are named for operating-model redesign, against 46 of 1,011 units with a 24/7 self-service zone today. The Cash2Card national deposit service, launched 4 August 2026, is the business case ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The counter still handles the cash. Albania's central bank recorded 2,279,914 over-the-counter cash deposits worth ALL 783.7bn in the first half of 2026, against ATM deposits of ALL 68.6bn. It had 408 branches at end-2025, up from 400. So this is fit-out demand in a growing network, not closures ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Montenegro shows the same flow for businesses. Roughly EUR 2.9bn a year of company cash still arrives at a teller. CKB reopened its Podgorica Business Point on 24 July 2026 with no counter cash at all, on a transition closing around 24 January 2027. That is a dated template to quote to the other ten banks ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Two Greek public programmes are inside their decision window. ELTA's EUR 6m retail and delivery transformation is open for comments on its specification until 10 September 2026. ODAP's EUR 30.0m visitor-services award, covering ticket-issuing machines across 125 sites, was still unpublished on 27 August 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo has turned from a build market into a refit market. The commercial-bank network peaked at 237 units in August 2025 and has stayed at 234 since March 2026. So the roughly 35 units opened since 2022 are the target base for counter recyclers and kiosks ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

The kiosk layer beyond the ATM is almost untouched at the region's largest retail network. Exactly one of DSK Bank's 777 Bulgarian sites has a kiosk device, and coin deposit is 100% manual at the counter. This sits against a disclosed 22% year-on-year rise in Bulgarian operating expenses, which the bank puts partly down to information-technology costs ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
The trigger is that cutting staff has moved faster than automation. Branch counts are falling far more slowly than the people behind them. BCR now runs 211 of 282 branches with no staffed cash desk and only 71 with a teller. The lobby machines therefore carry the load rather than being a convenience ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Where branches are being kept flat or opened, as in Albania, Kosovo and at VÚB in Slovakia, the same automation is bought as fit-out instead of as closure.

What is new this cycle is that the buyers have published their own specifications. Postbank has defined exactly two Express Banking device types, a cash device and a cashless kiosk, and named network expansion among its coming initiatives ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)). Komercijalna banka has repeated one modernised-branch template across at least five sites ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)). CEC has named the branch count.

When the customer writes the requirement, the product being sold is the standard. Those standards are being set now.
cite_ungrounded: Postbank's two published Express Banking device types are cited in the rationale from the postbank-eurobank-bulgaria-postbank-next-branch-format-rebuild signal, which sits in the card_issuing slice rather than in this line's own slice; the claim is sourced but the routing key is not in cite_signals.

product_outlooks.label: POS, acquiring & terminal management
product_outlooks.scope: Legal card-acceptance mandates and the growth of terminal estates
product_outlooks.summary:
Card acceptance is the fastest-growing area Printec sells into. The growth is being ordered by law rather than chosen by merchants. Albania's terminal count rose 57.9% in eighteen months to 38,662, under a legal duty that covers the last businesses on 31 December 2026. Kosovo added roughly 9,400 terminals in a single year. Slovakia's eKasa duty to accept a cashless payment on any sale above EUR 1 has been in force since 1 May 2026 ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

At the same time, the terminal itself is becoming a commodity underneath that growth. Three things pull margin out of the hardware: tap-to-phone software terminals; hardware-abstraction specifications that make different makes interchangeable; and a Bulgarian terminal maker that now owns its own acquiring rail. An acquiring rail is the network used to process card payments.

The lasting revenue is therefore in the layer above the device. It covers terminal management, remote key injection, certification, monitoring and field logistics. Remote key injection means loading security keys onto terminals remotely. The buyers are acquirers, the banks and firms that process card payments for merchants, and they run mixed hardware-and-software estates.

Printec should aim this line at the acquirers doing the deploying rather than at the merchants. The lead argument is the complexity of running the estate.
product_outlooks.projected:
Strong growth in volume is expected, with the value moving from the terminal to the platform that runs it.

The clearest mandates are dated. Albania's Law on Tax Procedures, as amended at end-2025, requires accommodation, transport and public enterprises to have a terminal from end-May 2026. Everyone else must have one by 31 December 2026. The central bank's own series already shows 38,662 terminals at end-Q2-2026, against 24,481 at end-2024. The POSi free-terminal programme runs through five named acquirers until 31 December 2026 ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Slovakia's Act 384/2025 has been in force since 1 January 2026, with the acceptance duty applying from 1 May 2026. It carries a scale of fines rising to EUR 3,000–40,000 per further detection, and the possible loss of a trade licence. Its section 15(3) expressly allows a third party to supply the technical means that confirm a QR payment back to the cash register. That is a legal opening. The Financial Directorate had still not published its specification on 27 August 2026 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo's acceptance estate jumped 45% to about 30,300 terminals in one year. Montenegro's reached an all-time high of 23,250 in the first quarter of 2026. That is up roughly 4,475 in five quarters, in a market of 633,000 people ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Against that, three things weaken the economics of hardware and must be priced in. North Macedonia's central bank has publicly named the cost of the acceptance device as the barrier. It is backing a national interoperable QR code, aliases and request-to-pay, while NLB ships a certified tap-on-phone application ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)). Romania's newly obliged merchants are being served largely by bank software-POS applications and shared terminals rather than by new devices ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)). And a Bulgarian terminal manufacturer had its payment-institution licence extended on 27 August 2026 to cover cash withdrawal and payment-instrument issuing, on top of an existing acquiring rail ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Where to aim: the acquirers carrying the deployment load.

- Albania: Raiffeisen, Union Bank, BKT, Credins and OTP, where Printec's own footprint is roughly 150 terminals against a national estate of 38,662.
- Bosnia and Herzegovina: UniCredit Bank d.d. Mostar, the largest card-acceptance estate in the Federation at 11,131 terminals, with falling software capitalisation and two shareholder-ordered audits running.
- Romania: Raiffeisen Romania, as its 45,000-terminal book folds into the Garanti BBVA integration closing in early October 2026, and Banca Transilvania's 200,000-plus installed terminals.
- Slovakia: Penta Bank, a greenfield platform build with a new chief executive, operating officer and finance officer, where acquiring and key management are all still being chosen.

([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

One live public contest is worth tracking whatever the bid decision. Operátor ICT's CZK 250m Prague payment gateway was republished with a 31 August 2026 deadline, and an award is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

In short: sell one management platform across several acceptance formats, which are attended, unattended and phone-based. Take the recurring estate revenue rather than the device.
drivers: Three separate legal mandates land inside the horizon. Albania's terminal duty covers all remaining businesses on 31 December 2026, on an estate already up 23.7% in six months to 38,662. Slovakia's eKasa acceptance duty on any sale above EUR 1 has applied since 1 May 2026, with a scale of fines that can cost a merchant its trade licence. Romania's acceptance duty has been reported in force since 1 January 2026 ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

The estates are growing fast where the mandates are softer too. Kosovo's card-accepting terminals rose about 45% to 30,300 in a year, and Montenegro's to an all-time high of 23,250. The Bosnian Federation added 3,079 terminals in six months, against thirty more ATMs ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Value is moving out of the device. North Macedonia's central bank has named device cost as the barrier. It is backing a national QR code, an alias directory and request-to-pay. NLB's certified tap-on-phone application, where the merchant's own handset becomes the terminal, grew installations 46% year on year ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

A structural competitor has put the whole stack together. On 27 August 2026 the Bulgarian National Bank extended DatecsPay's licence to cover cash withdrawal, card-transaction execution, credit transfers and instrument issuing. It already holds an acquiring rail passported and agented into Romania. A terminal maker like this can bundle in a way a reseller cannot match on price ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Whole banks have no acquiring estate at all. Seven of the thirteen banks headquartered in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina reported zero own POS terminals at 30 June 2026. So acceptance there is a build, not a fight to displace someone ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Bank-side buying teams are forming now. ČSOB in Czechia posted five concurrent international-acquiring vacancies inside four weeks in August 2026. That was a third of the whole national demand for the skill. Platform and terminal-vendor choices freeze once those architects are in post ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
Two things are happening at the same time. Terminal estates are being expanded by law on fixed dates, Albania on 31 December 2026 and Slovakia since 1 May 2026. Acquirers are therefore adding thousands of devices in months, and physically cannot manage them by hand. That turns terminal management, remote key injection and deployment logistics from a nice-to-have into the operational bottleneck ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

At the same time the hardware itself is being deliberately turned into a commodity. Banks specify hardware-abstraction layers so one payment application runs unchanged across makes. Regulators sponsor phone-based acceptance to cut device cost. And a manufacturer with its own acquiring licence can undercut any reseller ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

The timing matters for two reasons. A fleet installed in one burst starts its refresh clock at the same time. And the acquirers deciding how to run these estates are hiring the people who will choose the platform.
cite_ungrounded: DatecsPay's 27/08/2026 licence supplement and its Romanian acquiring agency, the seven Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina banks with zero own POS estate, and ČSOB Czechia's five August-2026 acquiring vacancies are all sourced, but their signal keys sit in the card_issuing and payments_instant slices rather than in this line's slice, so they are not represented in cite_signals.

Raiffeisen Romania's “nearly 45,000” POS terminals at 30/06/2026 comes from the raiffeisen-bank-romania-1-211-device-own-estate signal in the payments_instant slice, which is not among this card's cite_signals.

product_outlooks.label: Managed services / outsourcing
product_outlooks.scope: Managed services: regulatory duties on uptime, patching and telemetry
product_outlooks.summary:
Managed services grows over the next year because supervisors, not sales teams, are making the case. The European Central Bank's 31 October 2026 filing reaches into the contract terms and service levels of every information-technology supplier at a significant institution. Bosnia's Federation banks must file an external audit of their systems by 31 March 2027. Kosovo's own resilience rulebook has been binding since 1 June 2026. It names ATMs as critical infrastructure, and their make, model and firmware must be reported within four hours of an incident ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Cutting branch staff has also made uptime essential. 211 of BCR's 282 Romanian branches now run with no cash desk and depend on lobby machines staying up ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec should aim this line at estates where a regulator has created a reporting duty that the bank cannot meet from its own records. It should sell device telemetry, meaning remote machine monitoring, together with documented patching and auditable key management, as the evidence pack. The one thing to settle first is the supply channel, because Printec's main ATM supplier is changing owners.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, with the buying decision moving from information-technology managers to boards, because the requirements now arrive as regulatory filings.

The European Central Bank's letter SSM-2026-0301 requires an artificial-intelligence and cyber action plan to be with the supervisor by 31 October 2026. Its focus area 1 demands accurate information-technology asset inventories, which is a device-telemetry sale. Focus area 2 pulls patching into the contract terms and service levels of any external service provider. The same letter is therefore both an opening and a duty to review every Printec managed-service agreement at a supervised bank ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina makes the same demand on a national calendar. Its binding information-technology risk decision has applied since 31 December 2025. Every one of the thirteen Federation banks must file a standalone external audit of its systems each year, next by 31 March 2027. Supervisory expectations also require penetration testing, continuous monitoring and a full register of every outsourced activity, with direct board accountability ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo's central bank went further and earlier. Its resilience regulation has bound every financial institution since 1 June 2026. It requires notification within four hours of discovering an incident, and names ATMs among the critical systems. Its most useful clause in that market requires the cybersecurity budget to be separate from the overall information-technology budget, so business projects cannot compete with it ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Two commercial triggers sit alongside the regulatory ones. Hungary's rural mandate cannot be handed over on a contract of less than five years. That turns each of the 80 settlement packages into a multi-year operating relationship rather than a supply order ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)). Ageing estates are already paying for this in the wrong budget line. NLB Komercijalna's maintenance bill for electronic-banking equipment rose 30.7% year on year to RSD 207.8m, which is the exact spend a managed contract replaces ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Where to aim:

- BCR in Romania, where three quarters of branches have no cash desk, so service levels are contractual rather than optional.
- NLB Komercijalna in Serbia, where 49 towns have a machine and no branch behind it. Remote monitoring and predictive maintenance earn their fee there without waiting for a refresh.
- The thirteen Federation banks, and the Republika Srpska banks under the parallel rule.
- Every Kosovo bank, against the four-hour reporting duty.
- The nine Hungarian banks holding settlement packages.
- The two Croatian government lots decided inside a month. One is scored on price plus response time to a service call-out, where a dense field team wins on merit ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

In short: sell the regulator's own evidence requirement, which is asset inventory, patch record, incident pipeline and service levels written into the contract. Let the hardware follow.
drivers: The 31 October 2026 European Central Bank filing writes patching into “contractual terms and service level agreements when an ICT service provider is involved”, and requires accurate asset inventories. So it creates demand for device telemetry and managed patching. It also requires a review of every existing Printec service agreement at a supervised bank ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Bosnia's Federation Banking Agency requires a standalone external audit of each bank's information systems, filed by 31 March every year and next on 31 March 2027. This applies across all thirteen Federation banks. On top of that, supervisory expectations cover penetration testing, continuous monitoring and a register of every outsourced activity, with board accountability ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo's resilience regulation has been binding since 1 June 2026. It requires incident notification within four hours, and names ATMs explicitly among critical systems. The report must give the affected hardware manufacturer, software developer, make and model. No bank can produce that without visibility of its estate ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Uptime is now essential rather than convenient. 211 of BCR's 282 branches are tagged cashless with no staffed cash desk, and only 71 still run a teller counter. So incident management and cash forecasting become the lead product rather than an add-on ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The cost is already being paid in maintenance rather than in service. NLB Komercijalna's electronic-banking equipment maintenance rose 30.7% year on year to RSD 207.8m, while capital work in progress rose 15.7%. 49 of the towns it covers have a machine and no branch behind it ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Structural events create multi-year operating work rather than one-off supply. Hungary's hand-over of rural ATM operation cannot be contracted for under five years across 80 settlement packages. Croatia must set up a shared national ATM network by 1 January 2027. That needs multivendor software, monitoring and field services rather than devices alone ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

Printec's main ATM supplier, NCR Atleos, is being bought by Brink's, which competes directly in managed services. The UK Competition and Markets Authority opened a Phase 1 inquiry on 26 August 2026, with a decision deadline of 22 October 2026. Completion was brought forward to early Q1 2027. A supplier becoming a competitor in this specific line is a channel question to resolve before signing long-dated service commitments.
product_outlooks.rationale:
The change is that the requirement is now filed rather than argued. Until this cycle, telemetry, documented patching and service levels were an efficiency pitch. From 31 October 2026 a significant institution has to name its unsupported technology to a supervisor. From 1 June 2026 a Kosovo bank has to report an ATM incident within four hours, with make and model. And by 31 March 2027 every Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina bank has to give a regulator an external audit of its systems ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Each of those is a document a bank cannot produce from its own records if it does not know what is in its estate.

The operational dependency has also become real. Branch counters have been removed faster than the machines behind them were modernised. A machine that is down is now a branch that cannot serve cash ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

One factor pulls the other way, and it sits on the supply side rather than the demand side. The ownership of the hardware channel is changing, and this call depends on how that settles.
cite_ungrounded: The NCR Atleos / Brink's transaction in its entirety — the acquisition, Brink's position as a managed-services competitor, the UK Competition and Markets Authority Phase 1 inquiry of 26/08/2026, the 22/10/2026 decision deadline and the early-Q1-2027 completion. It was supplied as briefing context and does not trace to any signal tagged to this line.

Kosovo's Central Bank Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management — the 01/06/2026 compliance date, the four-hour incident notification, the naming of ATMs in the reporting template and the ring-fenced cybersecurity budget in Article 10 — is sourced, but its signal key sits in the payments_instant slice; the Kosovo key carried in cite_signals is the Law 08/L-304 banking-compliance row, which is a different instrument.

product_outlooks.label: Payments modernization (instant / ISO 20022)
product_outlooks.scope: Payments: two fixed cutover dates inside the next twelve months
product_outlooks.summary:
This is the smallest of Printec's large lines at EUR 100.0m, and it carries the firmest dates. On 14–15 November 2026 the unstructured postal address stops being accepted across the European payment scheme rulebooks and the euro settlement system. The practical deadline is earlier: testing closes on 28 October 2026. Messages that do not conform are simply rejected ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Seven weeks later, on 1 January 2027, every payment service provider licensed in Bulgaria must send instant euro transfers and run Verification of Payee. Verification of Payee is the check that the name on a transfer matches the account. European primary law names the ATM and the self-service terminal among the channels in scope ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Czech, Hungarian and Romanian banks follow on 9 January and 9 July 2027. The whole Western Balkans is joining a shared instant-payment rail in a November 2026 window.

Printec should aim this line at the layer around the settlement core. That means address and party-data cleansing, real-time sanctions and money-laundering screening, name-matching at the machine, and reject monitoring through the cutover weekend.
product_outlooks.projected:
Strong growth is expected, because every driver is a deadline rather than a preference.

The first is the ISO 20022 structured-address cutover. European Payments Council guidance EPC153-22 v2.1 fixes 15 November 2026 as the end of the unstructured address across four scheme rulebooks. It states that its use “will hence lead to rejects” on both the inter-bank leg and corporate file upload. The euro real-time settlement release goes into production on Saturday 14 November 2026. Its testing window opens on 25 September and closes on 28 October 2026 ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Two rules go with it and cap the scope. Seven core payment messages stay on the 2019 version until probably November 2027, so a core schema migration is the wrong scope this year. And only the structured Town and Country fields are needed for regulatory screening ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The second driver is Verification of Payee. Because Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, Article 16(9) of Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 applies one year later. From 1 January 2027 every provider licensed there must send instant euro transfers at price parity, meaning the same price as a standard transfer, and run payee-name matching. Recital 11 of Regulation 2024/886 names “an automated teller machine, a self-service terminal” expressly among the initiation channels. That turns a payments-department item into a device-estate item for any bank that limited the work to online and mobile ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Czech banks must receive by 9 January 2027 and send with Verification of Payee by 9 July 2027. The Czech National Bank has said plainly that it runs no euro instant rail, so every Czech bank buys its own reachability ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)). Romania has the same dates. It also has a national ordinance requiring ten-second settlement across all payment-initiation channels, plus regular reporting of fees and rejected transactions ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

The third driver is the Western Balkans build-out. The TIPS Clone platform went live on 20 July 2026 with Bosnia and Montenegro. Montenegro's eleven banks all joined at once, under a compulsory Verification of Payee duty and a five-cent fee cap. Bosnia's rulebook makes participation compulsory from 1 January 2027, with about sixteen banks still outside and a five-second execution ceiling. Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected in a November 2026 window ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Where to aim:

- The roughly sixteen Bosnian banks outside the instant scheme.
- The small-team Montenegrin banks: Adriatic, Zapad, Universal Capital, Ziraat and Lovćen. One packaged real-time monitoring and name-matching offer sells eleven times there.
- The Bulgarian banks that limited Verification of Payee to online and mobile and now have a gap on their machines.
- The named Czech institutions buying their own euro instant stack.
- The seven Macedonian banks facing two integrations on two calendars.
- Above all, the non-European Union markets: Serbia, Bosnia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo and Ukraine. These are the largest un-owned pocket on the address cutover, because no domestic regulator forces it while correspondent-bank flows do ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

In short: sell emergency fixes in September and October 2026 on the address cutover. Sell commit-window integration work now for the January and July 2027 instant-payment dates.
drivers: The address cutover is a network hard stop, not a target. Unstructured postal addresses stop being allowed across the scheme rulebooks on 15 November 2026 and will cause rejects. The euro settlement release deploys on 14 November 2026. The true deadline is the close of testing on 28 October 2026 ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Verification of Payee reaches the machine estate as a matter of primary European law. Recital 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/886 names the automated teller machine and the self-service terminal among initiation channels. Bulgarian law defines an ATM as a device that also executes transfers between payment accounts. So a bank that limited payee verification to online and mobile has an open gap on 1 January 2027 ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Four non-euro markets buy the same three things inside eighteen months. These are instant message handling, a name match that answers in under a second, and sanctions screening that clears in real time. The whole customer book must also be re-screened daily under Article 5d ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Czechia is a pure vendor market by the regulator's own statement. The Czech National Bank confirms it does not operate the euro instant system and has nothing to do with CERTIS. So every named Czech bank must buy its own reachability against 9 January and 9 July 2027 ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

The Western Balkans rail is live and compulsory rather than planned. Montenegro put all eleven banks on TIPS Clone on 20 July 2026, with mandatory Verification of Payee, fines of EUR 10,000–40,000 and an irrevocable ten-second rail. Bosnia's rulebook sets a five-second execution ceiling and compulsory participation from 1 January 2027, with roughly sixteen banks still outside ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

An irrevocable rail with no overnight batch window removes the chance to review fraud after the fact. That is what pulls inline sanctions and money-laundering screening, real-time transaction monitoring, hardware security module capacity and 24/7 managed operations through behind every go-live ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Ukraine's duty is already binding rather than coming. National Bank Resolution No. 85 of 5 August 2026 required every participant, from 7 August 2026, to push payment-execution status to the central processor within one hour. That includes the non-bank providers that settle through its accounts. The customer-facing status query follows on 1 January 2027 ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
This is a decision for now rather than for 2027 because of simple budget arithmetic. Money for a January 2027 go-live had to be committed in the first half of 2026. Anything still uncommitted by roughly September 2026 becomes 2027 remediation, bought at remediation prices. The programme window for the address cutover has already closed, leaving September and October 2026 as an emergency-fix market ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Two facts became clearer this cycle, and both widen the addressable scope. The Bulgarian legal basis was settled from the Official Journal text rather than left as a regulator's claim. The same reading put ATMs and self-service terminals expressly inside payee-verification scope.

The Western Balkans rail also stopped being a plan. It went into production on 20 July 2026, with a second onboarding window in November 2026. Albanian, Kosovar and Macedonian banks are therefore behind, and are buying integration capacity inside one quarter ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).
cite_ungrounded: The European Payments Council's own site was Cloudflare-blocked to every collection route this cycle, and the master record flags five EPC scheme dates as unverified at primary. The 15/11/2026 address date used here rests on the re-downloaded EPC153-22 v2.1 guidance and on the Bundesbank's independent 14/11/2026 production date; it should not be quoted to a customer as a certification deadline without that caveat.
The description of payments_instant as the smallest of Printec's large lines rests on comparing the six `m` figures supplied with this task, not on any signal.

product_outlooks.label: Card issuing & management
product_outlooks.scope: Card issuing: national processors hold the core, with openings at the edges
product_outlooks.summary:
This line is expected to stay flat. At EUR 30.6m across just 13 opportunity rows in 10 markets, card issuing is the smallest line by a wide margin. It has no driver of its own inside the horizon. It depends on the instant-payments build-out and on a handful of bank-side platform cutovers.

The reason is structural. The card issuing and lifecycle core is held by national processors that will not be displaced. BORICA's Way4 platform is the technological foundation of Bulgaria's national card infrastructure. Bankart is 100% bank-owned and controls both the ATM and POS networks for its Slovenian members. CaSys has made the Macedonian Banking Association its structural channel ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Movement is limited to the edges. A Croatian bank has said in writing that its card ecosystem must change. A Czech bank is staffing an international acquiring platform. A Romanian card-platform programme is running. Printec's realistic positions there are key management, card personalisation, terminal-side work and instant card issuance, not the platform itself.

Plan the line flat and take the adjacent work.
product_outlooks.projected:
Flat, and it should be planned that way rather than talked up. The structural reason is that the layer this line would sell into is already held by processors that banks own or depend on.

OpenWay's Way4 platform was confirmed on 23 July 2026 as the technological foundation of Bulgaria's national card infrastructure. It covers authorisation, card issuing, merchant servicing, switching, ATM and POS device management, fraud prevention and processing across more than 35 participants ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Bankart is the single chokepoint for Slovenian issuing, lifecycle, acquiring processing and terminal management. It is wholly bank-owned and runs development as seventeen in-house product teams. It is a gatekeeper to qualify with rather than an account to sell to. Its new chief technology officer, appointed 17 April 2026, is the moment technology roadmaps reopen ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

In North Macedonia the domestic processor CaSys signed a memorandum with the Macedonian Banking Association on 30 April 2026, covering payment infrastructure, cybersecurity and fraud prevention. That raises rather than lowers the barrier to selling bank by bank ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Two market events pulled issuing scope further away this year. Erste Croatia completed the sale of Erste Card Club to Global Payments in January 2026, booking a EUR 116m gain. The Croatian acquiring estate now sits with a new owner that will move it to its own platform. Worldline's bank-facing division shrank 7.1% organically in the first half of 2026, on EUR 60m of contract terminations. Management says it will not return to growth before the second half of 2027. That brings outsourced estates back to market, but it is a processing rather than an issuing opening ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Where to aim:

- Hrvatska poštanska banka. Its live vacancy states that the bank has defined a card strategy that “requires implementing changes in our card ecosystem” across both issuing and acquiring. It also won the Hrvatske autoceste motorway acceptance contract at EUR 1,141,358, dated 7 April 2026 and published 7 August 2026, so it must field a new unattended terminal estate. It is the best-qualified card buying centre in Printec's markets, and the decision is taken in Zagreb rather than at a group hub.
- ČSOB Czechia, which posted five international-acquiring vacancies inside four weeks in August 2026, ahead of a KBC digital-transformation investor event on 11 February 2027.
- Banca Transilvania, whose board-approved 2026 sub-lines include IT and cards at RON 663.17m. Only the machines, cash-processing-centre and security lines of RON 39.06m are close to hardware and quotable.
- OTP Albania, three to twelve months after its end-May 2026 card-services cutover, which is exactly when terminal re-certification, key management and monitoring get bought.
- The Greek OPSEA security-documents competitive dialogue, whose stage-one deadline was extended again to 10 September 2026. The realistic position there is enrolment kiosks, personalisation, key management and field service, under whichever prime contractor goes forward.

([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md))

In short: expect no growth from this line on its own. Carry it as an attachment to instant payments, acquiring platform builds and merger card migrations. Treat CETIS in Slovenia as a regional personalisation partner rather than a competitor.
drivers: The core is held and will not be displaced inside the horizon. Way4 underpins Bulgaria's national card infrastructure end to end. BORICA holds the state acquiring rail on a formally declared sole-source incumbency extended to 29 May 2027. Bankart controls Slovenian issuing and lifecycle with seventeen in-house product teams. CaSys has the Macedonian Banking Association as its channel ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).
The line is small and thinly spread: EUR 30.6m across 13 opportunity rows in ten markets. So a single bank programme would move it, and no programme of that size is dated inside the horizon.

Issuing scope has been leaving rather than arriving. Erste Croatia's sale of Erste Card Club to Global Payments closed in January 2026 for a EUR 116m gain and cut Croatian fee income 13.2%. That removed an in-house payments arm. The estate now sits with an owner that will move it to its own platform on its own timetable ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The one bank that has publicly declared a platform change is Hrvatska poštanska banka. Its card-strategy vacancy was confirmed live on 31 August 2026, and states that the bank's card ecosystem must change across both issuing and acquiring. It also won a motorway acceptance contract at EUR 1,141,358 that forces a new unattended terminal estate ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

The second is ČSOB Czechia, which posted five concurrent international-acquiring roles in August 2026. These were a business architect, an IT process manager, a business development manager, an application engineer and a card scheme manager. This is a platform programme being staffed rather than vacancies being refilled, and vendor choices freeze once the architects are in post ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Card economics are visibly hurting mid-size banks, and that is a conversation rather than a contract. UNIBanka's H1-2026 filing puts an 8.8% rise in operating expenses mainly down to commission costs charged by the card organisations for cross-border transactions and licences. An extraordinary shareholders' meeting on the use of profit is set for 24 September 2026 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Adjacent identity and personalisation work is where the reachable money in this line actually sits. Greece's OPSEA security-documents competitive dialogue, at EUR 415.6m excluding value-added tax, remained open at stage one with a twice-extended deadline of 10 September 2026. Slovenia's national secure-document personalisation is locked to CETIS on a ten-year, EUR 41.9m framework, with no way to displace it ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
Nothing changed this cycle that would move this line, and that is itself the finding. The signals tagged to card issuing are almost all other lines' events seen from the card side. Examples are Banca Transilvania's capital programme, Erste Croatia's withdrawal-only fleet and Postbank's branch-format rebuild. The genuinely card-specific developments are two hiring clusters and one disposal.

Meanwhile the processing layer was strengthened twice. Way4's role under the whole Bulgarian national infrastructure was restated in an award release on 23 July 2026. Bankart's structural position was re-confirmed at source, with a fresh central-bank mandate signed 30 April 2026 and running to about February 2029 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

The one thing worth timing is the arrival of new technology leadership. Bankart appointed a chief technology officer on 17 April 2026, and it was the company's only publication of the year. Roadmaps reopen with the role, and none of that buying happens through a public tender.

Flat is the correct call. The correct response is to attach this line to the instant-payments and acquiring programmes that are funded.
cite_ungrounded: Alpha Bank Cyprus is not used as a card-reissue prospect here, deliberately: the signal itself corrects the “whole-portfolio reissue onto new card numbers” premise as unsupported, with only the co-branded Aegean Visa portfolio moving to Mastercard. Anyone reading the cite_signals list should not reconstruct the merger-driven mass-reissuance story from it.
The characterisation of card_issuing as the smallest of the six lines rests on comparing the six `m` figures supplied with this task, not on any signal.

product_outlooks.label: Compliance & operational resilience
product_outlooks.scope: Supervisory deadlines and the second-largest technology spending line
product_outlooks.summary:
At EUR 320.5m this is the second-largest line in the business. Only ATM and cash automation is bigger. It also has the firmest set of deadlines of any line.

By 31 October 2026 every significant institution in the euro-area part of the footprint must file an action plan on artificial-intelligence-enabled cyber threats with its Joint Supervisory Team. A significant institution is a large bank under direct ECB supervision. The annex names "legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies" as a focus area. That makes an ageing estate a repair job the supervisor monitors, rather than an optional refresh ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

Behind that sits the anti-money-laundering package. It applies directly from 10 July 2027, and not a single binding technical text has been published yet. AMLA, the new EU anti-money-laundering authority, is also selecting cross-border groups for direct supervision in 2027 ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)). The same requirements reach outside the EU through national rulebooks in Bosnia, Kosovo and Montenegro.

Aim the line at three things. First, rules layers that can be reconfigured. Second, inventories of information and communications technology assets with device telemetry (remote device data). Third, the group-level data work that cross-border banks now have to prove.
product_outlooks.projected:
Strong growth is expected, and this line has the clearest dates in the portfolio. The nearest firm date is 31 October 2026. By then every significant institution across Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Greece, Croatia, Slovenia and Slovakia must file its artificial-intelligence cyber action plan with its Joint Supervisory Team. The ECB then discusses each plan with the bank and compares all the plans side by side ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

Three things give this deadline more weight than a letter usually has. First, it was repeated in the Official Journal through the European Systemic Risk Board's Warning ESRB/2026/3 of 25 June 2026, published on 16 July 2026. Second, on 31 July 2026 the three European Supervisory Authorities extended the same governance expectation to the smaller banks supervised at national level. Most of the installed estate sits with those banks. Third, the ECB's annual information-technology risk questionnaire moved from September 2026 to February 2027. That gives banks more time to gather evidence, not less.

The second supervisory tool is threat-led penetration testing, which means simulated attacks based on real threats, under the digital operational resilience rules. The same ESRB warning points national authorities towards those testing frameworks, so wider scope is the likely next step.

The anti-money-laundering package is the largest single budget line. Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 applies directly from 10 July 2027, and the sixth directive must be written into national law the same day. Yet a search of the EU Publications Office on 27 August 2026 found no delegated or implementing act at all. AMLA has missed its own 10 July 2026 delivery date on roughly nineteen mandates.

Four consultations close between 3 September and 6 October 2026. The first of them, the ongoing-monitoring guidelines, is in effect the functional specification for transaction monitoring ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)). AMLA's provisional list of groups eligible for direct supervision is expected at end-September 2026. The first selection must start by 1 July 2027, based on a test of whether a group operates in six Member States ([AMLA selection process](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

Outside the EU the same requirements arrive through national rulebooks. The Federation of Bosnia's banking agency requires an external information and communications technology audit report from all thirteen of its banks by 31 March 2027. It names cryptographic key protection and locally tuned transaction monitoring explicitly ([FBA supervisory expectations for 2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf)). Kosovo's Law 08/L-304 on Banks gives every licensed bank until about 11 February 2027 to comply. Montenegro is adopting the European prudential and resolution packages, which are the rules on bank capital and on handling failing banks. It is doing so against a stated end-2026 target for closing accession talks.

Where to aim it. First, the mid-market banks that the European Supervisory Authorities brought into scope on 31 July 2026. These are the banks supervised by the Bulgarian, Greek, Cypriot, Croatian, Slovak and Slovenian central banks and by Austria's Finanzmarktaufsicht. Offer them an evidence pack on asset inventories, large-scale patching and end-of-life systems, timed for the Q4-2026 filings and the February 2027 questionnaire.

Second, the cross-border groups facing AMLA's six-Member-State test. Here the work is group-level customer-due-diligence data lineage, which means tracing where customer-check data comes from. It is bought centrally rather than country by country.

Third, three funded and dated integrations. Raiffeisen Bank International has a roughly EUR 75m Addiko programme across Croatia, Slovenia and Austria. Raiffeisen Romania has a roughly EUR 70m Garanti BBVA migration running through 2027, paid for with money already raised in a EUR 600m eurobond. The four Western Balkans Addiko banks are being carved out to Alta Group, with a twelve-plus-twelve-month transitional-services clock written into the deal documents.

Fourth, the thirteen Federation of Bosnia banks and Kosovo's licensed banks, where the filing dates are fixed and the rulebooks name the products.

In short, treat this as the leading line for the financial-year-2027 planning round that opens now. Sell a configurable rules layer that can be re-pointed when the official texts arrive, rather than a hard-coded flow. Open every euro-area conversation with what the 31 October 2026 plan commits to on end-of-life estate.
drivers: Every significant institution must file an artificial-intelligence cyber action plan by 31 October 2026. The annex names "legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies" and accurate asset inventories. It also pulls supplier service-level agreements into the patching focus area ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

The anti-money-laundering regulation applies directly from 10 July 2027, but no level-2 text is yet in the Official Journal. These are the detailed technical rules. Roughly nineteen AMLA mandates have been overdue since 10 July 2026, and four consultations close between 3 September and 6 October 2026 ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

AMLA's pipeline for direct supervision in 2027. The provisional list of eligible cross-border groups is expected at end-September 2026, and selection must start by 1 July 2027 ([AMLA selection process](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

Threat-led penetration testing, which means simulated attacks based on real threats, under the digital operational resilience rules. It got a fresh push from the European Systemic Risk Board's Warning ESRB/2026/3, adopted 25 June 2026 and published in the Official Journal on 16 July 2026 (see [findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Non-EU rulebooks are heading the same way. The Federation of Bosnia's binding information and communications technology decision requires an external audit report from all thirteen banks by 31 March 2027 ([FBA supervisory expectations for 2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf)). Kosovo's Law 08/L-304 has a compliance date of about 11 February 2027. Montenegro is aligning with EU prudential and resolution rules against an end-2026 accession target.

Funded, dated bank integrations that merge compliance systems. Raiffeisen Bank International has a roughly EUR 75m Addiko programme. Raiffeisen Romania has a roughly EUR 70m Garanti BBVA migration through 2027. The Addiko carve-out of four Western Balkans banks to Alta Group has a transitional-services exit date written into the deal.
product_outlooks.rationale:
What changed this cycle is that the supervisory expectation stopped being advice and gained both legal weight and reach. The 31 October 2026 deadline is now recorded in the Official Journal through the European Systemic Risk Board's June-2026 warning. On 31 July 2026 the three European Supervisory Authorities extended the same governance expectation to the smaller, nationally supervised banks. Those banks make up most of the footprint's installed base ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

At the same time the anti-money-laundering detail is still missing. With about ten months to go before a directly applicable regulation, and not one binding technical standard published, every bank in the footprint is planning against drafts. That favours a configurable rules layer over a fixed-scope build ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

Budget for both is committed in the financial-year-2027 planning round, which runs from September to November 2026. The sales window is therefore open now, not at the deadlines themselves.
cite_ungrounded: The Official Journal reference C/2026/3795 for Warning ESRB/2026/3, and its footnote 11 pointing authorities to TIBER, threat-led penetration testing, advanced red teaming and cyber stress testing: the slice confirms the warning, its 25/06/2026 adoption and its 16/07/2026 publication, but not the OJ citation number or the footnote contents.

The pre-announced SECOND ECB letter on post-quantum cryptography, referred to here as a forward signal only. It is announced in writing but carries no date, is not traceable to a cited signal in this slice, and must never be presented to a customer as a deadline.

The ISO 20022 structured-address end date of 15 November 2026, at 03:30 CET for the instant credit transfer schemes, rests on European Payments Council guidance EPC153-22 v2.1. The EPC site was Cloudflare-blocked to every route this cycle, so no EPC scheme date is verified at primary and none may be quoted to a customer without that caveat.

The characterisation of this line as "second-largest, behind only ATM and cash automation at EUR 377.8m and ahead of POS" comes from the product-value ranking supplied to this outlook, not from any signal inside the slice.

product_outlooks.label: Fraud & transaction monitoring
product_outlooks.scope: Real-time screening: instant payment rails and regulator-ordered remediation
product_outlooks.summary:
Fixed deadlines, rather than general trends, are rebuilding this line. Instant payment rails went live across the Western Balkans on 20 July 2026. They reach Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia in a November 2026 window. Bosnia's rulebook sets a five-second maximum execution time and makes joining compulsory for large banks from 1 January 2027 ([CBBiH instant-payment rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

An overnight batch run cannot check a payment that settles in five seconds. Sanctions screening, fraud scoring and transaction monitoring therefore all move inline, which means they are checked live as the payment happens. Separately, the instant-payments regulation requires banks to screen their whole customer book against sanctions lists once every calendar day ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

Alongside the rails comes required repair work. The Czech central bank has institutions, named to them but not made public, carrying out ordered fixes to fuzzy-matching sanctions screening. Fuzzy matching means matching names that are spelt slightly differently. Hungary's regulator has set out a list of required compliance fixes in two binding orders.

Aim the line at inline screening and payee-name matching, case management, and the banks building the function from scratch.
product_outlooks.projected:
Strong growth is expected, on the densest set of near-term dates in the portfolio. The rails came first. The shared instant settlement platform built for the Western Balkans went live on 20 July 2026 with the central banks of Bosnia and Montenegro. A second onboarding window in November 2026 is expected to bring in Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia ([Banca d'Italia go-live](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

Montenegro went live with all eleven of its banks at once. Payee-name verification, which checks that the receiver's name matches the account, is compulsory. Money must be credited within ten seconds, and fees are capped at five cents ([CBCG instant payments](https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/instant-placanja-tips-clone)).

Bosnia is the opposite. Only five banks have joined so far, out of twenty-one or twenty-two licensed banks. Banks above the transaction threshold must join by law from 1 January 2027. The threshold is rolling, so more banks are pulled in every year. Article 15 sets the engineering limits of five seconds' execution and a seven-second scheme timeout ([CBBiH rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

Then comes the EU calendar. Every payment service provider licensed in Bulgaria must offer instant euro sending from 1 January 2027, at the same price as normal transfers and with full payee verification. Recital 11 of the instant-payments regulation names automated teller machines and self-service terminals among the channels where a payment can be started. That turns a payments-department item into a device-estate item ([BNB SEPA FAQ](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/AUFAQ/CONTR_SEPA_FAQ)).

Czech, Hungarian and Romanian banks must be able to receive instant euro transfers by 9 January 2027. They must be able to send them with payee verification by 9 July 2027. The Czech central bank says plainly that it runs no euro instant rail, so every Czech bank buys its own ([ČNB instant payments](https://www.cnb.cz/cs/platebni-styk/certis/okamzite-platby/)).

Required repair work is the second source of demand. The Czech regulator tested 88 sanctions-screening systems across 37 institutions. It reports that those scoring below market standard are now carrying out imposed remedial measures. Fuzzy name matching was the common weakness. In a single month, 38 financial-crime vacancies were posted across seven institutions and the regulator ([ČNB supervision report 2025](https://www.cnb.cz/export/sites/cnb/cs/dohled-financni-trh/.galleries/souhrnne_informace_fin_trhy/zpravy_o_vykonu_dohledu/download/dnft_2025_cz.pdf)).

Hungary's central bank has ordered Raiffeisen Bank Hungary to complete internal-audit testing of beneficial-owner identification by 30 September 2026. Beneficial-owner identification means finding who really owns a customer company. The bank must deliver the audit reports plus a register of unresolved ownership structures by 31 October 2026. The named weakness sits with an outsourced provider that pre-screens alerts.

Bulgaria adds a national layer. BORICA's centralised anti-fraud model has its rules due by end-2026 and market roll-out from 2027. The scheme core is already committed to a named design partner and engine ([BORICA on PSD3 and PSR](https://www.borica.bg/latest/novini/evropeyskite-regulatsii-psd3-psr-postavyat-novi-predizvikatelstva-pred-finansoviya-sektor)).

Where to aim it. The roughly sixteen Bosnian banks still outside the instant scheme can be tracked through the central bank's own announcements of new joiners. In Montenegro, one packaged offer of real-time monitoring, fraud scoring, payee-name matching and round-the-clock operations can be sold eleven times. Thinly staffed banks such as Adriatic, Zapad, Universal Capital, Ziraat and Lovćen have no in-house option.

The November group is Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia. Budget that is not committed there by about September 2026 becomes 2027 repair work. In Bulgaria's device estate, any bank that limited payee verification to online and mobile has a gap on its machines and kiosks.

In Czechia, target the newer and smaller institutions building the function from nothing. Penta Bank's Czech branch posted a head of anti-money-laundering and fraud monitoring and an anti-fraud team lead on the same day. Banka CREDITAS is in the same position. These are better targets than incumbents merely tuning what they already run.

In short, lead with speed and evidence rather than licences. Package inline screening with the instant-rail integration it is bought alongside. Treat the BORICA scheme core as background, and sell the per-bank connectivity underneath it.
drivers: Instant rails went live across the Western Balkans from 20 July 2026, with a November 2026 window for Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia. Bosnia's rulebook fixes five-second execution and compulsory participation from 1 January 2027 ([Banca d'Italia go-live](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/), [CBBiH rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

Verification of Payee and instant euro duties take effect on 1 January 2027 in Bulgaria. In Czechia, Hungary and Romania they take effect on 9 January and 9 July 2027. The primary text names automated teller machines and self-service terminals ([BNB SEPA FAQ](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/AUFAQ/CONTR_SEPA_FAQ), [Regulation (EU) 2024/886](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

Daily re-screening. Article 5d of the instant-payments regulation requires banks to screen users against sanctions lists at least once every calendar day. It attracts the least attention in the package and is the hardest to run day to day ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

Regulator-ordered repair work in Czechia. Institutions that scored below market standard on a 10,000-record fuzzy-matching test are under imposed remedial measures. In a single month, 38 financial-crime vacancies were posted ([ČNB supervision report 2025](https://www.cnb.cz/export/sites/cnb/cs/dohled-financni-trh/.galleries/souhrnne_informace_fin_trhy/zpravy_o_vykonu_dohledu/download/dnft_2025_cz.pdf)).

Two binding Hungarian central-bank orders on Raiffeisen Bank Hungary, with deadlines of 30 September and 31 October 2026. They name automated risk scoring, information-technology-supported control testing and beneficial-owner repair work. They place the weakness with an outsourced pre-screening provider (see [findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

A national anti-fraud model in Bulgaria, with rules due end-2026 and bank-by-bank roll-out from 2027. It is sized on local losses of about EUR 7.9m from credit-transfer fraud and EUR 13m from account-substitution fraud in 2025 ([BORICA on PSD3 and PSR](https://www.borica.bg/latest/novini/evropeyskite-regulatsii-psd3-psr-postavyat-novi-predizvikatelstva-pred-finansoviya-sektor)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
The change is to the whole design, not a small step. Until this year most footprint banks screened payments in a batch that ran while the market was closed. From 20 July 2026 several of them no longer have a market close. Bosnia's rulebook puts a five-second ceiling on the whole transaction, which leaves roughly five seconds for fraud and sanctions checks to clear ([CBBiH rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

At the same time the bar for compliance evidence moved. The Czech regulator has turned screening quality from a supervisory opinion into an enforceable finding. It treats screening that is not effective enough as a breach of law ([ČNB supervision report 2025](https://www.cnb.cz/export/sites/cnb/cs/dohled-financni-trh/.galleries/souhrnne_informace_fin_trhy/zpravy_o_vykonu_dohledu/download/dnft_2025_cz.pdf)).

Rails plus enforcement are why this line grows on a mandatory budget and a repair budget at the same time. They are also why the buying happens in the September-to-November 2026 planning round, not at the 2027 deadlines.
cite_ungrounded: The European Payments Council's Verification-of-Payee rulebook v1.1, reported as binding at 20/09/2026 03:30 CET, is NOT verified at primary: the EPC site was Cloudflare-blocked to every route this cycle and none of five EPC scheme dates could be confirmed. It is deliberately not used as a date in this outlook and must not be quoted to a customer as a certification deadline.
The ISO 20022 unstructured-address end date of 15 November 2026 rests on the same unverified EPC guidance and carries the same caveat.

The inference that an overnight batch is incapable of scoring an instantly settled payment is an engineering reading of the five-second and ten-second scheme envelopes, not a statement made by any regulator in the cited signals.

product_outlooks.label: Digital identity, onboarding & e-signature
product_outlooks.scope: Digital identity: fixed EU rules and national wallets delayed beyond end-2026
product_outlooks.summary:
This line grows, but steadily rather than sharply. The supply-side date is firm, and the duty on banks sits just beyond the window.
