Every EU Member State must provide at least one digital identity wallet by 24 December 2026. The register regime for businesses that accept wallet presentations applies the same day. A wallet presentation is identity data shared from a wallet.

Yet Austria's responsible State Secretary told a parliamentary committee on 29 June 2026 that no Member State will have met the requirements by the end of 2026. The bank acceptance date of 24 December 2027 is worked out from the text rather than printed in it. Two delays to 11 August 2028 ease near-term pressure further. Identity proofing with a document and a selfie therefore stays necessary alongside wallet acceptance, rather than being replaced by it ([EUDI architecture and reference framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

The earliest firm duty on banks in the footprint is actually North Macedonia's, on 1 June 2027 ([European Commission North Macedonia Report 2025](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/267b368e-6b55-4a42-bb72-6395593de4da_en?filename=north-macedonia-report-2025.pdf)). Aim the line at a wallet-agnostic acceptance layer, meaning one that works with any wallet, at chip and document reading, and at the repeated re-verification waves that national schemes create.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, and it builds up gradually rather than arriving on a single date. The dated events inside the window are on the supply side and the register. All ten EU footprint markets must have a wallet in place by 24 December 2026. The relying-party register regime applies from the same day, and it covers the businesses that accept wallet identities.

The Commission's architecture and reference framework reached version 3.0.0 on 23 July 2026. It now includes a functional conformance assessment framework with a live public test catalogue. A bank's wallet acceptance can therefore be tested objectively before any duty applies ([EUDI architecture and reference framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

Three amending implementing regulations were checked against the official text. Regulation 2026/1731, in force from 11 August 2026, adds a biometric warning and an explicit confirmation step whenever a portrait is requested.

The counterweight is just as well evidenced. Two things are deferred to 11 August 2028: the portrait becoming mandatory identity data, and wallets having to check relying-party registration certificates. Austria's State Secretary for Digitalisation said on the parliamentary record on 29 June 2026 that no Member State will meet end-2026. The 24 December 2027 acceptance date is also worked out from Article 5f(2) rather than printed.

The one firm bank-side date within reach is outside the EU. North Macedonia's national law applies from 1 June 2027 to private relying parties in banking and financial services. That is six months ahead of the EU's own derived date ([European Commission North Macedonia Report 2025](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/267b368e-6b55-4a42-bb72-6395593de4da_en?filename=north-macedonia-report-2025.pdf)).

Two public contests in Croatia are open to bid on now. One is for travel-document authentication devices for border crossings, at about EUR 1,280,000, closing 22 September 2026. The other is a 24-month maintenance lot for personal-document scanners and fingerprint readers, at about EUR 216,000, closing 11 September 2026. It is scored on tender price plus response time to a service call-out ([TED 555035-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/555035-2026/xml)). The Czech agency that cancelled its relying-party register framework on 16 June 2026 with no winner has to come back to market before the December 2026 obligation ([NEN N006/26/V00002507](https://nen.nipez.cz/verejne-zakazky/detail-zakazky/N006-26-V00002507)).

Where to aim it. North Macedonia comes first. Seven banks — Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB Skopje, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse and UNIBanka — must build a wallet verifier for 1 June 2027 and must commit budget from H2-2026. The national OneID scheme already forces a re-verification wave through its two-year expiry, one-device rule and once-a-month update cap. UNIBanka, TTK Banka and ALTA banka Bitola are the short list still outside it ([OneID adoption timeline](https://www.oneid.mk/news.nspx)).

Austria and Czechia come next, where the national wallet slips but the relying-party date does not. The lasting product there is a wallet-agnostic acceptance layer. It works with today's national credentials now and with a certified wallet later.

In Albania, the electronic identification and wallet law adopted on 7 May 2026 is the legal step that unblocks remote enrolment and qualified signature. There are also 3.25m paper credit transfers per half-year still crossing branch counters. In Kosovo, one bank had to extend a remote-onboarding and digital-signature tender twice, to 29 June 2026, without awarding it. That is evidence of funded demand.

Greece has two dated opportunities. Alpha Bank's innovation call closes on 20 September 2026, with digital onboarding named among its themes. At Piraeus, digital onboarding sits at 23%.

Two routes should be treated as closed rather than fought over. Romania's tier-one banks have built chip-based onboarding in-house against the national electronic identity card, with no vendor named. UniCredit Romania's know-your-customer layer sits inside a group cloud agreement.

In short, sell a wallet-agnostic acceptance and verification layer plus document-and-chip proofing. Size the verifier for optional rather than universal traffic. Never tie a proposal's date to a national wallet programme arriving on time.
drivers: Member State wallet issuance and the relying-party register regime both apply from 24 December 2026. The acceptance duty is worked out as 24 December 2027, and two important elements are deferred to 11 August 2028 ([EUDI architecture and reference framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

A conformance assessment framework with a live public test catalogue, published on 23 July 2026. It lets banks test their wallet acceptance objectively before the duty applies ([EUDI architecture and reference framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

North Macedonia's national-law duty on banks as relying parties applies from 1 June 2027. It is the first legal wallet-acceptance duty on banks anywhere in the footprint ([European Commission North Macedonia Report 2025](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/267b368e-6b55-4a42-bb72-6395593de4da_en?filename=north-macedonia-report-2025.pdf)).

A repeated, compulsory re-verification wave created by national scheme rules. OneID identities expire after two years, work on one device only and allow data updates only once a month. Seven Macedonian banks have adopted the scheme ([OneID adoption timeline](https://www.oneid.mk/news.nspx)).

Two open Croatian contests for identity-document hardware close on 11 and 22 September 2026, with the maintenance lot scored partly on service call-out response time ([TED 555035-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/555035-2026/xml)). A cancelled Czech relying-party register framework must also be re-run before December 2026 ([NEN N006/26/V00002507](https://nen.nipez.cz/verejne-zakazky/detail-zakazky/N006-26-V00002507)).

Anti-money-laundering standards under Article 28(1) are still unpublished, against a missed 10 July 2026 delivery date. They will set out the reliable independent sources for verifying identity and the attributes electronic identification must carry ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
The reason to move now is a mismatch that will not fix itself. The duties on banks and on businesses that accept identity presentations are fixed in EU law. But the national wallets those duties assume are publicly expected to be late and uneven. The minister responsible in Austria said so on the parliamentary record on 29 June 2026.

That gap defines the product: an acceptance and verification layer that does not depend on any one national wallet arriving, paired with document and chip proofing. The proofing stays necessary because the portrait is not guaranteed before 2028 ([EUDI architecture and reference framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

Meanwhile the anti-money-laundering standards that will define acceptable electronic identification are overdue. Buying a hard-coded onboarding flow this year is therefore the wrong kind of purchase ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).
cite_ungrounded: The statement that Romania's tier-one banks have built chip-based onboarding in-house is drawn from the Romanian chip-identity signal, which sits in the payment security slice rather than this one; the supporting detail (Garanti BBVA's 14/04/2026 launch, BRD in Q2-2026) is therefore not traceable to a signal key cited above.
The count of "ten EU footprint markets" for wallet issuance is read off the eIDAS 2 signal's stated EU footprint rather than enumerated in it.

product_outlooks.label: Physical ATM security
product_outlooks.scope: Physical security and cash-cycle services: unattended estates grow, institutional estates stay with current suppliers
product_outlooks.summary:
The honest view of this line is that it runs at two speeds.

Bank-side demand is genuinely rising. Hungary has passed a law putting 1,039 barrier-free machines into service by 31 December 2026. They are hosted by municipalities in rural, low-footfall settlements, and there is no tender to bid on. Barrier-free means accessible to all users.

A separate 2026 law froze decommissioning, so roughly 5,700 machines can only be swapped, not removed. The law itself expects that a replacement may be larger and carry higher security requirements ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.)](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)).

Card skimming, which is the copying of card data at the machine, is back as a public, dated event. OTP Slovenia warned customers on 6 August 2026 across a fleet of roughly 384 machines. Ukraine's new highest banknote enters circulation on 4 September 2026 across about 38,700 self-service devices ([NBU device table](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx)).

Against that, the institutional estates are largely closed to a new supplier. Aim the line at unattended bank sites, anti-skimming and note-cycle field services, not at central-bank security contracts.
product_outlooks.projected:
The outlook is mixed, and the two halves should be read separately rather than added together.

The growing half is the unattended, bank-owned estate. Hungary's Annex 1 allocation assigns 80 settlement packages covering 1,039 named settlements to nine obligated banks. OTP holds 428 settlements, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste Hungary 104 and Raiffeisen 65. 

The deadline to swap packages, 28 February 2026, has passed, so the map is fixed. A hand-over of operation cannot be contracted for less than five years. Every machine must be barrier-free, with no exemption for older machines ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.)](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)).

Act XIV of 2026 then changed the economics of the estate from 14 May 2026. A credit institution may no longer stop operating an existing machine, and replacement is expressly allowed. Subsection (1b) expects that a like-for-like swap may be impossible "for purely technological or technical reasons". It names in particular "the dimensions of the new ATM and its security requirements" ([Act XVIII consolidated text](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00)).

Card skimming is the second live driver, and it releases emergency budget. OTP Slovenia published a security notice on 6 August 2026. It said it has been detecting card abuse at its machines through devices that copy magnetic-stripe data, and through cameras or fake keypad overlays that capture the PIN. Its fleet of about 384 machines is barely shrinking, while branches close at nearly seven per cent in six months.

The third driver is a field event with a fixed date. Ukraine's UAH 2,000 note enters circulation on 4 September 2026. For the first time the National Bank has released configuration materials before the circulation date. The estate is confirmed at 38,721 self-service devices at 1 July 2026 ([NBU device table](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx), [NBU UAH 2,000 page](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/uah/obig-banknote/2000_2026_2026)).

The flat half is the institutional estate. Austria's central bank extended its security-technology maintenance only to 31 December 2026. The recorded reason is that the current supplier developed the entire security-management software and all subsystem interfaces. Romania's central bank has its security maintenance with the state technical-security operator, which sits under the intelligence service. Bulgaria's central bank bought its banknote-sorter modules from the machines' maker alone, on a single tender.

At PrivatBank, the published stage-1 qualified list for the banknote-sorter contest names four firms, none of them Printec. That is a supplier-registration issue, not a pricing one ([PrivatBank recycler tender](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-03-17-3068329)).

Where to aim it. Approach the nine Hungarian obligated banks account by account, because there will be no tender. Offer physical security for unattended municipal sites, and remote monitoring and telemetry (remote device data) where no branch staff are nearby to clear a jam. Also offer a paid site-survey and fit study for machines that will not fit their old spaces.

Approach OTP Slovenia now, while the incident is live, on anti-skimming detection, hardening of card slots and keypads, and disabling the magnetic stripe. Target the Ukrainian device population from September to December 2026. The commercial race starts on 4 September and is won on verified per-device coverage.

On a 2027-28 horizon, look at the Slovak central bank's permanent backup site at Kremnica. Its construction-supervision framework was awarded on 15 July 2026. It still has vaults, cash handling, physical security, access control and a resilient equipment room to buy.

Two near-term calendar entries are worth noting even where the current supplier is strong. Croatian Post's roughly EUR 1,150,000 technical-protection maintenance award has been pending since bids closed on 17 August 2026. Austria's central-bank bridge contract expires on 31 December 2026.

In short, this line does not grow across the whole footprint. Fund the unattended, anti-skimming and note-cycle work where the dates are real. Log the institutional estates as calendar intelligence. Fix supplier qualification at PrivatBank before the larger recycler round, not after it.
drivers: Hungary's rural rollout is required by law. It covers 1,039 named settlements in 80 packages assigned bank by bank, all barrier-free with no exemption for older machines. The deadline is 31 December 2026, and fines run from HUF 2m to HUF 200m ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.)](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)).

Hungary's freeze on decommissioning and relocating machines from 14 May 2026. It turns a shrinking estate into a guaranteed replacement market, and it expressly allows for larger replacement machines with higher security requirements ([Act XVIII consolidated text](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00)).

A live, publicly disclosed card-skimming wave at OTP Slovenia, announced on 6 August 2026 across a fleet of roughly 384 machines. This releases emergency rather than planned budget (see [findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Ukraine's UAH 2,000 banknote enters circulation on 4 September 2026 across a confirmed 38,721 self-service devices. Every acceptor, dispenser, recycler and sorter needs note-template and firmware work ([NBU device table](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx), [NBU UAH 2,000 page](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/uah/obig-banknote/2000_2026_2026)).

A dated central-bank fit-out pipeline in Slovakia. A four-year construction-supervision framework was awarded on 15 July 2026, which puts the vault, cash-handling, physical-security and equipment-room purchases at roughly 2027-28 (see [findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Current suppliers are locked in on the institutional side. The Austrian central bank's security estate is tied to the vendor that wrote its security-management software, on a bridge contract expiring 31 December 2026. The Romanian central bank's maintenance sits with the state technical-security operator. Bulgaria's sorter modules were bought from the manufacturer alone (see [findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
Two things changed at once, and they point in opposite directions. That is why the call is mixed rather than one of growth.

On the demand side, Hungary has turned a shrinking estate into a legally protected replacement market. At the same time it has ordered a thousand new machines into rural, municipality-hosted, unstaffed sites. Those are exactly the places where physical protection, telemetry and remote service matter most ([Act XVIII consolidated text](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00)).

On the supply side, this cycle gave unusually clear evidence that the institutional estates cannot be won on merit. The Austrian bridge extension records software ownership as the reason only the current supplier can do the work. At PrivatBank, the qualification gate rather than price is what kept a bidder out of a live cash-automation contest ([PrivatBank recycler tender](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-03-17-3068329)). An honest allocation follows the first half and treats the second as intelligence.
cite_ungrounded: Hungary's Act XIV of 2026 decommissioning freeze, its 14/05/2026 effect date and the roughly 5,700-machine national estate come from the Hungarian freeze signal cited above; the URL used for it is the consolidated Act XVIII text named in that signal's source list, so the Act XIV amending text itself is not directly linked here.

The characterisation of the roughly 384-machine OTP Slovenia fleet and the 6 August 2026 skimming notice traces to the cited signal, but no case numbers, locations or machine models were published by the bank, so the scale of the incident is unquantified.
The judgement that the institutional physical-security estates are effectively non-contestable is an inference from four separate incumbency findings, not a statement made by any of the buyers.

product_outlooks.label: Payment security & key management (HSM)
product_outlooks.scope: Key management: demand from instant payment rails and terminal growth
product_outlooks.summary:
Two measurable forces are increasing demand for key management, the systems that protect the secret keys used to secure payments.

Instant payment rails now need round-the-clock cryptographic capacity in markets that had none. Bosnia's banks must join from 1 January 2027 inside a five-second limit ([CBBiH rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)), and Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected in a November 2026 onboarding window.

At the same time card acceptance is growing quickly. Estate management, remote key injection and PIN security become the recurring revenue, rather than the terminal itself. Remote key injection means loading keys into terminals over the network. Albania reached 38,662 terminals at end-Q2-2026, up 23.7% in six months, under a legal duty that binds the remaining businesses by 31 December 2026 ([Bank of Albania terminal series](https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/F6_TERMINALS_T2_Shqip_34619.xlsx)). Kosovo added roughly 9,400 terminals in a year ([CBK card usage report](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf)).

Non-EU resilience rulebooks in Bosnia and Kosovo name cryptographic key protection explicitly. Aim the line at acquirers running mixed hardware-and-software estates, not at central-bank general-purpose key storage, which is closing.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is driven by volume and by rulebooks, rather than by any single large contract.

The rails come first. About sixteen Bosnian banks must connect by 1 January 2027. The rulebook's five-second execution ceiling forces hardware security modules and key management into the build alongside screening. Hardware security modules are dedicated devices that hold and protect keys ([CBBiH rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

North Macedonia's seven main banks face two integrations on two calendars. One is a national system rebuilt on ISO 20022, with its first test cycle completed in July 2026. The other is a private clearing house's instant service, with banks expected to start sending from 15 September 2026. Albania and Kosovo join the shared regional platform in the November 2026 window.

The second driver is acceptance volume. Albania's terminal estate reached 38,662 at end-Q2-2026, a rise of 23.7% in six months and 57.9% over eighteen months. This is under a tax-procedures duty that binds the remaining businesses by 31 December 2026, and a free-terminal programme valid to the same date ([Bank of Albania terminal series](https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/F6_TERMINALS_T2_Shqip_34619.xlsx)).

Kosovo's card-accepting terminals reached about 30,300, up roughly 9,400 in a single year. A fleet installed in one burst starts its refresh clock together ([CBK card usage report](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf)).

Romania's reported estate passed 729,408 terminals, but it is served largely by bank software-based acceptance and shared terminals. The layer to sell there is certification, key injection, PIN-security services and capacity for acquirers running several types of acceptance device at once.

The third driver is the card-security rulebooks. North Macedonia's app-based strong authentication has been compulsory since 1 March 2026 across a two-million-card base. More than 350,000 of those cards are already tokenised, up 137.5% year on year. Tokenised means the card number is replaced by a stand-in number for digital use ([NBRSM strong-authentication notice](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-27022026.nspx)).

Bosnia's Federation banking agency requires protection of the cryptographic keys that encrypt data at rest and in transit. An external audit report is due 31 March 2027 ([FBA supervisory expectations for 2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf)). Kosovo's cyber-risk regulation, binding since 1 June 2026, names automated teller machines as critical systems. It also keeps the cybersecurity budget separate from the general technology budget ([CBK regulation on information systems](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-sistemet-e-informacionit-1-1.pdf?lang=en)).

A fourth driver is only an early signal and must be treated that way. The ECB has committed in writing to a further letter on post-quantum cryptography, which is encryption designed to resist quantum computers. No date was given. It is not a deadline, and no compliance date may be quoted from it.

Where to aim it: acquirers rather than card schemes. Acquirers are the banks that process card payments for shops. Start with Albania's five named programme acquirers. Then take Kosovo's commercial banks under the World Bank-funded faster-payments component. Their goods and information-technology tables are still empty. Anything at or above USD 1.5m goes to open international competition ([World Bank P507881](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051526174517828/pdf/P507881-c295d365-73e9-4972-93a5-a4072086c160.pdf)).

Bulgaria's device estate comes next, where payee verification from 1 January 2027 reaches machines and kiosks and drives round-the-clock key capacity ([BNB SEPA FAQ](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/AUFAQ/CONTR_SEPA_FAQ)). Serbia's central bank is also a target. Its 2026 procurement plan version 9 of 26 August 2026 carries a named hardware-security-module line alongside SEPA and instant-payment work. It publishes everything and accepts bids in English ([NBS 2026 procurement plan v9](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/propisi/propisi-tend/2026/plan_nabavki_2026_v9.pdf)).

Croatia's largest domestically owned bank has said its card ecosystem must change. It has just won a motorway card-acceptance contract that forces it to run an unattended terminal estate ([TED 549006-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/549006-2026/xml)).

Two routes are closing and should not take up effort. Hungary's central bank has written a named vendor's key-storage appliances into its specification down to part number, and placed a local integrator behind them for three years. That closes general-purpose key storage there, but does not touch the payments key layer ([TED 511411-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/hu/notice/511411-2026/xml)). Slovenia buys identity and key infrastructure through small local integrators on single bids, so the route there is through partners.

In short, sell the services around the hardware: multivendor terminal management, remote key injection, PIN-security attestation (proof of compliance) and round-the-clock key capacity. Time approaches to the instant-rail integrations, where key management is bought as part of a funded programme rather than on its own.
drivers: Instant-rail integrations need round-the-clock key capacity. Bosnia has a legal participation date of 1 January 2027 inside a five-second limit ([CBBiH rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)). North Macedonia is running two rails at the same time, and Albania and Kosovo have a November 2026 onboarding window.

Terminal estates are growing fast enough that managing them becomes the revenue. Albania is at 38,662 terminals and up 23.7% in six months, under a duty binding the remaining businesses by 31 December 2026 ([Bank of Albania terminal series](https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/F6_TERMINALS_T2_Shqip_34619.xlsx)). Kosovo is up about 9,400 terminals in a year ([CBK card usage report](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf)).

Verification of Payee reaches the device estate in Bulgaria from 1 January 2027. The primary text names automated teller machines and self-service terminals among the channels where a payment can be started ([BNB SEPA FAQ](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/AUFAQ/CONTR_SEPA_FAQ)).

Compulsory app-based strong customer authentication in North Macedonia since 1 March 2026, across a two-million-card base with tokenised cards up 137.5% year on year. This drives PIN-security compliance and remote key injection ([NBRSM strong-authentication notice](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-27022026.nspx)).

Non-EU resilience rulebooks name cryptography directly. The Federation of Bosnia's decision covers protecting the keys that encrypt data at rest and in transit, with an audit report due 31 March 2027 ([FBA supervisory expectations for 2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf)). Kosovo's cyber-risk regulation, binding since 1 June 2026, requires a separate, protected cybersecurity budget ([CBK regulation on information systems](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-sistemet-e-informacionit-1-1.pdf?lang=en)).

A named central-bank pipeline in Serbia that has not yet been awarded. It carries a hardware-security-module line plus SEPA, instant-payment and card-system work. It is published openly and accepts bids in English ([NBS 2026 procurement plan v9](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/propisi/propisi-tend/2026/plan_nabavki_2026_v9.pdf)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
The demand is arriving as a by-product of programmes that are already funded. That is why timing matters more than campaigning. Every instant-rail connection includes key management and hardware security modules in its scope, and four footprint markets are connecting within twelve months ([CBBiH rulebook](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

At the same time acceptance estates are growing faster than at any point on record. Albania added roughly 10,700 terminals in a year under legal compulsion, and Kosovo about 9,400. A fleet installed in one burst refreshes together. That turns a one-off supply event into steady income from terminal management, key injection and PIN security ([Bank of Albania terminal series](https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/F6_TERMINALS_T2_Shqip_34619.xlsx), [CBK card usage report](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf)).

The one thing that must not be sold is a post-quantum deadline. The ECB has announced a further letter but has given no date.
cite_ungrounded: The pre-announced SECOND ECB letter on post-quantum cryptography is referenced here as an undated forward signal. It does not trace to any signal key in this slice, it carries no date, and it must never be presented to a customer as a deadline or as a compliance requirement.

Romania's reported 729,408 terminals and the acceptance mandate behind them are carried with the slice's own warning that Law 239/2025's article numbers, fine bands and thresholds could not be confirmed against the official gazette by any agent, and that the reported six-month ATM jump may be a reporting-scope artefact.

The description of Verification of Payee obligations as directly driving key capacity is an engineering inference from the round-the-clock, all-channel scope of the duty rather than a regulator statement.

product_outlooks.label: Core / digital channels (adjacent)
product_outlooks.scope: Growth in channel and integration work, while core-platform prime contracts stay closed
product_outlooks.summary:
This related line grows on integration and channel work, not on prime contracts for core platforms. The supervisor's end-of-life clause is the single strongest driver. Every euro-area significant institution files an action plan by 31 October 2026, saying what it will do about legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technology. That requirement reaches ageing channel and self-service software directly ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

Around it sit funded programmes with fixed dates. A core-system cutover at the merged Cypriot bank is targeted for April 2027. A Czech core migration completes during 2026. A Greek bank still has sixteen branch fit-outs to specify within about five months, on a disclosed transformation budget. Romania's widest branch network has committed to convert roughly 350 branches rather than close them ([CEC Bank Cash2Card launch](https://www.cec.ro/presa/cec-bank-lanseaza-serviciul-cash2card-numerarul-poate-fi-depus-direct-pe-cardurile-de-debit)).

The counterweight is real. Tier-one banks are bringing front-end development in-house and locking analytics into group cloud agreements. The conclusion is to aim this line at the integration and channel layer around core programmes that other vendors lead.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, but of a specific kind. The revenue sits in the channel and integration layer wrapped around core programmes that other vendors lead.

Supervision is the strongest single driver. By 31 October 2026 every significant institution files an action plan. Its fifth focus area requires "modernising infrastructure by replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies". Its first requires accurate asset inventories. Its second pulls patching into contract terms and service level agreements wherever a service provider is involved ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

This turns an ageing channel and self-service software estate from an optional refresh into a named repair item that the supervisor watches. The information-technology risk questionnaire moving to February 2027 keeps the evidence window open. The funded programmes then supply the dates.

In Cyprus the merged Eurobank Limited runs the island's largest machine estate, at 156 units. 95% of withdrawals and almost 90% of deposits are now made at machines. It has two legacy estates to bring onto one driver and one service contract, and an April 2027 core cutover ahead of it ([Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026](https://acb.com.cy/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/review-2026_low.pdf)).

In Czechia Komerční banka is replacing its core system with Temenos step by step. It says that finishing the migration of individual clients during 2026 should free up capacity in its distribution network. Meanwhile it is cutting branches at 8.6% year on year, and hosting a competitor's newest dispenser generation as a launch pilot ([Komerční banka H1-2026 results](https://www.kb.cz/getmedia/efba2b93-dcc9-4284-ab1f-ef48426b0c3e/KB-Results-2Q2026-CZ.pdf)).

In Greece CrediaBank has completed eight of twenty-four "New Experience" branch conversions. It has sixteen to specify and deliver within about five months, on a disclosed EUR 60m-plus programme for 2026-2028. Roughly 42 further sites sit behind them ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)).

Piraeus has committed about EUR 800m of capital expenditure for 2026-2030. Roughly 80% is set aside for artificial intelligence and technology. Its branch count has been frozen for ten consecutive quarters ([Piraeus Capital Markets Day 2026](https://www.piraeusgroup.gr/-/jssmedia/Com/2026/Files/Investors/Capital-Markets/CMD_Presentation_Mar05.pdf)).

In Romania CEC Bank has announced an operating-model redesign covering roughly 350 branches. It has also turned deposit-taking into national infrastructure with a service that lets anyone pay cash onto any Romanian bank's debit card ([CEC Bank Cash2Card launch](https://www.cec.ro/presa/cec-bank-lanseaza-serviciul-cash2card-numerarul-poate-fi-depus-direct-pe-cardurile-de-debit)).

In Hungary MBH runs 1,285 machines with four different quick-withdrawal set-ups across one bank. That shows its software and configuration estate is not yet unified. A new channels owner has been in post since 1 August 2026 ([MBH branch and ATM locator](https://www.mbhbank.hu/apps/backend/branch-and-atm)).

In Bulgaria Postbank is the one bank growing rather than shrinking its physical network, and has published its own two-device specification for the format ([Postbank rebrand release](https://www.postbank.bg/za-nas/novini/s-obnovena-vizualna-identichnost-i-novo-pozicionirane-na-postbank/)). In Czechia ČSOB posted five acquiring roles in four weeks, a third of national demand for the skill in one bank ([jobs.cz acquiring search](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=acquiring)).

Where to aim the effort. The first group is merged and migrating banks where two channel stacks have to become one. That includes Eurobank Limited in Cyprus before April 2027, and Alpha Bank Cyprus, where two live digital estates still run side by side against a published H2-2026 integration date. Raiffeisen's Romanian and Croatian integrations belong in this group as well.

The second group is branch-conversion programmes with published specifications and short deadlines. These are CrediaBank's sixteen fit-outs, CEC Bank's redesign of about 350 units, and Postbank's growing network.

The third is the Czech acquiring build at ČSOB. Approach it while the architecture roles are still being filled, and before the group's 11 February 2027 digital-transformation investor event resets guidance.

The fourth is the Slovak central bank's core-banking replacement, which is still before procurement. No tender was found in a sweep to 27 August 2026. Realistically that is a route through a local partner rather than a prime bid.

Two lanes are genuinely closing and should be respected. Banca Transilvania moved an entire development company's staff and contracts in-house during H1-2026, and lifted its assistant's resolution rate from 43% to 82% ([Banca Transilvania H1-2026 results](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TLV_20260821153439_Financial-results-30-06-2026.pdf)). UniCredit Romania's central analytics and know-your-customer layer sits inside a group ten-year cloud agreement.

The conclusion is simple. Stop pitching front-end digital to tier-one banks that are building it in-house. Sell instead the integration, channel and self-service layer that every core migration and branch conversion needs, and that an internal software team does not make.
drivers: The supervisory filing due on 31 October 2026. Its focus areas name legacy, unsupported and end-of-life technology, accurate asset inventories, and patching written into supplier service level agreements ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

Core and channel cutovers with fixed dates. The merged Cypriot bank that runs the island's largest machine estate has a core cutover in April 2027 ([Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026](https://acb.com.cy/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/review-2026_low.pdf)). A Czech core migration of individual clients is due to complete during 2026 ([Komerční banka H1-2026 results](https://www.kb.cz/getmedia/efba2b93-dcc9-4284-ab1f-ef48426b0c3e/KB-Results-2Q2026-CZ.pdf)).

Funded branch-conversion programmes with published specifications and short deadlines. Sixteen "New Experience" fit-outs are to be delivered by end-2026, on a disclosed EUR 60m-plus transformation programme ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)). Roughly 350 Romanian branches are set aside for operating-model redesign, against only 46 self-service zones built so far ([CEC Bank Cash2Card launch](https://www.cec.ro/presa/cec-bank-lanseaza-serviciul-cash2card-numerarul-poate-fi-depus-direct-pe-cardurile-de-debit)).

Large, disclosed and rising technology budgets attached to networks that are being kept rather than shrunk. One bank has about EUR 800m of capital expenditure for 2026-2030, with roughly 80% for artificial intelligence and technology. Its branch count has been frozen for ten quarters ([Piraeus Capital Markets Day 2026](https://www.piraeusgroup.gr/-/jssmedia/Com/2026/Files/Investors/Capital-Markets/CMD_Presentation_Mar05.pdf)).

Post-merger channel estates that are not yet unified. One Hungarian bank has 1,285 machines across three predecessor brands, with four different quick-withdrawal set-ups. A new channels owner with an automation mandate has been in post since 1 August 2026 ([MBH branch and ATM locator](https://www.mbhbank.hu/apps/backend/branch-and-atm)).

A new acquiring buying centre being staffed in Czechia. Five card-acceptance roles were posted in four weeks, and a group digital-transformation investor event is fixed for 11 February 2027 ([jobs.cz acquiring search](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=acquiring)).

The counterweight is tier-one banks bringing work in-house and locking into group agreements. One Romanian bank moved an entire development company's staff and contracts inside during H1-2026 ([Banca Transilvania H1-2026 results](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TLV_20260821153439_Financial-results-30-06-2026.pdf)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
Two changes came together this cycle. Supervision made legacy technology a named repair item that must be filed, rather than a budget preference. This is the first time a regulator has in effect written the business case for replacing end-of-life channel and self-service infrastructure ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

At the same time the tier-one banks closed the front-end opportunity by building it themselves. So the growth is not in core platforms or digital front ends. It is in the integration and channel layer that every migration, merger and branch conversion still has to buy from outside ([Banca Transilvania H1-2026 results](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TLV_20260821153439_Financial-results-30-06-2026.pdf)).

The timing is set by programmes that other organisations lead. The Cypriot cutover is due in April 2027. The Czech migration completes during 2026. Sixteen Greek fit-outs are due by year-end. The approach should therefore be made while scopes are being written, not after they are announced.
cite_ungrounded: Alpha Bank Cyprus still running two live digital estates against a published H2-2026 full-integration date comes from the Alpha Bank Cyprus ex-AstroBank signal, which sits in the payment security slice rather than this one, so it is not traceable to a signal key cited above.
Raiffeisen's Romanian and Croatian integrations are named here as channel-consolidation targets; the underlying EUR 70m and EUR 75m programme evidence sits in the compliance slice, not in this one.

The Slovak core-banking replacement is described as pre-procurement on the strength of a negative finding — a notice sweep to 27/08/2026 that returned no tender — which is evidence of absence at a point in time rather than a statement of the buyer's intent.

outlooks.scope: CrediaBank: sixteen branch conversions still to complete in 2026
outlooks.summary:
CrediaBank has promised to convert 24 branches to its "New Experience" format by the end of 2026. That format is built around cash automation. At its half-year results, published on 6 August 2026, only eight conversions were complete. Sixteen branch fit-outs therefore have to be specified and delivered in the rest of the year, on a network that stays at 66 branches ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results presentation](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)).

The money is already disclosed and being spent, as part of a EUR 60m-plus digital transformation programme for 2026-2028. The bank's own specification asks for teller cash recyclers across the whole network. These are machines that re-use the notes customers have just paid in. Virtual teller stations are planned only at flagship sites, so there are two separate hardware lines to bid for.

Printec should aim at the in-branch cash and self-service fit-out, not at the ATM estate, which has been contracted out to Euronet. The digital instant loan due in October 2026 is a second, separate way in, through remote identity checks.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, with most of it coming early. The triggers are dated, and the dates are close.

The half-year results published on 6 August 2026 confirm 24 branches due for conversion by end-2026. Only eight are complete. Six more are scheduled by early in the fourth quarter, and the remaining ten by year-end.

The Company Information Memorandum of 30 March 2026 says the bank plans to remodel the whole 66-branch network within two years. That leaves roughly 42 more sites for 2027-28. The same document names the same model for export to HSBC Malta's twelve branches.

The digital instant loan goes live in October 2026, which will need remote identity checks at scale. Customer Care launches in September 2026 and omnichannel in November 2026, either side of it ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results presentation](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)).

The limit to respect is scope. Euronet has exclusive rights over "ATM-related technical services" and CrediaBank's 141-machine ATM estate. That deal had still not closed as at 31 August 2026. There was no filing with the Hellenic Competition Commission, and no mention of CrediaBank in Euronet's second-quarter report ([Euronet Q2-2026 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1029199/000155485526001702/eeft-20260630.htm)).

Who to talk to: the CrediaBank branch-transformation and procurement owners. The topics are teller cash recyclers for the whole network, virtual teller stations for the flagship sites, card-on-entry customer recognition and accessibility kiosks. Work the October instant-loan launch separately. It is an electronic know-your-customer (identity check) conversation that sits fully outside the Euronet scope.

In short: the sixteen unbuilt conversions are the near-term contest. The roughly 42 sites behind them, plus the stated Malta export, are the reason to win the first one.
drivers: Only eight of the 24 planned "New Experience" branch conversions were complete at the half-year results published on 6 August 2026. Sixteen remain to be fitted out in the rest of 2026, on a network that stays at 66 branches ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results presentation](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)).

The bank has published its own specification, and it is built around cash automation. Customers are identified by bank card on entry, and cash transactions go through teller cash recyclers. Virtual teller stations link customers to staff through "CrediaConnect", and open collaboration areas replace the teller counter. Recyclers go network-wide, but virtual teller stations go only to flagship sites, so the two lines can be specified separately ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results presentation](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)).

Funding is disclosed and already being spent. There is a EUR 60m-plus Digital Transformation Programme for 2026-2028, with an 80-strong technology team. Half-year recurring operating expenses of EUR 76.7m are put down directly to the digital transformation and branch renovations ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results presentation](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)).

A dated digital timetable runs alongside the fit-outs. Customer Care is due in September 2026. The digital instant loan follows in October 2026, and omnichannel in November 2026. The loan launch will need remote identity checks at scale ([CrediaBank Company Information Memorandum, 30/03/2026](https://www.crediabank.com/media/sq2hz5w1/8-company-information-memorandum-30032026.pdf)).

Euronet's exclusive rights are worded around "ATM-related technical services" and cover the 141 ATMs. The deal was still not closed at 31 August 2026. There was no filing with the competition authority and no mention in the buyer's own quarterly report ([Euronet Q2-2026 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1029199/000155485526001702/eeft-20260630.htm)).
outlooks.rationale:
The plan has not changed, but the reported numbers have. The bank published its own progress on 6 August 2026. The gap between what it promised for 2026 and what it has built is now sixteen branches, with only the rest of the year to close it. Those branches must be specified and ordered this quarter, or the year-end promise slips ([CrediaBank H1-2026 results presentation](https://www.crediabank.com/media/4p2kyv35/crediabank-i1-2026-financial-results-presentation-vf.pdf)).

At the same time, the final Euronet contract is still unsigned. The line between the ATM scope, which is closed off, and the in-branch cash and self-service scope is therefore easiest to argue right now ([Euronet Q2-2026 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1029199/000155485526001702/eeft-20260630.htm)). Once that deal closes, the argument gets harder.
cite_ungrounded: The "five months" framing is arithmetic from the 06/08/2026 results date to 31/12/2026, not a period the bank itself states.

Whether teller cash recyclers, virtual teller stations, entry recognition and accessibility kiosks fall outside Euronet's "ATM-related technical services" exclusivity is a reading of the clause, not a determination by either party to the agreement.
No supplier is named on any of the sixteen outstanding fit-outs; that the scope is unawarded is inferred from the absence of a disclosed supplier, not from a statement that it is open.

outlooks.scope: ODAP Phase B visitor services, EUR 30m: award still to be decided
outlooks.summary:
The Organisation for the Management and Development of Cultural Resources closed bids on 23 July 2026 for Phase B of digital visitor services at Greek archaeological sites and museums. An independent re-check of Greek notices on 27 August 2026 found no contract-award notice. The decision is therefore being made right now ([TED notice 408136-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/408136-2026/xml)).

The notice gives a value of EUR 30,013,782.92. It does not say whether this includes value-added tax, so do not quote it either way.

The fit for Printec comes from the list of product codes. It includes ticket-issuing machines and point-of-sale software, alongside systems integration, across 108 existing Phase-A sites and 17 new ones. Printec's realistic role is a subcontract under whichever systems integrator wins. The value of this signal is knowing that the award is close, and reaching the likely lead bidders before it lands rather than after.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, with little time to act. The open tender was published in the EU tenders journal as notice 408136-2026 on 15 June 2026. Bids closed on 23 July 2026. The re-check of Greek notices on 27 August 2026 found no award notice, so bids are being evaluated now. The award goes to the best price-quality ratio ([TED notice 408136-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/408136-2026/xml)).

The scope adds to services already running at 108 Phase-A sites and extends them to 17 more. A Phase-A contract-change notice published 15 May 2026 shows a total contract value of EUR 23,202,224.50. That is the best guide to how the current supplier's work is shaped. This is the only Greek notice in the whole April-to-August 2026 window with a ticket-issuing-machine product code, so there is no similar second chance in this period.

Who to talk to: the systems integrators bidding for ODAP Phase B. The subject is the self-service ticketing kiosk, queue-management and card-acceptance parts of the lot, not leading the integration itself. Separately, talk to ODAP about the field-service, monitoring and cash-and-card operations layer that follows go-live across 125 visitor sites.

In short: get in position with the likely lead bidders in the weeks before the award is published. Once it is published, the subcontract structure is usually already fixed.
drivers: Bids closed on 23 July 2026, and no contract-award notice had been published as at 27 August 2026. The award decision is therefore still open at the time of writing ([TED notice 408136-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/408136-2026/xml)).

The product codes include ticket-issuing machines and point-of-sale software alongside systems integration. This is the only Greek notice in the whole April-to-August 2026 window with a ticket-issuing-machine code ([TED notice 408136-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/408136-2026/xml)).

The scope covers 108 Phase-A sites plus 17 new ones, 125 visitor locations in all. The award goes to the best price-quality ratio ([TED notice 408136-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/408136-2026/xml)).

A Phase-A contract-change notice published on 15 May 2026 records a total contract value of EUR 23,202,224.50. That gives a concrete example of how the earlier phase was sized and delivered ([TED notice 408136-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/408136-2026/xml)).
outlooks.rationale: The requirement has not changed; the timing has. Bids closed on 23 July 2026, and the independent re-check on 27 August 2026 confirms that no award notice has appeared. That puts the programme in the short window where a lead bidder is still building its subcontractor list. After that, the list is fixed for the life of the contract ([TED notice 408136-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/408136-2026/xml)). That window is the reason to act this month rather than next.
cite_ungrounded: The notice does not state whether EUR 30,013,782.92 is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, so any per-site or per-machine sizing derived from it is unsupported arithmetic.
The description of the 125 locations as high-footfall cash-and-card sites is inference from the scope, not language in the notice.
No bidder list is public, so identifying "plausible primes" has to be done from Greek market knowledge that sits outside this evidence base.
That a subcontract is the realistic route for Printec is a commercial judgement carried in the source's own reading, not a term of the tender.

outlooks.scope: ELTA EUR 6m retail transformation: consultation open until 10 September
outlooks.summary:
The Growthfund's Strategic Contracts Unit issued an amended invitation to a preliminary market consultation on 18 August 2026. It covers a "Retail and Delivery Transformation Initiative" at ELTA, Hellenic Post, budgeted at EUR 6,000,000 excluding value-added tax. Comments are due through the ESIDIS platform by 10 September 2026 ([Growthfund preliminary consultation invitation, 18/08/2026](https://media.elta.gr/uploads/media/etairia/diakirixeis/20260818diavoulepsi1982026.pdf)).

This is the only stage at which the specification can still be shaped, ahead of a tender that will probably launch in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The retail and counter half of the scope maps directly onto counter and point-of-sale systems, queue management, self-service kiosks and document management. It covers a post-office network that now takes deposits and pays out withdrawals as a bank agent for Eurobank.

Because the Growthfund runs it as a single strategic contract, the realistic shape is a consortium pairing a retail and counter partner with a logistics track-and-trace partner. Separately, every ELTA branch closed under the restructuring leaves a cash-access point without a provider, which an off-site ATM can serve.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, with a consultation that closes on 10 September 2026.

The consultation, reference 2026DIAB33462, was mandated by the Government Committee on Strategic Contracts on 27 July 2026 and is financed by ELTA itself. Comments must be filed through ESIDIS by 10 September 2026. They may cover the technical specifications, whether the budget matches the scope, and individual tender terms. The two-page invitation has no technical annex, so the split between the retail half and the logistics control-tower half has to be requested from the named contact ([Growthfund preliminary consultation invitation, 18/08/2026](https://media.elta.gr/uploads/media/etairia/diakirixeis/20260818diavoulepsi1982026.pdf)).

The counter network underneath it is working bank infrastructure. Eurobank re-issued its official ELTA branch-network page on 3 August 2026. It lists post offices where its customers open accounts, get debit cards, move payroll, and deposit and withdraw cash ([Eurobank ELTA branch-network page](https://www.eurobank.gr/el/diktuo-katastimaton-elta)).

The underlying restructuring marked 204 low-activity ELTA branches for closure, the first 46 from 3 November 2025. The stated reason is that branches carry under 10% of revenue and about 45% of operating cost.

Two pieces of context are useful in the meeting but should not lead the pitch. ELTA already runs 117 ATMs and buys ATM security and monitoring separately. The largest Greek counter cash-automation contract of the year was a five-year operational lease of 300 banknote counting and quality-sorting machines. It went to the Greek supplier BOOS S.A. at EUR 19.25 per machine per month excluding value-added tax, which is roughly 39% of the buyer's own published estimate. That sets both the commercial model and the price level that any bid into Greek counter cash automation has to survive ([Diavgeia — ELTA award decision](https://diavgeia.gov.gr/doc/%CE%A86%CE%93%CE%A8%CE%9F%CE%A1%CE%A12-%CE%A5%CE%9F%CE%A1)).

Where to aim:
- The Growthfund Strategic Contracts Unit and the named ELTA contact, before 10 September, on counter and point-of-sale systems, queue management, self-service kiosks and document management. Pair this with a logistics track-and-trace partner for the delivery half.
- The municipalities losing post-office counters, where Printec's own Cashflex off-site venture is the vehicle for cash access left without a provider. Its public locator returned exactly 480 ATM sites when pulled on 27 August 2026 ([Cashflex ATM locator](https://cashflex.gr/wp-json/atm/v1/all)).

In short: file a consultation response by 10 September and choose the logistics partner in the same fortnight. The specification written now is the specification that will be bid on in the fourth quarter.
drivers: An amended invitation to a preliminary market consultation was issued on 18 August 2026 under reference 2026DIAB33462. It is budgeted at EUR 6,000,000 excluding value-added tax, financed by ELTA and mandated by the Government Committee on Strategic Contracts on 27 July 2026. Comments are due through ESIDIS by 10 September 2026 ([Growthfund preliminary consultation invitation, 18/08/2026](https://media.elta.gr/uploads/media/etairia/diakirixeis/20260818diavoulepsi1982026.pdf)).

The invitation has no technical annex. The scope split between retail systems and logistics track-and-trace is therefore not fixed, and it has to be requested from the named contact. That is exactly what a consultation response can influence ([Growthfund preliminary consultation invitation, 18/08/2026](https://media.elta.gr/uploads/media/etairia/diakirixeis/20260818diavoulepsi1982026.pdf)).

The counter network is working bank-agency infrastructure. Eurobank re-issued its official ELTA branch-network page on 3 August 2026. It lists post offices where customers open accounts, get debit cards, move payroll, and deposit and withdraw cash ([Eurobank ELTA branch-network page](https://www.eurobank.gr/el/diktuo-katastimaton-elta)).

The restructuring marked 204 low-activity ELTA branches for closure, the first 46 from 3 November 2025. The stated reason is that branches carry under 10% of revenue and about 45% of operating cost. Each closure leaves a cash-access gap in its municipality ([Growthfund preliminary consultation invitation, 18/08/2026](https://media.elta.gr/uploads/media/etairia/diakirixeis/20260818diavoulepsi1982026.pdf)).

A competitor has just reset the price and commercial model for Greek counter cash automation. A five-year operational lease of 300 banknote counting and sorting machines at ELTA went to BOOS S.A. The price is EUR 19.25 per machine per month excluding value-added tax, about 39% of the buyer's own estimate. A 200-machine option was still unused as at 22 July 2026 ([Diavgeia — ELTA award decision](https://diavgeia.gov.gr/doc/%CE%A86%CE%93%CE%A8%CE%9F%CE%A1%CE%A12-%CE%A5%CE%9F%CE%A1)).
outlooks.rationale:
The consultation is the change. Until 18 August 2026, ELTA was a restructuring case. The amended invitation turns it into a budgeted, referenced procurement with a comment deadline three weeks away and a tender expected to follow ([Growthfund preliminary consultation invitation, 18/08/2026](https://media.elta.gr/uploads/media/etairia/diakirixeis/20260818diavoulepsi1982026.pdf)).

A preliminary consultation is the one stage where a supplier can influence what is asked for, not only how it is answered. Because the invitation has no technical annex, the scope split is still open.

The BOOS award of the 300-machine counting-machine lease at 39% of estimate is the second reason the timing matters. Someone else has just set the price benchmark for this buyer. It is better to argue that benchmark during specification than during evaluation ([Diavgeia — ELTA award decision](https://diavgeia.gov.gr/doc/%CE%A86%CE%93%CE%A8%CE%9F%CE%A1%CE%A12-%CE%A5%CE%9F%CE%A1)).
cite_ungrounded: A fourth-quarter 2026 tender launch is described in the evidence as plausible, not scheduled — no tender date has been published.
The mapping of the retail half of the scope onto counter systems, queue management, kiosks and document management is a reading of a two-page invitation that carries no technical annex.

The size of Printec's Cashflex off-site fleet is unreconciled: 480 ATM sites is what its own public locator returned on 27/08/2026 and no larger carried figure should be quoted until the installed base is reconciled internally.
That closed ELTA branches convert into siteable off-site cash-access points is a commercial inference; no municipality has published such a requirement.

outlooks.scope: Alpha Bank Cyprus still runs two channel systems in parallel
outlooks.summary:
Ten months after the deal legally completed, Alpha Bank Cyprus was still running two live digital estates on 31 August 2026. There was a separate ex-AstroBank e-banking login pointing at the old astrobank.com domain, a parallel product tree, a live system-integration help hub and two sets of call-centre numbers. This runs against a full-integration date the group itself placed in the second half of 2026 ([Alpha Bank Q2-2026 results presentation](https://www.alpha.gr/-/media/AlphaGr/Files/Group/Apotelesmata/2026-Q2/20260731-presentation.pdf)).

Running two parallel systems is the most expensive state a merged bank can be in. So the vendor choices on self-service driving software, screens, authentication and key management are being fixed over the next few months.

Nine branch mergers were announced on 18 March 2026, and a Cyprus voluntary separation scheme has EUR 18m set aside. Together these point at two things. The first is teller cash automation to replace lost staff capacity. The second is a decision at every merged site on whether to retire, move or replace the ATM. Size it honestly: at roughly 26 machines this is a contest for a reference and for managed services across a mixed two-vendor estate, not for hardware volume.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, but of the recurring-revenue kind rather than the volume kind. The dated triggers stack up. Alpha's second-quarter investor presentation of 31 July 2026 has a mergers-and-acquisitions tracker that puts the AstroBank full-integration date in the second half of 2026.

It books an EUR 18m provision for a Cyprus voluntary separation scheme. The audited provisions note gives EUR 17m, for a scheme approved in May 2026 offering a maximum EUR 225,000 per employee, with union consultation complete. Group administrative expenses rose partly because of "higher IT expenses, partly attributable to the integration of AstroBank's systems into Alpha Bank Cyprus" ([Alpha Bank Q2-2026 results presentation](https://www.alpha.gr/-/media/AlphaGr/Files/Group/Apotelesmata/2026-Q2/20260731-presentation.pdf)).

Nine branch mergers were announced on 18 March 2026. Each pairs an old Alpha site with an ex-AstroBank site, and no effective dates were published ([Alpha Bank Cyprus — Reorganization of Branch Network](https://www.alphabank.com.cy/en/the-bank/press-office/reorganization-of-branch-eng)). Paying utility bills and taxes at the branch was withdrawn on 2 February 2026, in favour of an app channel funded by card. That leaves cash-paying customers no route at all, which is an assisted self-service gap the bank created itself.

Two cautions must go with any proposal. The whole-portfolio card reissue onto new card numbers, described in earlier briefing material, is not supported by this cycle's evidence. The bank's own replacement hub and questions-and-answers pages show only the co-branded Aegean Visa portfolio moving to Mastercard, because that partnership is ending. So the card opportunity must not be sold as mass reissuance driven by the merger, and it has to be checked directly with the bank. The second caution is that Salesforce Financial Services Cloud went live on 30 April 2026, so the customer-relationship layer is already taken.

Where to aim, with Alpha Bank Cyprus channel and operations owners:

- A single managed-service and monitoring contract across the mixed two-vendor ATM estate.
- The machine decisions at each of the nine mergers.
- Teller cash automation, to replace the staff leaving under the separation scheme.
- Key management for the new card ranges. The bank's own ATM page still lists 3DES, an ageing encryption cipher, as its ATM-to-host protection, which is worth checking against a move to AES.

In short: no Printec incumbency is confirmed at this bank. Treat the published integration end-date as the decision date, and be in front of it rather than behind it.
drivers: At 31 August 2026 the bank still ran two live digital estates. These were an ex-AstroBank login on the old astrobank.com domain, a parallel product tree, a system-integration help hub and two sets of call-centre numbers. That is against a full-integration date the group placed in the second half of 2026 ([Alpha Bank Q2-2026 results presentation](https://www.alpha.gr/-/media/AlphaGr/Files/Group/Apotelesmata/2026-Q2/20260731-presentation.pdf)).

An EUR 18m provision was booked for a Cyprus voluntary separation scheme approved in May 2026, at up to EUR 225,000 per employee, with union consultation complete. Group administrative expenses rose on higher information-technology costs attributed to integrating AstroBank's systems ([Alpha Bank Q2-2026 results presentation](https://www.alpha.gr/-/media/AlphaGr/Files/Group/Apotelesmata/2026-Q2/20260731-presentation.pdf)).

Nine branch mergers were announced on 18 March 2026, each pairing an old Alpha site with an ex-AstroBank site, with no effective dates published. Every one is a live decision about what happens to the machine on that site ([Alpha Bank Cyprus — Reorganization of Branch Network](https://www.alphabank.com.cy/en/the-bank/press-office/reorganization-of-branch-eng)).

Paying utility bills and taxes at the branch was withdrawn on 2 February 2026, in favour of an app channel funded by card. Customers who pay in cash now have no in-branch route ([Alpha Bank Cyprus — Reorganization of Branch Network](https://www.alphabank.com.cy/en/the-bank/press-office/reorganization-of-branch-eng)).

A correction to carry, not repeat: the whole-portfolio card reissue driven by the merger, previously assumed at this bank, is not evidenced. Only the co-branded Aegean Visa portfolio is moving to Mastercard, because that partnership is ending ([Alpha Bank Q2-2026 results presentation](https://www.alpha.gr/-/media/AlphaGr/Files/Group/Apotelesmata/2026-Q2/20260731-presentation.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
The date has effectively arrived and the work has not. Alpha put full integration in the second half of 2026 in its presentation of 31 July 2026. Yet on 31 August 2026 both digital estates were still live and both call-centre numbers were still published. This means the platform, driving-software and authentication decisions that normally come with a cutover are being taken now, rather than already taken ([Alpha Bank Q2-2026 results presentation](https://www.alpha.gr/-/media/AlphaGr/Files/Group/Apotelesmata/2026-Q2/20260731-presentation.pdf)).

A voluntary separation scheme running while nine sites merge is the standard trigger for teller cash automation to replace lost capacity. And each merged site forces a machine decision that cannot be put off past the cutover ([Alpha Bank Cyprus — Reorganization of Branch Network](https://www.alphabank.com.cy/en/the-bank/press-office/reorganization-of-branch-eng)).
cite_ungrounded: "Roughly a third of a 26-machine ATM estate" is the source's own approximation of the nine consolidations; no per-site machine count is published.
That an AES key-management refresh is required is a qualification question raised by the bank's own published 3DES documentation, not a stated bank plan or budget line.
"Mixed two-vendor estate" describes the fact of a merger between two banks; no ATM hardware or software supplier is named on either side, and no Printec incumbency is confirmed.

The AML platform at this bank is undisclosed. Any suggestion that Printec supplies a named anti-money-laundering product inside the Alpha group is unsupported — a full-text search of the H1-2026 report returned no AML supplier at all.

outlooks.scope: Almost nine in ten Eurobank Cyprus deposits now arrive at a machine
outlooks.summary:
Eurobank Limited said on 6 August 2026 that 95% of withdrawals and almost 90% of deposits are now made at machines rather than at a counter. The branch share of all transactions fell from 4.7% in 2024 to 3.5% ([Eurobank 1H-2026 results presentation](https://www.eurobank.gr/-/media/eurobank/omilos/enimerosi-ependuton/enimerosi-metoxon-eurobank/oikonomika-apotelesmata/2026/2q-2026/2q2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

The fleet doing that work is 156 ATMs. It is the largest on the island and 49% of the 321 machines run by the eight member banks. It is really two legacy estates. They must be brought onto one driver, one hardware and software generation and one service contract before a core-banking cutover targeted for April 2027. The driver is the software that runs the ATMs ([Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026](https://acb.com.cy/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/review-2026_low.pdf)).

Printec is not a named incumbent here. So ATM and self-service consolidation, cash-cycle and cash-in-transit optimisation, and the branch-and-ATM re-imaging work are all genuinely open to compete for.

Aim at deposit-capable and recycling machines and at a single island-wide service contract. Do not size the opportunity off the group's EUR 1bn technology headline, because no Cyprus allocation is published.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth in addressable scope, against a cutover date the bank has set for itself. The triggers have dates and they add up.

The Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026 was read directly this cycle. It gives Eurobank Limited 156 ATMs, 59 branches and 2,450 staff, so the fleet figure no longer comes from the press ([Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026](https://acb.com.cy/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/review-2026_low.pdf)).

The bank's own channel data of 6 August 2026 puts 95% of withdrawals and almost 90% of deposits at machines, and card-at-point-of-sale at 68.5% of transactions. The half-year disclosures of 30 July 2026 show 67 outlets and 2,716 staff. The outlets are 52 retail branches plus 15 business and private-banking centres. 139 staff and six business centres were shed in the second quarter alone, while two retail branches were added.

The directors repeat that the operational merger is under way "to provide unified platforms". A voluntary exit of about 200 staff completed in April 2026, for an EUR 35m one-off charge and around EUR 14m of annual savings. EUR 140m of Cyprus merger synergies are to be fully phased by 2027, with EUR 85m still to capture. Only about EUR 25m of that is operating cost ([Eurobank 1H-2026 results presentation](https://www.eurobank.gr/-/media/eurobank/omilos/enimerosi-ependuton/enimerosi-metoxon-eurobank/oikonomika-apotelesmata/2026/2q-2026/2q2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

If nine in ten deposits already arrive through the machine estate, that estate is doing the teller's job. It has to be deposit-capable and recycling to keep doing it. A recycler is a machine that re-dispenses the notes customers have just paid in, which also removes cash-in-transit trips.

Two limits to respect. The far smaller ex-Eurobank Cyprus side went live on Temenos core, digital and financial-crime software in June 2024, so anti-money-laundering scope is contested. But ATM hardware, ATM driving, recyclers and managed services sit outside it. The group's roughly EUR 1bn "Banking Forward" technology programme for 2025-2028 names Cyprus in scope but publishes no Cyprus allocation, so no euro figure may be quoted from it.

Where to aim: the Eurobank Limited merger-integration and channels owners. The conversation covers standardising two ATM estates onto one driver and one service contract ahead of April 2027, and recycler-class replacement to absorb the deposit load. It also covers refilling and cash-in-transit optimisation, and the branch-and-ATM re-imaging the bank has itself named as infrastructure it must update to the new corporate image.

In short: the cutover is the forcing function. Decisions taken before it cover the whole estate, and decisions taken after it are made one machine at a time.
drivers: The bank's own channel data of 6 August 2026 puts 95% of withdrawals and almost 90% of deposits at machines rather than counters. The branch share of all transactions fell from 4.7% in 2024 to 3.5% ([Eurobank 1H-2026 results presentation](https://www.eurobank.gr/-/media/eurobank/omilos/enimerosi-ependuton/enimerosi-metoxon-eurobank/oikonomika-apotelesmata/2026/2q-2026/2q2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

The 156-ATM fleet is now confirmed from the banking association's own annual review rather than from the press. The review gives 156 machines, 59 branches and 2,450 staff. It is the largest estate on the island and 49% of the 321 machines run by the eight member banks ([Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026](https://acb.com.cy/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/review-2026_low.pdf)).

Two legacy estates have to be standardised before a core-banking cutover targeted for April 2027. The directors state that the operational merger is under way "to provide unified platforms" ([Eurobank 1H-2026 results presentation](https://www.eurobank.gr/-/media/eurobank/omilos/enimerosi-ependuton/enimerosi-metoxon-eurobank/oikonomika-apotelesmata/2026/2q-2026/2q2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

The staffed footprint is shrinking around the machines. A voluntary exit of about 200 staff completed in April 2026, for an EUR 35m one-off charge and around EUR 14m of annual savings. A further 139 staff and six business centres were shed in the second quarter of 2026 ([Eurobank 1H-2026 results presentation](https://www.eurobank.gr/-/media/eurobank/omilos/enimerosi-ependuton/enimerosi-metoxon-eurobank/oikonomika-apotelesmata/2026/2q-2026/2q2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

EUR 140m of Cyprus merger synergies are to be fully phased by 2027, with EUR 85m still to capture. Only about EUR 25m of that is operating cost, so the remaining benefit has to come from platform and channel consolidation rather than from headcount alone ([Eurobank 1H-2026 results presentation](https://www.eurobank.gr/-/media/eurobank/omilos/enimerosi-ependuton/enimerosi-metoxon-eurobank/oikonomika-apotelesmata/2026/2q-2026/2q2026-results-presentation.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
Two things changed on the same account in the same fortnight. The 156-ATM figure stopped being press-derived and was read directly from the banking association's annual review. And the bank published channel data showing that the machine estate, not the branch, is where its customers actually bank ([Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026](https://acb.com.cy/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/review-2026_low.pdf)).

Set against a core cutover targeted for April 2027, that turns a merger-integration item into a dated estate decision. Two ATM fleets cannot be driven by two systems through one new core ([Eurobank 1H-2026 results presentation](https://www.eurobank.gr/-/media/eurobank/omilos/enimerosi-ependuton/enimerosi-metoxon-eurobank/oikonomika-apotelesmata/2026/2q-2026/2q2026-results-presentation.pdf)).
cite_ungrounded: No Cyprus allocation of the roughly EUR 1bn "Banking Forward" group programme is published, so any euro sizing of this opportunity is unsupported.
How many of the 156 machines are already deposit-capable or recycling is not disclosed; the recycler case rests on the published deposit-share data, not on a capability split.
The April-2027 core cutover is a target carried in the evidence, not a contractual milestone, and no tender or vendor decision date has been published.
That the ATM and self-service scope is contestable rests on the absence of a named incumbent, not on a statement that the work is out to market.

outlooks.scope: Cyprus insolvency case-management tender of about EUR 7m, closing 15 September after six extensions
outlooks.summary:
Tender TA 03/2024 covers the supply, implementation, maintenance and operation of an integrated case-management system for Cyprus's Department of Insolvency. It also includes infrastructure-as-a-service, which is rented computing capacity. It closes at 11:00 on 15 September 2026. The contract starts on 5 October 2026 and runs for twelve years ([TED contract notice 414250-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/414250-2026/xml)).

The estimated contract amount is EUR 5,652,000, plus about EUR 1,390,000 of renewals and EUR 150,000 of options. That is a maximum lifetime value near EUR 7.19m.

The same notice has been republished six times on a rolling deadline since 30 October 2025, at an unchanged estimate. There has been no cancellation and no award. This suggests the local market has not been willing to price the requirement, in a country of about a million people. A regional integrator with local field engineers could address it, in consortium with a case-management and document-management partner.

The immediate question is whether to bid, not how to bid. The deadline is inside three weeks, and a seventh extension cannot be assumed.
outlooks.projected:
Mixed. The contract is long, large and genuinely open to new bidders, but it also carries real unpriced risk. The decision has to be made in days rather than months.

The mechanics are an open procedure awarded on best price-quality ratio, with a single lot and a twelve-year contract. A bid bond and twelve-month bid validity apply. Submission closes at 11:00 on 15 September 2026, and opening is the same morning. The portal's live countdown was still running when checked on 27 August 2026 ([eprocurement.gov.cy tender record 8034153](https://www.eprocurement.gov.cy/epps/cft/prepareViewCfTWS.do?resourceId=8034153)).

There have been six republications since 30 October 2025 at an unchanged estimate. A full-text search found no seventh extension, no cancellation and no award notice. That is what an unbid requirement looks like, and the reasons are visible: twelve years of commitment, hosting liability and a full custom build ([TED contract notice 414250-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/414250-2026/xml)).

The strategic argument is about adjacency as much as the contract itself. The Cypriot insolvency estate touches bank non-performing-loan workout and the KEDIPES run-off vehicle.
