A twelve-year term therefore secures a decade of adjacent access as well as a revenue line. That matters more than usual here, because Cyprus is structurally a direct-sales market rather than a tender market. The commercial banks are private companies and never appear on the procurement portal at all.

Several recent public awards drew exactly one bid. One example is the Housing Finance Corporation's project-management office, awarded to Deloitte at EUR 648,520 against a EUR 650,000 estimate. It drew a single bid, after the notice had to be published four times ([TED award notice 483317-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/483317-2026/xml)).

Where to focus: a consortium decision inside the next week. Printec would be the local delivery, field-service and infrastructure party, alongside a case-management and document-management software partner. Hosting and the twelve-year liability should be priced explicitly rather than absorbed.

Conclusion: the deadline, not the scope, is what forces this decision. Decide to bid or to stand down before 15 September, and record the reasoning either way, because the same buyer profile will come up again.
drivers: Bids close at 11:00 on 15 September 2026, and opening is the same morning. The contract starts on 5 October 2026 and runs for twelve years. It is an open procedure awarded on best price-quality ratio, with a bid bond and twelve-month bid validity ([TED contract notice 414250-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/414250-2026/xml)).

The estimated value is EUR 5,652,000, plus about EUR 1,390,000 of renewals and EUR 150,000 of options. That is roughly EUR 7.19m over the life of the contract ([TED contract notice 414250-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/414250-2026/xml)).

The same notice has been republished six times on a rolling deadline since 30 October 2025, at an unchanged estimate. No seventh extension, cancellation or award notice was found ([eprocurement.gov.cy tender record 8034153](https://www.eprocurement.gov.cy/epps/cft/prepareViewCfTWS.do?resourceId=8034153)).

The twelve-year term secures the Cypriot insolvency estate, which touches bank non-performing-loan workout and the KEDIPES run-off vehicle. Losing the tender means losing a decade of adjacent access as well as a single contract ([TED contract notice 414250-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/414250-2026/xml)).

Cyprus is a direct-sales market. No open or awarded Cypriot public notice for ATMs, self-service, terminals or monitoring exists in this cycle, because the banks are private companies. Several recent public awards drew exactly one bid ([TED award notice 483317-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/483317-2026/xml)).
outlooks.rationale:
What has changed is the timing, not the requirement. A notice that has been rolled over six times since October 2025 is now inside three weeks of closing. The portal countdown is still running, and no seventh extension has been published. That turns a standing item into a decision with a date attached ([eprocurement.gov.cy tender record 8034153](https://www.eprocurement.gov.cy/epps/cft/prepareViewCfTWS.do?resourceId=8034153)).

Nothing about the scope has become easier. What changed is that waiting is no longer an option. In this market, almost no public self-service demand ever reaches a portal. A rare visible contract with a thin bidder field therefore deserves an explicit decision to bid or not, rather than a default no.
cite_ungrounded: "The local market will not bid" is the source's inference from six republications; no bidder list, and no confirmed absence of bidders, is published.
No consortium partner is identified anywhere in the evidence — pairing with a case-management and document-management software house is a construction of Printec's, not a fact about the tender.
Whether a seventh extension will be published is unknowable; the evidence only confirms that none existed on 27/08/2026.
The scale of the KEDIPES and non-performing-loan adjacency is asserted qualitatively in the source and carries no published value.

outlooks.scope: DSK: disclosed information-technology costs and almost no kiosk layer
outlooks.summary:
On its half-year results call of 5 August 2026, OTP said that Bulgarian normalised operating expenses rose 22% year on year on a currency-adjusted basis. Rising information-technology costs were one of the reasons. OTP also said that joining the euro area cut the mandatory reserve ratio from 12% to 1%. That freed almost EUR 2bn of liquidity at DSK that had previously earned no interest ([OTP Group 1H-2026 results conference call, 05/08/2026](https://www.otpgroup.info/static/sw/file/2026_2Q_conference_call_final.pdf)).

Bulgaria's largest retail bank therefore has a named cost problem and the balance-sheet room to fund a response. It is also hiring to deal with it.

Two gaps are visible in the bank's own published estate. Exactly one site in 777 has a kiosk device. Coin deposit is entirely manual at the counter, pre-sorted by denomination. The card software layer is closed by BPC's SmartVista.

The opportunity at DSK is therefore self-service and kiosk hardware, cash automation including coin, and managed services. It also includes the resilience gap exposed by a run of outages in July 2026.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth is likely, because the spending cycle is disclosed rather than estimated. On its call of 5 August 2026, OTP said that in Bulgaria "normalized operating expenses increased by 22% year on year on an FX-adjusted basis". It attributed this to "several years of double-digit wage inflation as well as rising IT costs". OTP also said that euro accession cut the mandatory reserve ratio from 12% to 1% and released almost EUR 2bn of previously non-interest-bearing liquidity at DSK. Revenue fell because of lost foreign-exchange conversion income ([OTP Group 1H-2026 results conference call, 05/08/2026](https://www.otpgroup.info/static/sw/file/2026_2Q_conference_call_final.pdf)).

The estate is changing in the way that argument predicts. OTP's statutory half-year report gives DSK 952 ATMs at 30 June 2026 against 271 branches, so machines are up year on year while branches shrink. The locator re-pull of 27 August 2026 shows sites with ATMs flat at 724. The reduction is therefore entirely on the branch side.

Hiring points the same way. DSK had 38 live technology roles on dev.bg at 31 August 2026. These include two card-systems support postings running at once, an enterprise architect, a cloud infrastructure product owner and a senior governance expert for an innovation and artificial-intelligence office.

The gap sits where the bank has built nothing. Exactly one site in 777 has a kiosk device, and 129 have a twenty-four-hour self-service zone. Coin deposit is one hundred per cent manual at the counter, pre-sorted by denomination, and it is explicitly left out of the bank's ATM deposit campaign. Coin volumes nationally have been sized by the central bank's EUR 115,480,000 procurement of euro coin blanks. That order is split across the Bulgarian and Slovak mints, and bids closed on 3 August 2026 ([TED 449605-2026 — BNB euro coin blanks](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/449605-2026/xml)).

Two constraints are real. BPC's SmartVista is the entrenched card switch and ATM driving layer, and it completed the lev-to-euro migration of 2.6m debit and 300k credit card accounts. A cluster of mobile and card-payment outages also ran through July 2026, with no ATM or branch fallback offered.

Approach DSK's channel, cash-operations and procurement owners. Offer an assisted self-service and kiosk layer across a 777-site network that currently has one kiosk. Also offer coin counting and deposit automation, managed services and estate monitoring, and a fix for the resilience and fallback gap that the July outages exposed. Build the case on cost per transaction, using DSK's own 22% operating-expense figure.

In short: lead with hardware, cash automation and services rather than card software, and use the bank's own disclosed cost problem as the business case.
drivers: OTP disclosed on 5 August 2026 that Bulgarian normalised operating expenses rose 22% year on year on a currency-adjusted basis. Rising information-technology costs were part of the reason, and lost foreign-exchange conversion income cut revenue ([OTP Group 1H-2026 results conference call, 05/08/2026](https://www.otpgroup.info/static/sw/file/2026_2Q_conference_call_final.pdf)).

Joining the euro area cut the mandatory reserve ratio from 12% to 1%. That released almost EUR 2bn of previously non-interest-bearing liquidity at DSK. The cost problem therefore sits alongside balance-sheet room to act ([OTP Group 1H-2026 results conference call, 05/08/2026](https://www.otpgroup.info/static/sw/file/2026_2Q_conference_call_final.pdf)).

The assisted self-service layer is close to empty. Exactly one site in 777 has a kiosk device, and 129 have a twenty-four-hour self-service zone. The estate held 952 ATMs at 30 June 2026 against 271 branches ([OTP Group 1H-2026 results conference call, 05/08/2026](https://www.otpgroup.info/static/sw/file/2026_2Q_conference_call_final.pdf)).

Coin deposit at DSK is one hundred per cent manual at the counter. It is pre-sorted by denomination and explicitly left out of the ATM deposit campaign. The central bank has meanwhile procured EUR 115,480,000 of euro coin blanks, split across two mints, with bids closed on 3 August 2026 ([TED 449605-2026 — BNB euro coin blanks](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/449605-2026/xml)).

The card software layer is closed. BPC's SmartVista is the entrenched card switch and ATM driving platform, and it completed the lev-to-euro migration of 2.6m debit and 300k credit card accounts. Printec can therefore address hardware, cash automation and services rather than card processing ([OTP Group 1H-2026 results conference call, 05/08/2026](https://www.otpgroup.info/static/sw/file/2026_2Q_conference_call_final.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
Rising information-technology cost at DSK is now on the record from the bank's own parent, rather than estimated from outside. It came in the same disclosure as the balance-sheet room to act on it. It also came alongside a hiring wave of 38 technology roles ([OTP Group 1H-2026 results conference call, 05/08/2026](https://www.otpgroup.info/static/sw/file/2026_2Q_conference_call_final.pdf)).

Wage inflation and lost foreign-exchange income are the cost structure that makes handling cash at the branch counter unaffordable. The two things the bank has not built are a kiosk layer and coin automation. These are the two cheapest ways to take work off that counter.

The coin side has just been sized independently by the central bank's EUR 115m coin-blank programme. That programme puts a growing number of coins into circulation, in a system that still handles them by hand ([TED 449605-2026 — BNB euro coin blanks](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/449605-2026/xml)).
cite_ungrounded: That the released EUR 2bn of liquidity is available for technology capital spending is an inference; OTP describes it as a balance-sheet effect, not an investment budget.
"Between roughly 510 and 620 DSK sites are cash-out-only" is a range the locator supports because two different deposit tags are used; the bank publishes no deposit-capability split.
Calling the kiosk layer the lowest-competition entry point is a judgement drawn from the absence of any deployed devices, not from evidence that no supplier has been chosen.
The euro coin-blank award had not been published as at 27/08/2026, and the coin blanks themselves are outside Printec's lines — only the downstream counting and sorting demand is addressable.

outlooks.scope: Bulgaria's Verification of Payee rules include ATMs as an initiation channel
outlooks.summary:
From 1 January 2027, every payment service provider licensed in Bulgaria must offer instant euro credit transfers in both directions. It must also offer Verification of Payee, a check that the name on a transfer matches the account it is going to.

The legal basis is settled. Article 16(9) of Regulation (EU) No 260/2012, inserted by the Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886, requires compliance within one year of euro introduction. Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026 ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Official Journal text](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

Recital 11 matters most for the device estate. It names the initiation channels expressly: online banking, a mobile application, an automated teller machine, a self-service terminal, in a branch or by phone. It requires no difference between instant and other credit transfers across those channels.

Any Bulgarian bank that scoped this work to online and mobile only therefore has a gap on its machines, with four months left to close it. The commercial opportunity is name-matching built into multivendor ATM software and bank kiosks. It also covers sanctions screening at instant speed, real-time monitoring and key-management capacity for round-the-clock volumes.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth is likely, and the work has to fit into four months. The duty is directly applicable European law, not a regulator's interpretation. The Bulgarian National Bank's own SEPA questions-and-answers page was re-read on 27 August 2026. It gives the same 1 January 2027 date for both instant euro sending and Verification of Payee at every provider licensed in Bulgaria ([Bulgarian National Bank — SEPA FAQ](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/AUFAQ/CONTR_SEPA_FAQ)).

Bulgarian law supports the channel point from the other direction. The changeover act defines a Bulgarian ATM as a device that also carries out transfers between payment accounts ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Official Journal text](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

Alongside the payee check, Article 5d requires screening of users against sanctions lists at least once every calendar day. This is the least noticed and most demanding part of the package in day-to-day operations. It means re-screening the entire customer book daily, rather than only at the moment of payment.

Two live reference points already exist, and they are not prospects. UBB went live with Verification of Payee on 15 July 2026, with four match outcomes and round-the-clock operation, citing the same 1 January 2027 market duty. BORICA's service has run since October 2025. The European Payments Council certifies it as a Qualified Routing and Verification Mechanism.

A second wave follows, with its own dates. At an event on 9 July 2026, BORICA set out a centralised national fraud-prevention model built with the Portuguese processor SIBS. The national concept and rules are to be agreed by the end of 2026. Market implementation starts in 2027. The stack already runs a pre-transaction risk platform built on IBM Safer Payments ([BORICA — PSD3 and PSR pose new challenges for the financial sector, 09/07/2026](https://www.borica.bg/latest/novini/evropeyskite-regulatsii-psd3-psr-postavyat-novi-predizvikatelstva-pred-finansoviya-sektor)).

The scheme core is closed, but every Bulgarian bank has to connect to that model during 2027. That work is bank-side connectivity, channel-level fraud and transaction monitoring, case management and testing. Banks buy it one by one rather than through the scheme. BORICA is a private company owned by the banks and buys commercially, so none of this will ever appear as a public procurement notice.

Approach the Bulgarian banks other than UBB. The topics are the payee check in transfer initiation at the machine and the kiosk, daily sanctions re-screening at instant speed, and the 2027 connection to the national fraud model. Banks will fund the work using the local loss figures BORICA itself published. Those figures are about EUR 7.9m of Bulgarian credit-transfer fraud, roughly 70% of national losses, and EUR 13m of account-number-substitution fraud in 2025.

In short: work that was not funded in the first half of 2026 now prices as late-stage remediation. Lead with the channel gap on the machines, which is the part most programmes have not scoped.
drivers: The legal basis was checked against the Official Journal text on 27 August 2026. Article 16(9) of Regulation (EU) No 260/2012, inserted by the Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886, requires compliance within one year of euro introduction. Bulgaria's duty therefore starts on 1 January 2027. The 9 January 2027 date for non-euro countries does not apply here ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Official Journal text](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

Recital 11 of the same regulation names the initiation channels expressly: online banking, a mobile application, an automated teller machine, a self-service terminal, in a branch or by phone. It requires no difference between instant and other credit transfers across them. That puts the ATM and kiosk estate inside scope through the primary text, not through inference ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Official Journal text](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

The Bulgarian National Bank's own SEPA questions-and-answers page gives the same 1 January 2027 date. It applies to both instant euro sending and Verification of Payee at every provider licensed in Bulgaria ([Bulgarian National Bank — SEPA FAQ](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/AUFAQ/CONTR_SEPA_FAQ)).

Article 5d separately requires screening of users against sanctions lists at least once every calendar day. That is a daily re-screen of the whole customer book, not a check at payment time ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Official Journal text](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

A second dated wave follows straight after. BORICA set out on 9 July 2026 a centralised national fraud-prevention model built with SIBS. National rules are to be agreed by end-2026, with market implementation from 2027. BORICA is owned by the banks and buys commercially. This work will never appear as a public notice ([BORICA — PSD3 and PSR pose new challenges for the financial sector, 09/07/2026](https://www.borica.bg/latest/novini/evropeyskite-regulatsii-psd3-psr-postavyat-novi-predizvikatelstva-pred-finansoviya-sektor)).
outlooks.rationale:
This cycle settled the Verification of Payee position, and it changed who owns the work. Reading the Official Journal text confirmed that the deadline is 1 January 2027, not the 9 January 2027 date for non-euro countries. Recital 11 places automated teller machines and self-service terminals inside the scope of the payee check as a matter of primary European law ([Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Official Journal text](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R0886)).

That moves Verification of Payee out of the payments department and onto the device estate, with four months to run. A bank whose programme covered only online and mobile now has a scope gap it has not budgeted for.

UBB went live on 15 July 2026, which removes the argument that the date cannot be met. At every other bank, that turns a compliance discussion into a procurement one ([Bulgarian National Bank — SEPA FAQ](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/AUFAQ/CONTR_SEPA_FAQ)).
cite_ungrounded: No European Payments Council scheme or rulebook dates are used in this outlook. Any 2026 Verification-of-Payee rulebook cut-over date circulating in briefing material is UNVERIFIED — the EPC site returned a Cloudflare block to every route attempted this cycle — and must not be put in a client paper.
Which Bulgarian providers other than UBB have or have not completed Verification-of-Payee work is not established anywhere in the evidence; naming target banks is Printec's own account selection.
"Four months" is arithmetic from 31/08/2026 to the 01/01/2027 obligation.
That unfunded work now prices as late-stage remediation is a commercial judgement, not a documented market price.

Validator correction: the Article 5d daily sanctions-screening duty carried its own deadline of 09/01/2025 for all PSPs and is NOT part of the 01/01/2027 Art.16(9) package — the outlook's placement of it inside the 2027 package overstates the cited evidence.

outlooks.scope: Roughly 1,900 Bulgarian ATM sites are still dispense-only
outlooks.summary:
Each of Bulgaria's four largest banks had its live locator feed re-pulled on the same day, 27 August 2026. Between roughly 1,840 and 1,950 ATM sites across them are dispense-only. These are machines that give cash out but take none in ([UBB branch and ATM locator feed](https://ubb.bg/en/locations/pins/desktop:1?type=atms)).

The national fleet has fallen to 5,031 machines from a 5,751 peak in 2016. ATM deposits meanwhile rose to 12.53m transactions worth EUR 7.2bn across 2025, up 50% by value. Over-the-counter branch deposits jumped 70% by volume to 9.7m transactions worth EUR 16.4bn in the second half of 2025. So fewer machines are doing far more deposit work, and a large remainder still crosses the counter.

Two details show that the decision window is still open. Postbank is adding new machines that are still dispense-only. UniCredit Bulbank has named "ATM obsolescence" as a risk driver in its own annual report.

The opportunity is replacement with recycler-class machines, which are ATMs that re-use deposited notes, together with deposit-capable upgrades. Size the work on sites rather than terminals, until each bank confirms how many machines sit on a site.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth is likely, and the evidence is unusually solid, because it comes from the banks' own published feeds rather than from claims. All figures below come from the synchronised pull of 27 August 2026 ([UBB branch and ATM locator feed](https://ubb.bg/en/locations/pins/desktop:1?type=atms)).

UBB shows 737 ATM pins, of which 244 can take cash deposits, so 493 are dispense-only. That is flat against 30 July. Postbank shows 501 ATM-tagged sites with 226 deposit-capable, so 275 are dispense-only. Its estate grew by three sites in four weeks while the deposit-capable share did not move, which is the strongest available evidence that no recycler decision has been taken.

DSK shows 724 sites with ATMs, but only 214 carry either deposit tag. So between roughly 510 and 620 sites take no cash in, and in 169 of 285 localities not one site accepts a deposit. UniCredit Bulbank shows 761 ATM records with only 197 deposit-capable, so 564 machines are cash-out only. That is 74.1% of its estate.

Three bank-specific hooks sit on top of the total. UniCredit Bulbank's 2025 annual report names "ICT and ICT Security Risks — ATM obsolescence" as a non-financial risk driver to focus on in 2026. Its conversion of branches to cashless is running at about one branch a month, with 32 of 162 branch records converted and 130 still to go. Roughly 443 of its machines sit off-site at retail hosts, where the current supplier's hold is usually weakest.

Two limits apply to that account. The Bulgarian share of the group renewal is not disclosed, so no unit number and no euro band may be quoted. Its 2025 euro programme also states that ATM and point-of-sale upgrade work was already contracted to a vendor it does not name ([UniCredit Bulbank 2025 Annual Report](https://www.unicreditbulbank.bg/media/filer_public/00/18/00187e6b-6f5f-45e9-a40f-9e9160680f20/ucb_ar2026_en_all_a4_am_long.pdf)).

Postbank has published its own device requirement. It covers two Express Banking types: a cash device that withdraws, deposits and performs cashless operations, and a cashless kiosk for statements, transfers, utility bills and municipal taxes. Postbank lists expansion of the office network among its coming initiatives. It also has 137 sites with round-the-clock self-service zones that need no building work ([Postbank — 35th-anniversary rebrand and repositioning](https://www.postbank.bg/za-nas/novini/s-obnovena-vizualna-identichnost-i-novo-pozicionirane-na-postbank/)).

The sector's budget freeze has also lifted. The Bulgarian National Bank governor declared the technical euro changeover complete on 21 August 2026. That releases information-technology and cash budgets into the 2027 planning round, which is being set between September and November 2026.

Three concrete pieces of paid work come with it.
- A screen and receipt reversion release, now that the duty to show both currencies on ATM screens fell away on 9 August 2026.
- Retirement of lev validator profiles, once the exchange duty ends on 31 December 2026.
- A single-currency re-baselining of cash forecasting and routing, on a fleet that has never run a full euro year ([evroto.bg — BNB Governor Radev, seven-month assessment](https://evroto.bg/bg/news/464-dimitar-radev-upravitel-na-bnb-evroto-e-ramka-stabilnostta-e-izbor-)).

Approach Postbank first. It is the one Bulgarian bank expanding rather than shrinking its physical network, and it has published the two-device specification itself. Then take DSK's estate outside branches, which is the single largest gap in the country. Then take UniCredit Bulbank's 130 unconverted branch records and its off-site machines at retail hosts.

In short: size every proposal on sites rather than terminals, because DSK alone has at least 228 machines its locator cannot see. Lead with the cost of the EUR 16.4bn a half-year that still crosses branch counters.
drivers: All four big-bank locator feeds were independently re-pulled on the same day, 27 August 2026. Together they show between roughly 1,840 and 1,950 dispense-only ATM sites. UniCredit Bulbank alone has 564 cash-out-only machines, which is 74.1% of its estate ([UBB branch and ATM locator feed](https://ubb.bg/en/locations/pins/desktop:1?type=atms)).

Central-bank payment statistics were updated on 22 July 2026. They show the national fleet falling to 5,031 ATMs at end-2025, from a 5,751 peak in 2016. ATM deposits meanwhile rose to 12.53m transactions worth EUR 7.2bn across 2025, up 50% by value ([UBB branch and ATM locator feed](https://ubb.bg/en/locations/pins/desktop:1?type=atms)).

Over-the-counter branch deposits jumped 70% by volume to 9.7m transactions worth EUR 16.4bn in the second half of 2025. That is the cost the machine estate is not yet taking on ([UBB branch and ATM locator feed](https://ubb.bg/en/locations/pins/desktop:1?type=atms)).

Postbank is still adding dispense-only machines. It has also published a two-device Express Banking specification and names network expansion among its coming initiatives. It has 137 sites that already carry round-the-clock self-service zones ([Postbank — 35th-anniversary rebrand and repositioning](https://www.postbank.bg/za-nas/novini/s-obnovena-vizualna-identichnost-i-novo-pozicionirane-na-postbank/)).

UniCredit Bulbank names "ATM obsolescence" as a risk driver in its 2025 annual report. It is converting branches to cashless service at about one a month, with 32 of 162 done and 130 to go. Roughly 443 of its machines sit off-site at retail hosts ([UniCredit Bulbank 2025 Annual Report](https://www.unicreditbulbank.bg/media/filer_public/00/18/00187e6b-6f5f-45e9-a40f-9e9160680f20/ucb_ar2026_en_all_a4_am_long.pdf)).

The changeover budget freeze has lifted. The central bank governor declared the technical transition complete on 21 August 2026. That releases bank information-technology and cash budgets into the 2027 planning round now being set ([evroto.bg — BNB Governor Radev, seven-month assessment](https://evroto.bg/bg/news/464-dimitar-radev-upravitel-na-bnb-evroto-e-ramka-stabilnostta-e-izbor-)).
outlooks.rationale:
The gap was re-measured on a single synchronised date, rather than assembled from figures of different ages. It barely moved in a month, and that is the important point.

Postbank added ATM sites in those four weeks without changing its deposit-capable share. New machines are therefore still going in dispense-only. No recycler decision has been taken at the bank most likely to take one ([UBB branch and ATM locator feed](https://ubb.bg/en/locations/pins/desktop:1?type=atms)).

The changeover budget freeze also lifted on 21 August 2026, and the 2027 planning round is being set between September and November. The question is being asked in the one quarter when the answer can still be shaped ([evroto.bg — BNB Governor Radev, seven-month assessment](https://evroto.bg/bg/news/464-dimitar-radev-upravitel-na-bnb-evroto-e-ramka-stabilnostta-e-izbor-)).
cite_ungrounded: Locator pins are locations, not terminals: OTP's own report puts DSK at 952 ATMs against 724 ATM-bearing sites, so every site-based count here understates machine numbers by an unknown margin at all four banks.

The Bulgarian share of UniCredit's group ATM renewal to 2027 is undisclosed, so no unit volume and no euro value may be attached to it, and the "ATM obsolescence" flag may be monitoring rather than funded remediation.

Whether the roughly 443 UniCredit off-site retail-host machines are contractually open is unknown — the bank states that ATM and point-of-sale upgrade work for the 2025 euro programme was already contracted, to a vendor it does not name.
The 1,840-to-1,950 range is a sum of four independently derived site counts using each bank's own deposit tagging, and the tagging conventions differ between banks.

outlooks.scope: Raiffeisen and Garanti BBVA Romania merger, expected October 2026
outlooks.summary:
Raiffeisen Bank International expects to close its purchase of Garanti BBVA Romania in early October 2026, creating the country's third-largest bank. It is the largest Romanian channel event with a fixed date. Data migration and rebranding run across 2027, with a one-off integration budget of about EUR 70m. That is already paid for by a EUR 600m eurobond raised on 20/08/2026 ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

Two self-service estates, two card portfolios and two acquiring books must now become one. Acquiring books are merchant card-payment businesses. A fresh pull of Raiffeisen's own machine locator feed shows that 617 of its 1,151 machines still cannot take a deposit. The bank is also live on only one feature of the national RoPay scheme ([RoPay participant register](https://www.ropay.ro/institutii-participante/)).

Printec should aim at the decisions on the merged estate. These are taken between RBI group procurement in Vienna and the Bucharest integration office. Printec needs to be inside the scoping before RBI's quiet period starts on 23/10/2026.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, driven by a deadline rather than a trend. RBI's own half-year materials put the closing in early October 2026. Data migration and rebranding run across 2027. The legal merger comes in the fourth quarter of 2027, and savings start from 2028.

The purchase price is EUR 591m, with a one-off integration cost of about EUR 70m, mostly in 2027. Garanti adds roughly EUR 4.3bn of assets to Raiffeisen's EUR 17.5bn, and about 200,000 active customers ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

RBI says integration planning is already under way, and the funding is committed rather than forecast. Raiffeisen Bank Romania raised EUR 600m in a 6.4-year eurobond at 4.626% on 20/08/2026, with orders above EUR 1.3bn. A further EUR 400-600m of Romanian bond issuance is flagged for 2027.

In practice, that money pays for a lot of work. Every acquired machine gets a new fascia, new keys and new certification. Two self-service estates merge onto one switch and one monitoring system, and two card portfolios are re-issued. Two acquiring books and terminal-management systems are combined, and two anti-money-laundering and transaction-monitoring systems become one.

The estate being merged has just been re-counted. A cleaner pull of Raiffeisen's locator on 27/08/2026 returns 2,069 network points. Once 595 Euronet-branded devices are taken out, the bank's own fleet is 1,151 machines. Only 534 of these list cash deposit as a service, and 69 carry the multifunctional name but list no deposit service at all (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

On card acceptance, the book grew from over 42,000 point-of-sale terminals at 31/03/2026 to nearly 45,000 at 30/06/2026. Over the same period the bank stayed live on one RoPay feature, phone-number Alias payment, while six banks are live on eleven ([RoPay participant register](https://www.ropay.ro/institutii-participante/)). Raiffeisen also posted a job for a Product Manager for Cards Issuing and Merchant Acceptance on 31/08/2026, closing 23/09/2026. Card issuing and acquiring are therefore being put under one owner just as the merger lands (findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md).

Who to talk to: RBI group procurement in Vienna and the Bucharest integration office. The topics are multivendor ATM software and re-certification across two mixed fleets. They also include terminal management and remote key injection for the combined acquiring book. Deposit-capable machines are needed for the 617 cash-out-only sites. Last is the keep-or-replace decision on Garanti's remote onboarding system.

That onboarding system uses a selfie, a chip read of the Romanian electronic identity card and a liveness test. It has been live since 14/04/2026, and no technology vendor has ever been named publicly. Garanti also brings the national land-registry card-processing framework, 473 contracts worth RON 6.4m, into the merged acquiring business (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).

In short: treat the weeks to 23/10/2026 as the scoping window. Fold every Romanian proposal into the EUR 70m integration budget rather than selling it on its own.
drivers: Closing is expected in early October 2026. Data migration and rebranding run across 2027, with the legal merger in Q4/2027. The one-off integration cost is about EUR 70m, mostly in 2027, against roughly EUR 90m of extra profit in 2028 ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

The integration is already funded. Raiffeisen Bank Romania raised EUR 600m in a 6.4-year eurobond at 4.626% on 20/08/2026, with orders above EUR 1.3bn. RBI has flagged a further EUR 400-600m of Romanian bond issuance in 2027 (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

A cleaner locator pull on 27/08/2026 puts Raiffeisen's own fleet at 1,151 machines, not the 1,211 counted before. Of these, 617 (54%) cannot take a deposit, and 69 are labelled multifunctional but list no deposit service (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Card acceptance and issuing are being put under one owner as the merger lands. The terminal book grew from over 42,000 to nearly 45,000 in a single quarter, while the bank stayed live on one RoPay feature ([RoPay participant register](https://www.ropay.ro/institutii-participante/)).

Garanti already runs its own chip-based remote onboarding, which means signing up new customers remotely. It launched on 14/04/2026 using the Romanian electronic identity card, with no technology vendor named. The keep-or-replace decision therefore falls inside the 2027 scope, with no publicly known supplier to displace (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).
outlooks.rationale:
Within three weeks, the deal moved from approval to action, and the budget moved from plan to balance sheet. RBI put the closing in early October 2026 and said integration planning had already started. The EUR 600m pre-funding was priced on 20/08/2026 ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

The decisions that matter for sales are being scoped before the closing, not after it. These are whose software drives the merged fleet, whose terminal-management platform survives, and whose monitoring system is kept. The window has a hard end, because RBI holds no investor or analyst contact from 23/10/2026.

The estate itself was re-counted from the bank's own locator feed on 27/08/2026. For the first time, the merged estate can therefore be argued machine by machine rather than from a slide deck (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).
cite_ungrounded: The 23/10/2026 date is sourced as the start of RBI's investor and analyst quiet period; treating it as a practical cut-off for commercial scoping conversations is our inference, not a stated RBI policy.

The list of integration workstreams (single switch, single monitoring stack, consolidated terminal management, merged monitoring and screening) is derived from the disclosed 'data migration and rebranding' scope. RBI has not published a technical integration plan and no vendor decisions are disclosed.
That Garanti's onboarding stack is a genuine keep-or-replace decision follows from no vendor being named publicly; it is not stated by either bank.

outlooks.scope: Deposit automation on Romania's cash-dispense-only ATM fleets
outlooks.summary:
Within two weeks, four Romanian banks either published new figures or had their own machine feeds re-counted. The figures point the same way: bank counters are closing faster than machines are being upgraded.

BCR now runs 1,100 cash-dispense-only ATMs out of 1,668 devices, and 211 of its 282 branches already have no tellers ([BCR locator API](https://www.bcr.ro/bin/erstegroup/gemesgapi/locations/gem_site_location_locations-ro-bcr?types=MFM&items=9000&page=0)). UniCredit has 1,093 machines that cannot take cash in, after cutting 19 branches in six months ([UniCredit half-year report 30/06/2026](https://www.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/UCB27_20260825154550_HALF-YEAR-REPORT-30-06-2026-IN-ACCORDANCE-WITH-FSA-REGULATIO.pdf)). BRD shows about 946 cash-out-only self-service sites, against only eleven cashless agencies. Banca Transilvania reports roughly 1,300 cash-out-only machines ([Banca Transilvania H1-2026 filing](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TLV_20260821153439_Financial-results-30-06-2026.pdf)).

The direction is growth, but the work is converting existing machines, not building new estates. It has to be priced as opex, meaning a running cost, not as a capital purchase. Printec should aim at named, finite pools of machines to convert, bank by bank, with multivendor ATM software as the way in.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, mainly in deposit automation and in the software that runs mixed fleets. The pools of machines are now counted, not estimated.

BCR's own locator was re-pulled on 27/08/2026. It returns 1,100 cash-dispense-only ATMs, 568 multifunctional machines and 282 branch records. Every multifunctional machine accepts cash in, and not one of the 1,100 does. 211 of the 282 branches have no staffed cash desk, and only 66 accept business cash at a machine, in lei only ([BCR locator API](https://www.bcr.ro/bin/erstegroup/gemesgapi/locations/gem_site_location_locations-ro-bcr?types=MFM&items=9000&page=0)).

UniCredit filed its half-year report on 25/08/2026. It shows 246 branches against 265 at the year-end, with 35 retail units closed in six months. That is the steepest fall in its Central and Eastern European division. Its estate is flat at 1,207 ATM records, of which only 114 can take any cash deposit. 27 branches are already flagged as running with no cash at the counter ([UniCredit half-year report 30/06/2026](https://www.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/UCB27_20260825154550_HALF-YEAR-REPORT-30-06-2026-IN-ACCORDANCE-WITH-FSA-REGULATIO.pdf)).

BRD's locator pull of 27/08/2026 gives about 1,233 separate self-service sites, of which roughly 946 are cash-out-only. Its own data feed classes 322 of 335 agencies as staffed cash agencies, against eleven cashless ones. That is a model the bank built and never scaled up. Meanwhile active staff fell to 4,641 from 4,965 in six months (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Banca Transilvania's interim report of 21/08/2026 gives over 2,000 ATMs, of which 691 are multifunctional, plus 616 BT Express terminals. Roughly 1,300 machines are therefore cash-out-only. The board-approved 2026 budget lines that can actually be quoted are machines RON 21.39m, security RON 9.79m and cash processing centre RON 7.88m ([Banca Transilvania H1-2026 filing](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TLV_20260821153439_Financial-results-30-06-2026.pdf)).

A second, market-wide trigger is moving at the same time. Draft law B409/2026 would require every ATM operator in Romania to accept any withdrawal amount the customer chooses. It rules out preset fast-cash buttons, and gives 90 days from entry into force to comply. It has cleared all four advisory opinions, with none opposing. The National Bank did not oppose it on 17/08/2026, and asked for the banks to be consulted on the technical characteristics of terminals. The Competition Council cleared it on 18/08/2026 ([Senat file and text, B409/2026](https://www.senat.ro/legis/lista.aspx?nr_cls=b409&an_cls=2026)).

No bank can specify, build, test and re-certify one screen flow across mixed hardware in 90 days from a standing start. Free-amount entry also changes the mix of notes a machine pays out. That brings in cash forecasting and denomination optimisation, which means planning which notes to load.

Who to talk to: BCR through Erste group procurement and Erste Digital rather than Bucharest, since BCR has posted no Romanian technology vacancies for three months. Use UniCredit's 27 already-cashless branches as the reference design for the rest. Present BRD's eleven-site cashless model as a scale-up rather than a new idea, sold as a managed service, because BRD is funding software and not machines. At Banca Transilvania, work only the board-approved machines, security and cash-processing lines, plus the regulated infrastructure, because front-end digital work has been taken in-house.

In short: sell the conversion of named, finite dispense-only pools on a cost-per-transaction and lease basis. Use multivendor software and the free-amount screen change as the way in.
drivers: BCR's locator was independently re-pulled on 27/08/2026. It shows 1,100 cash-dispense-only ATMs against 568 multifunctional. 211 of 282 branches already have no staffed cash desk, and only 66 accept business cash at a machine ([BCR locator API](https://www.bcr.ro/bin/erstegroup/gemesgapi/locations/gem_site_location_locations-ro-bcr?types=MFM&items=9000&page=0)).

UniCredit's half-year report, filed 25/08/2026, shows 246 branches against 265 at 31/12/2025. 1,093 of its 1,207 ATM records cannot take cash in, and 27 branches are already flagged as running without a cash desk ([UniCredit half-year report 30/06/2026](https://www.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/UCB27_20260825154550_HALF-YEAR-REPORT-30-06-2026-IN-ACCORDANCE-WITH-FSA-REGULATIO.pdf)).

BRD's own feed gives about 946 cash-out-only self-service sites. It classes 322 of 335 agencies as staffed cash agencies, against eleven cashless. Staff numbers fell 1.7 times faster than branches, and capital spending went overwhelmingly to software (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Banca Transilvania's interim report of 21/08/2026 shows over 2,000 ATMs, with 691 multifunctional and 616 BT Express units. The fleet is flat to shrinking, while transaction volume is up more than 17%. The board-approved hardware-related budget lines total about RON 39m ([Banca Transilvania H1-2026 filing](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TLV_20260821153439_Financial-results-30-06-2026.pdf)).

Draft law B409/2026 would force a free-amount withdrawal screen onto every ATM in the market within 90 days of entry into force. It has now cleared every advisory opinion, and the central bank has asked for a technical consultation with the industry ([Senat file and text, B409/2026](https://www.senat.ro/legis/lista.aspx?nr_cls=b409&an_cls=2026)).
outlooks.rationale:
The measurement changed, and with it the sales argument. In the two weeks to 27/08/2026, all four large Romanian retail fleets were re-counted from the banks' own locator feeds and interim reports. The deposit gap can now be argued site by site instead of just claimed.

Every one of those banks is removing counters and staff faster than it is converting machines. That forces cash deposits onto self-service machines the banks have not yet built.

The commercial structure is also decided for us, not by us. A revenue-based turnover tax lifted UniCredit's operating expenses 39.9%, and BCR's banking levy has doubled. Large possible competition fines are carried across the sector with no provisions set aside. Romanian buying through 2026-27 therefore leans towards leases, managed services and payback arguments rather than capital purchases (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).
cite_ungrounded: The four fleets are counted on four different bases — locator records, distinct sites and disclosed devices — so any single national total of Romanian cash-out-only machines is our own aggregation and must not be quoted as a published figure.
B409/2026 was still in first chamber with no committee report and no scheduled vote as at 27/08/2026, so the 90-day compliance clock is contingent on a vote that has not happened.
Banca Transilvania's filings say 'multifunctional', never 'recycling', so nothing here should be read as BT already operating recyclers.
Printec's historic BCR foothold traces only to a 2018-dated vendor page and is not re-verified; it must not be briefed as current incumbency.

outlooks.scope: Public-sector cash and card collection moving to self-service in Romania
outlooks.summary:
Romania's public sector is moving counter cash and card collection onto self-service machines, and CEC Bank has become the channel.

On 24/08/2026 CEC was named winner of the National Lottery electronic-transaction contract. That is its ninth verified public acquiring win in four months, and roughly RON 30.7m of contracted acquiring. Acquiring means card-payment processing. CEC also won a 48-month treasury cashier-services framework worth RON 4,457,700, which hands a state cash desk to a bank ([TED 564413-2026 — DGRFP Ploiesti cashier services](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/564413-2026/pdf)).

CEC also opened its deposit fleet to every Romanian debit cardholder with Cash2Card on 04/08/2026 ([CEC Bank — Cash2Card launch](https://www.cec.ro/presa/cec-bank-lanseaza-serviciul-cash2card-numerarul-poate-fi-depus-direct-pe-cardurile-de-debit)). It has published a plan to redesign roughly 350 branches around autonomous, self-service equipment. Printec should aim at CEC as an acquiring and cash-in account, and at the municipal self-service frameworks that are still failing to attract valid bids.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, and unusually well documented, because most of it goes through public procurement.

On the card-acceptance side, the routing has changed. A contract-by-contract check puts CEC Bank, not Banca Transilvania, as Romania's most-awarded public-sector card acquirer. It has nine award notices totalling about RON 30.7m in four months. These cover regional tax directorates in Bucharest, Iasi, Brasov and Ploiesti, the National Trade Register Office, Bucharest Sector 6 and Municipiul Bacau. They also cover Posta Romana online card processing at RON 10.76m and the National Lottery at RON 3.76m on 24/08/2026. A further 22 award notices named CEC between 01/05 and 24/08/2026 (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).

Printec cannot bid for these contracts, because only a licensed acquiring bank can. The pool is therefore sold through the winning acquirers, on terminal supply, terminal management, remote key injection and softPOS, which is card acceptance on a phone.

The state is also closing its own treasury cash desks and buying the counter service from banks. A 48-month cashier framework was awarded to CEC at RON 4,457,700 ([TED 564413-2026 — DGRFP Ploiesti cashier services](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/564413-2026/pdf)). Every treasury office handed over becomes a branch taking in extra public cash, which is the argument for teller cash recyclers.

On the cash-in side, CEC launched Cash2Card on 04/08/2026. It lets anyone, including non-customers, deposit cash straight onto any Visa or Mastercard debit card issued by any Romanian bank, free and around the clock. CEC describes the fleet as more than 270 last-generation multifunctional machines ([CEC Bank — Cash2Card launch](https://www.cec.ro/presa/cec-bank-lanseaza-serviciul-cash2card-numerarul-poate-fi-depus-direct-pe-cardurile-de-debit)). An independent locator count of 27/08/2026 returns 1,244 ATM and 256 multifunctional locations, so roughly 83% of the estate is still cash-out-only.

Behind that sits the bank's own published Operational Model Redesign Program, covering about 350 rural and urban branches. Today only 46 of 1,011 units run a 24/7 self-service zone, and just five new zones were built in the whole of 2025 (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Municipalities are the third strand, and the only one Printec can bid for directly. Municipiul Arad's framework for collecting local taxes through self-service stations is estimated at RON 1,536,964. Its deadline has been pushed back twice and it closes 10/09/2026 ([TED 584205-2026 — Arad corrigendum](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/584205-2026/pdf)). Municipiul Onesti's RON 800,540 procedure has sat unawarded more than three months past its 25/05/2026 deadline. Twice-extended deadlines and an overdue award show the market is not producing valid bids.

A fourth strand is small but unclaimed: the State Treasury's own note-counting machines, repaired job by job by very small vendors. There were fourteen below-threshold direct awards in three weeks at Cluj-Napoca totalling RON 25,463.94. At Craiova there were five county frameworks worth RON 449,628, or RON 649,228 including three further contracts under the same scheme. There is no national service framework holder at all (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).

Who to talk to: CEC Bank directly, as the single highest-value Romanian acquiring prospect visible from public data and, at the same time, the largest cash-in conversion opportunity. Also the Arad framework before 10/09/2026, then Onesti. And the tax administration, for a single national managed-service framework covering the treasury counting-machine fleet.

In short: offer a financed, standard roll-out package with service, never a hardware purchase. CEC put over 92% of 2025 investment into IT, while branch works-and-equipment capital spending fell from RON 21.5m to RON 8.8m.
drivers: CEC Bank was named winner of the National Lottery electronic-transaction contract on 24/08/2026. That is its ninth verified public acquiring win in four months and about RON 30.7m of contracted acquiring. A further 22 award notices have named it since 01/05/2026 (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).

The Romanian state is handing its own treasury counters to banks. A 48-month cashier-services framework was awarded to CEC Bank at RON 4,457,700 ([TED 564413-2026 — DGRFP Ploiesti cashier services](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/564413-2026/pdf)).

Cash2Card, launched 04/08/2026, turns CEC's deposit fleet into national infrastructure by accepting deposits onto any Romanian bank's debit card. That pushes the economics towards true recycling, meaning re-using deposited notes, rather than deposit-only machines ([CEC Bank — Cash2Card launch](https://www.cec.ro/presa/cec-bank-lanseaza-serviciul-cash2card-numerarul-poate-fi-depus-direct-pe-cardurile-de-debit)).

CEC's own audited report names an Operational Model Redesign Program covering roughly 350 branches. Today only 46 of 1,011 units have a 24/7 zone, and the 2025 build rate was five zones a year (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Municipal self-service collection can be bid for directly and is short of suppliers. Arad's RON 1,536,964 framework closes 10/09/2026 after two extensions ([TED 584205-2026 — Arad corrigendum](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/584205-2026/pdf)). Onesti's RON 800,540 procedure is more than three months overdue for award.

The State Treasury's note-counting machines have no national framework holder and are repaired job by job. There were fourteen direct awards in three weeks at Cluj-Napoca totalling RON 25,463.94 (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).
outlooks.rationale:
Two things moved in the same month. A contract-by-contract re-check changed the acquiring picture. CEC Bank, not Banca Transilvania, is now the most-awarded public card acquirer, and its ninth win landed on 24/08/2026. That changes who Printec should be talking to about terminals, terminal management and key injection (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).

On 04/08/2026 CEC also opened its own deposit fleet to everyone. That is the argument that finally justifies converting an estate which is still 83% cash-out-only ([CEC Bank — Cash2Card launch](https://www.cec.ro/presa/cec-bank-lanseaza-serviciul-cash2card-numerarul-poate-fi-depus-direct-pe-cardurile-de-debit)).

The municipal frameworks are the part with near dates. Arad closes 10/09/2026 after two extensions, and a neighbouring city's award is three months overdue. That is an opening rather than a warning.
cite_ungrounded: The Cluj-Napoca treasury counting-machine direct awards come from one agent and were flagged by another that could not re-retrieve the notice identifiers, so the count and totals are single-source.
No CEC primary document re-checked this cycle names a core-banking vendor, and the RON 332.98m competition-fine figure previously carried for CEC could not be re-sourced — neither should be repeated.
Reading the twice-extended Arad deadline and the overdue Onesti award as evidence of a shortage of compliant bids is an inference from procedure status, not a statement by either buyer.

outlooks.scope: Hungary's ATM Act and the resulting machine replacement market
outlooks.summary:
Hungary has passed a law that makes replacement, rather than removal, the only option for its cash machines. Act XIV of 2026, in force since 14/05/2026, stops a bank from shutting down any ATM that existed on that date. The same no-closure rule now covers a branch's cash-payout service. Replacing the machine is clearly allowed ([consolidated ATM Act text in force from 14/05/2026](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00)).

Its subsection (1b) even expects that the replacement may not fit the old site, because of its size and security requirements. That is exactly what happens when an old cash dispenser becomes a deposit or recycling machine.

On top of that, 1,039 new rural sites are required by 31/12/2026. They are allocated bank by bank, and the list is now frozen ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.), consolidated text](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)). Locator pulls show 1,029 cash-out-only machines at MBH and about 1,450 more at OTP and Erste. Printec should go to the nine obliged banks directly, because there will never be a tender.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, and unusually well protected from the shrinking-fleet pattern that dominates the rest of the region.

Two agents re-read the consolidated law word for word. From 14/05/2026 a credit institution may no longer shut down any ATM that existed when the amendment came into force. The same rule now covers a branch's cash-payout service. Moving a machine is allowed only in justified cases, and only if a machine keeps running in the same settlement or Budapest district. Breaking the rule carries a supervisory fine of HUF 2m to HUF 200m. Replacing the machine is clearly excluded from the ban ([consolidated ATM Act text in force from 14/05/2026](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00)).

Subsection (1b) goes further. It accepts that a like-for-like swap may be impossible at a site for purely technological or technical reasons. It names the size of the new machine and its security requirements. In that case the replacement may be installed elsewhere in the same settlement. That provision turns a decade of quiet machine removals into a multi-year replacement pipeline.

It also creates two linked sales. The first is a paid site-survey and fit study for machines that will not fit their old spaces. The second is withdrawal-volume telemetry, meaning remote usage data, because a bank now needs volume evidence to justify any move.

Alongside this runs the rural build. Annex 1 of the central bank's decree, read independently by two agents, allocates 80 settlement packages covering 1,039 named settlements to one obliged bank each. The allocation is OTP 428, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste 104, Raiffeisen 65, CIB 52, UniCredit 52, Granit 13 and MagNet 13. All are due 31/12/2026, and all must be barrier-free with no exemption for older accessibility standards. The package-swap deadline of 28/02/2026 has passed, so the map is frozen ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.), consolidated text](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)).

The open space is now measured. MBH's own locator, pulled 27/08/2026, returns 1,285 fixed ATMs, of which only 256 accept cash in. None of the 803 older machines inherited from Takarekbank takes a deposit at all. 525 of 538 branch-type points still run a staffed cash desk. The feed also shows four different quick-withdrawal preset set-ups inside one bank ([MBH branch and ATM locator](https://www.mbhbank.hu/apps/backend/branch-and-atm)).

OTP's half-year report of 05/08/2026 shows 1,929 Hungarian ATMs, 58 fewer than at the year-end. That runs against both the standstill and OTP's own stated duty to install 233 new or moved machines in 2026. Its locator gives 1,220 cash-out-only machines, with 376 sites hosted in municipal or other public buildings ([OTP Bank statutory half-year report 2026](https://www.otpbank.hu/apps05/capital-market/api/getPublicationFile?token=72F1DFA1AEDBB713B47C000000000079F847A02D44BC72F1DFA1AEDB)). Erste Hungary adds 237 more, on a very thin base of 97 branches.

Either the required machines sit outside OTP's reported estate, or a catch-up on compliance is due in the second half of 2026. Both readings are live sales openings. There will be no tender notice to answer. A full sweep of the Hungarian public-procurement register found no ATM supply procedure of any kind in 2026. The nine obliged institutions are private banks, and are not public contracting authorities for this spend.

Who to talk to: MBH first. A new deputy chief executive for standard customer service took office there on 01/08/2026 with a clear automation mandate and is setting a 2027 budget. Its switching layer is known to run on a competitor-owned platform. Then OTP and Erste Hungary on the cash-in gap. Then the smaller obliged banks on their rural packages, where a five-year minimum on hand-over contracts means whoever equips a package holds it for years.

In short: sell the legal replacement cycle as a programme, covering hardware, accessibility package, telemetry and vendor-neutral software. Lock the service and telemetry wrap into the price. Otherwise a brand-independent local workshop will take the yearly service income (findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md).
drivers: Act XIV of 2026 rewrote section 3 of the ATM Act with effect from 14/05/2026. No existing ATM may be taken out of service, and the same no-closure rule now covers a branch's cash-payout point. Replacement is clearly excluded from the ban ([consolidated ATM Act text in force from 14/05/2026](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00)).

Subsection (1b) expects that a replacement may not fit its old site for technological or technical reasons, and names size and security requirements. That is exactly the case of a dispenser being swapped for a deposit or recycling machine (findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md).

1,039 named rural settlements in 80 packages are each allocated to one obliged bank, and are due 31/12/2026, all barrier-free. The swap deadline of 28/02/2026 has passed, so the allocation is frozen ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.), consolidated text](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)).

MBH's locator, pulled 27/08/2026, shows 1,285 fixed ATMs with only 256 accepting cash in. None of the 803 older Takarekbank machines can take a deposit, and 525 of 538 branch points are still staffed ([MBH branch and ATM locator](https://www.mbhbank.hu/apps/backend/branch-and-atm)).

OTP removed 58 Hungarian ATMs in the first half of 2026, despite a standstill in force since 14/05/2026 and its own stated duty to add 233 machines this year. That leaves 1,220 cash-out-only machines at OTP and 237 at Erste ([OTP Bank statutory half-year report 2026](https://www.otpbank.hu/apps05/capital-market/api/getPublicationFile?token=72F1DFA1AEDBB713B47C000000000079F847A02D44BC72F1DFA1AEDB)).

None of this creates a tender. A full sweep of the national procurement register found no ATM supply procedure in 2026, because the obliged institutions are private banks buying bank by bank (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).
outlooks.rationale:
The legal position changed in May, and the estate data caught up in August. Before 14/05/2026 Hungary looked like every other shrinking-fleet market. Since then a bank may not retire a machine but may replace it. The law itself accepts that the replacement may be physically bigger and carry higher security requirements ([consolidated ATM Act text in force from 14/05/2026](https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-18-00-00)).

On 27/08/2026 the two largest cash-in gaps were measured from the banks' own locator feeds for the first time. OTP's half-year report showed the estate moving the wrong way, against a legal deadline four months away. A new channels owner at MBH took office on 01/08/2026, in the middle of a 2027 budget round.

A regional rival has put capital into a Budapest company that has not yet hired anyone. That gives Printec a short head start, not a permanent one (findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md).
cite_ungrounded: The figure of roughly 5,700 machines nationally comes from the signal's own framing of the protected estate; it is not reconciled to a per-bank census and should be presented as an order of magnitude.
The source link is the consolidated ATM Act text as in force from 14/05/2026; the amending instrument is Act XIV of 2026, so the two citations refer to the same law before and after amendment.
Reading subsection (1b) as an invitation to swap dispensers for deeper deposit and recycling machines is our commercial interpretation of a technical provision, not the legislator's stated purpose.
OTP, joined by Erste and Raiffeisen, filed a constitutional complaint against the rural mandate on 10/11/2025 and no decision could be found, so the obligation is live but contested.
Whether OTP's missing mandated machines reflect a shared installation pool or a compliance catch-up is explicitly undetermined in the evidence.

The ~5,700-machine national estate total is not evidenced in any cited finding — the per-bank figures in evidence (MBH 1,285, OTP 1,929, Erste 505) do not sum to it. The protected-refresh mechanism stands on the statute; the national total awaits the MNB's unpublished 2026 Payment Systems Report.
The claim that MBH's new deputy CEO 'is setting a 2027 budget' goes beyond the cited jobs finding, which records only the 01/08/2026 appointment and mandate.

outlooks.scope: Regulatory order requiring K&H to add branch cash capacity
outlooks.summary:
Hungary's central bank has ordered one bank, in a binding decision, to put physical cash-handling capacity back into its branches and to prove queue performance with data. The order fined K&H HUF 60,000,000. From 01/03/2026 it re-imposed three duties.

The bank must add staffed teller positions in named branches. It must extend online appointment booking for cash transactions to every branch with a teller. It must also file monthly waiting-time reports. The March-to-May data was filed on 15/06/2026 and is still being assessed.

At the same time, the owner disclosed on 06/08/2026 that the Hungarian mortgage interest cap no longer has an end date. It booked a EUR 42m loss, which makes cost cutting permanent, on the fastest-shrinking branch network in its international unit ([KBC Group 2Q2026 company presentation](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-company-presentation.pdf)).

Printec should aim at teller cash recyclers, plus queue and appointment analytics good enough to show a supervisor. It should bring the bank's 117 required rural sites into the same conversation.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, from an unusually specific trigger: the supervisor has set out what the bank must provide.

Decision H-KPL-I-4/2025 of 17/12/2025 fined K&H HUF 60,000,000, the largest cash-area fine in the Hungarian group of banks. From 01/03/2026 it re-imposed three duties. The first is to add staffed teller positions in named branches. The second is to extend online appointment booking for cash transactions to every branch with a teller, including the lunchtime and closing periods. The third is to file a monthly waiting-time report.

The per-branch data for March to May 2026 went to the regulator by 15/06/2026 and is still being assessed (findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md). K&H has already been fined once for missing these same deadlines, so another decision is a real possibility.

The economics push the same way. KBC's second-quarter figures of 06/08/2026 put K&H at 188 branches, down from 189 at 31/03/2026, 191 at the year-end and 193 a year earlier. That is the fastest-shrinking network in its International Markets business unit. Customer numbers are flat at 1.7 million, with EUR 9bn of loans and EUR 12bn of deposits.

K&H booked a EUR 42m lifetime modification loss in the quarter, because the Hungarian mortgage interest-cap law no longer had an end date at 30/06/2026. That came on top of a EUR 134m windfall and deposit-guarantee tax charge in the first quarter ([KBC Group 2Q2026 company presentation](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-company-presentation.pdf)).

The bank is ordered to add cash capacity while its margin is capped with no end date and its branch count falls. Automating the counter is the one way it can meet both demands. K&H is separately allocated 117 of the 1,039 required rural settlements due 31/12/2026 ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.), consolidated text](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)). Its own machine count still cannot be measured from outside, because the bank's website returns an error to automated access. That in itself is an argument for a joint estate audit as the first piece of work.

A third, quieter budget line sits alongside. Hungary's first mandatory cybersecurity audits fell due on 30/06/2026, and the rules have moved from set-up to enforcement. This is where fixes for asset inventory, logging, patching and supplier management land, and it reaches the self-service estate ([SZTFH cybersecurity pages](https://sztfh.hu/kiberbiztonsag/)).

Who to talk to: K&H, about branch cash automation, meaning teller cash recyclers that add capacity without adding staff. Bundle this with queue management, appointment booking and waiting-time analytics whose reports are good enough to file with a supervisor. Put the 117 required rural machines and the audit-fix evidence layer in the same account plan.

In short: this is a compliance-funded branch-automation sale at a named bank. Two supervisory deadlines have already passed, and the assessment is still open.
drivers: Binding decision H-KPL-I-4/2025 of 17/12/2025 fined K&H HUF 60,000,000. From 01/03/2026 it re-imposed duties to add staffed teller positions, extend appointment booking for cash transactions to every branch with a teller, and report waiting times monthly (findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md).

The March-to-May 2026 per-branch waiting-time evidence was filed on 15/06/2026 and is still being assessed by the supervisor. The bank has already been fined once for missing these same deadlines (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

KBC disclosed on 06/08/2026 that K&H is down to 188 branches, the fastest-shrinking network in its International Markets unit. It booked a EUR 42m loss because the Hungarian interest cap no longer has an end date ([KBC Group 2Q2026 company presentation](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-company-presentation.pdf)).

K&H is responsible for 117 of the 1,039 required rural settlements due 31/12/2026. The branch conversation and the legally required build therefore sit in the same budget ([MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.), consolidated text](https://net.jogtar.hu/jogszabaly?docid=a2500019.mnb)).

Hungary's first mandatory cybersecurity audits fell due 30/06/2026 and enforcement has begun. That pushes fixes for asset inventory, logging, patching and supplier management onto the same estates ([SZTFH cybersecurity pages](https://sztfh.hu/kiberbiztonsag/)).
outlooks.rationale:
The two halves of the case landed within two weeks of each other. The supervisory duties are still running, with evidence filed on 15/06/2026 and no assessment published.

Then on 06/08/2026 the owner confirmed that the margin squeeze is permanent, not temporary. It also confirmed that the branch network is being cut faster than anywhere else in its group ([KBC Group 2Q2026 company presentation](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-company-presentation.pdf)).

The bank is ordered to add cash capacity, cannot earn it back on margin, and is shrinking the branches that deliver it. That combination makes automation the only answer that meets the rules, and it has to be budgeted in the round that opens now.
cite_ungrounded: No agent refiled the underlying supervisory decisions this cycle, so the fine amount, the duties and the deadlines are carried forward from an earlier reading rather than re-verified at primary source.
K&H's own ATM and machine count could not be measured — the bank's site refuses automated access — so no estate sizing is available for this account.
No enforcement decision or fine has been located under the Hungarian cybersecurity regime since 30/06/2026, so the remediation wave is expected rather than evidenced, which caps its urgency.
Reading teller cash recyclers as the specific answer to the supervisor's capacity order is our commercial interpretation; the decision names staffing, booking and reporting duties, not equipment.

The MNB decision number H-KPL-I-4/2025 (17/12/2025) and the HUF 60,000,000 fine against K&H appear in NONE of this cycle's findings files. An independent validation pass flagged this outlook as unsupported on that basis. The claim traces only to the previous cycle's disclosure file (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-07-30.md), which itself records the decision as 'partially confirmed'. It is retained as carried context with that provenance stated, and must not be quoted client-facing until re-confirmed at the MNB's own decision register.
The characterisation of the fine as 'the largest cash-area fine in the Hungarian cluster' is a ranking that no cited document supports.

outlooks.scope: Hungarian public unattended self-service: police and BKK procurements
outlooks.summary:
Two Hungarian public buyers are replacing unattended self-service hardware at the same time. In both cases the card-acquiring layer is closed, but the hardware layer is not.

The National Police's two-lot supply tender covers automated border-control gates, self-service kiosks and biometric capture points. It closed on 28/07/2026. No result was published a month later, after five republications since April ([TED 497245-2026 — border kiosk and biometric capture](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/497245-2026/xml)).

Budapest's transport authority is running an open-loop contactless card ticketing programme, which means paying with an ordinary bank card. Its already-signed acceptance contract revealed an estate of 317 ticket machines with built-in unattended terminals. The authority owns these and is already swapping them brand for brand ([TED 424870-2026 — BKK card acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/424870-2026/xml)).

Printec should aim at the kiosk and terminal hardware and its service wrap. The way in is through the ticket-machine subcontractor and the winning acquirers, not through the acquiring notices.
outlooks.projected:
Mixed, because the two halves of this market are moving in opposite directions.

The acquiring half is closing. One payments company took both lots of the State Treasury's card-acceptance framework, at a combined HUF 13,200,000,000 over 36 months. It then took Budapest's transport contract at HUF 1,318,733,639 on 16/06/2026, beating the current bank head to head. The tax administration's own virtual-terminal tender has transaction-history entry rules that in practice limit lead bidders to established Hungarian acquirers (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md). A lead bid is therefore not the route.

The hardware and service half is wide open and unusually well documented. The transport authority's signed acceptance notice sets out the estate. There are 19 sites with 88 terminals in service, plus 317 ticket-vending machines with built-in unattended terminals, of which 286 are from one manufacturer and 31 from another. The authority itself planned to swap these for newer unattended models by the third quarter of 2026. There are also 15 fixed and 350 mobile terminals for on-street penalty collection, and software-based acceptance on around 350 devices ([TED 424870-2026 — BKK card acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/424870-2026/xml)).

Those 317 machines are the authority's own property. They are serviced and terminal-managed by a separate subcontractor, so that estate is bought entirely outside the acquiring contract. That is a live Budapest hardware replacement wave, reachable through the service subcontractor.

Alongside it, the open-loop contactless acquiring and processing procedure was republished on 17/08/2026, moving bids to 08/09/2026. It is a 48-month utilities contract, deliberately not split into lots, with a HUF 10,000,000 bid bond. Its scope includes real-time and near-time fraud prevention and master-data management for the validators and ticket-sales points ([BKK cEMV transaction-processing notice](https://ekr.gov.hu/api/publikus/kozbeszerzesi-hirdetmenyek/8805660980571/dokumentum-letoltes)). That is three layers Printec can address, under a mandate only a licensed acquirer can hold.

The police procurement is the other opening. It is in trouble, and that difficulty is what makes it reachable. Lot 1 covers 75 outdoor biometric face-capture devices plus four options, and 75 managed switches across eleven road border crossings. Lot 2 covers 16 self-service kiosks plus four options, eight automated border-control gates, four switches, four dual-monitor workstations and eight wall-mounted screens across four crossings. The term is nine months per lot, with option deliveries by 30/06/2027.

Only new equipment qualifies, one bidder may take both lots, and fingerprint readers come from the buyer's own stock. The bid is therefore capture hardware plus integration, not a full biometric system ([TED 497245-2026 — border kiosk and biometric capture](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/497245-2026/xml)). Five republications since 22/04/2026, and no award notice a month after the deadline, point to a procedure struggling with its specification or with finding bidders. The previous automated-gate contract sits with a single Budapest incumbent.

Who to talk to: the ticket-machine service subcontractor in Budapest, for the 317-unit swap. Then the winning acquirers, for terminal supply, terminal management and field service on the Treasury and transit estates. Then the police procurement, for a re-run, where the same kiosk hardware, outdoor enclosure and field-service capability sold to banks applies directly.

In short: bid for the hardware, terminal management and service layer through subcontract and parallel supply. Treat the winner of the border tender as the Hungarian public-sector self-service reference to displace later.
drivers: The National Police's two-lot border tender closed 28/07/2026, after five republications since 22/04/2026. No result notice had been published as at 27/08/2026. Lot 2 covers 16 self-service kiosks plus four options and eight automated gates. Lot 1 covers 75 outdoor biometric capture devices ([TED 497245-2026 — border kiosk and biometric capture](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/497245-2026/xml)).

Budapest's signed card-acceptance contract of 16/06/2026 reveals 317 authority-owned ticket machines with built-in unattended terminals, already marked for a brand-for-brand swap. It also lists 350 mobile terminals and software-based acceptance on around 350 devices ([TED 424870-2026 — BKK card acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/424870-2026/xml)).

Those 317 machines are serviced and terminal-managed by a separate subcontractor, and are bought entirely outside the acquiring contract. That is where the reachable hardware demand sits (findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md).

The open-loop contactless acquiring procedure was republished 17/08/2026, with bids due 08/09/2026. It is a 48-month contract whose scope covers real-time fraud prevention and validator master-data management ([BKK cEMV transaction-processing notice](https://ekr.gov.hu/api/publikus/kozbeszerzesi-hirdetmenyek/8805660980571/dokumentum-letoltes)).

Public acquiring itself is now held for three years by a single payments company across the Treasury and transit frameworks. Its transaction-history entry rules rule out a lead bid (findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md).
outlooks.rationale:
Both procedures reached their decision point in the same weeks, and neither produced a published winner. The border tender's deadline passed on 28/07/2026 with no result a month later, and five republications behind it. That is exactly the moment a new entrant can position for a re-run ([TED 497245-2026 — border kiosk and biometric capture](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/497245-2026/xml)).

The transit acquiring award of 16/06/2026 did something more useful than change an acquirer. It published, in unusual detail, an unattended estate that the authority owns, is already replacing and buys through someone else ([TED 424870-2026 — BKK card acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/424870-2026/xml)). Details of the layer Printec can address became visible only because the acquiring layer was lost.
cite_ungrounded: No estimated value was published for either police lot or for the open-loop acquiring procedure, so none of this is sized — that is a disclosure gap, not evidence of a small budget.
Whether the police procedure is in evaluation or heading for a sixth republication is unknown; reading five republications as a procurement in trouble is an inference from the publication history.
The identification of the ticket-machine service subcontractor comes from a single agent and the scope limit is inferred from the acquiring notice rather than from a service contract.

outlooks.scope: Croatian cash-point registry maps deposit capability bank by bank
outlooks.summary:
