Croatia's central bank publishes a national registry of cash access points in machine-readable form. A full download on 27/08/2026 turned it into a target list of 6,852 records from 26 providers. Of these, 3,841 are withdrawal-only ATMs, 901 take cash both in and out, and only 126 are coin deposit machines ([HNB cash-point registry, devices endpoint](https://www.hnb.hr/o/info-cash-point/v1.0/devices?page=1&pageSize=20000)).

The split by bank is the main finding. Zagrebacka banka has a 19.6% deposit share, the lowest of the big four. Erste Croatia has 466 withdrawal-only machines, and 100 of its 106 branches still have staffed cash desks. OTP has 350 withdrawal-only machines.

All of this comes four months before 01/01/2027. From that date, free withdrawals twice a month at other banks' ATMs begin under the law published as Narodne novine 105/2025 ([Ministry of Finance — free basic services package](https://mfin.gov.hr/vijesti/od-1-sijecnja-2026-gradjani-mogu-zatraziti-koristenje-paketa-besplatnih-usluga-koji-je-vezan-za-racun-za-placanje-na-koji-primaju-redovita-primanja/4055)).

Printec should aim at named groups of machines to convert, bank by bank. Coin automation is the part that banks can still charge for.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, and for the first time there is a free, regularly updated target map published by the regulator.

The full registry download on 27/08/2026 returns 6,852 records with provider name, tax number, address and coordinates. These cover 3,841 withdrawal-only ATMs, 901 machines that take cash in and out, and 85 deposit-only machines. They also cover 126 coin deposit machines, 1,860 branches and 39 cashless branches ([HNB cash-point registry, devices endpoint](https://www.hnb.hr/o/info-cash-point/v1.0/devices?page=1&pageSize=20000)).

Zagrebacka banka has the largest fleet in the country. It has 562 withdrawal-only ATMs against 137 that can take deposits, and five cashless branches out of 95.

Privredna banka Zagreb has 429 against 239, the best ratio of the big four. Its own annual report records just 22 coin-payment devices and only five machines that take both banknotes and coins.

Raiffeisenbank Austria has 286 against 150, plus 17 cashless branches. That is the most in the market and the clearest sign that a conversion programme is already running. Roughly 2,400 withdrawal-only machines sit in the six largest bank-owned fleets.

Two more banks were re-counted the same day. Erste Croatia's own locator shows 665 ATMs, of which 199 accept deposits. 100 of its 106 branches still run a staffed cash desk, against only six cashless branches, which is worse than previously recorded. At the same time the bank has opened a fully cashless branch with a 24-hour self-service zone. From 01/04/2026 it has also split branch opening hours so that part of the day is cashless ([Erste Croatia branch and ATM locator](https://local.erstebank.hr/api/v1/atms)).

OTP Croatia lists 459 ATMs, with 109 able to take deposits and 350 withdrawal-only. It added 16 machines and closed three branches in six months ([OTP banka Hrvatska ATM locator feed](https://www.otpbanka.hr/sw/json/atms.json)).

The regulatory timetable is real and is now set in law. The amending act, published in the official gazette as Narodne novine 105/2025 on 23/07/2025, lets consumers request a free basic package. The package covers deposits at counters or ATMs and withdrawals at their own bank. From 01/01/2027 it also lets package holders and vulnerable basic-account holders withdraw free twice a month at any other Croatian bank's machines ([Ministry of Finance — free basic services package](https://mfin.gov.hr/vijesti/od-1-sijecnja-2026-gradjani-mogu-zatraziti-koristenje-paketa-besplatnih-usluga-koji-je-vezan-za-racun-za-placanje-na-koji-primaju-redovita-primanja/4055)).

The law does not force banks to offer ATM deposits, because a bank may comply using tellers alone. But free deposits at the counter are the expensive way to comply. From January, banks will also handle far more withdrawals by other banks' customers with no fee to recover. That is what makes a shared operating model attractive. The banking association's shared-network work has three candidate operating models on the table, and it will never appear on any procurement portal ([Government statement on ATM withdrawal fees](https://vlada.gov.hr/primorac-o-naknadama-za-podizanje-novca-na-bankomatima-gradjani-su-potpuno-zasticeni-imat-ce-besplatne-pakete/44479)).

The strongest commercial point is the coin exception, which the Ministry confirmed on 04/02/2026. Coin processing can still be charged for, in a country with only 45 coin-deposit machines installed. The state Financial Agency's EUR 400,000 coin-counter procedure closed with no winner on 25/06/2026 after its single bid was rejected. No re-tender had been published as at 31/08/2026 ([TED 435583-2026 — coin-counter, no-winner result](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/435583-2026/xml)).

One caution on sizing: the headline 22% national ATM growth in the first half of 2026 is coastal, contact-only and largely from third parties. Seven coastal counties account for more than the entire national increase, while Zagreb's fleet fell. Four non-bank deployers run 1,094 machines, every one of them withdrawal-only ([HNB table PI1 — accepting devices](https://www.hnb.hr/documents/20182/5774485/PI1%20ENG)).

Where to aim:
- Zagrebacka banka through group vendor management rather than the Zagreb board, since it advertises no self-service or channels roles at all.
- Privredna banka Zagreb and Raiffeisenbank Austria locally, where both are hiring.
- Erste Croatia, for added hardware and services on its 100 staffed counters.
- OTP, for its 350 withdrawal-only machines inside a branch-reformatting programme.
- The independent deployers, as buyers of hardware, monitoring and field service in their own right.
- The Financial Agency's failed coin line, as the cleanest re-tender to be ready for.

In short: lead with the registry as the account map. Sell recyclers, which are ATMs that re-use deposited notes, against the cost of free deposits. Price coin automation as a revenue product rather than a compliance cost.
drivers: A full download of the central bank's per-device registry on 27/08/2026 returns 6,852 records from 26 providers, including 3,841 withdrawal-only ATMs. This gives a bank-by-bank map of deposit capability down to machine coordinates ([HNB cash-point registry, devices endpoint](https://www.hnb.hr/o/info-cash-point/v1.0/devices?page=1&pageSize=20000)).

Erste Croatia's own locator shows 665 ATMs, with only 199 able to take deposits. 100 of its 106 branches still run a staffed cash desk. At the same time the bank is changing branch formats and splitting opening hours into cash and cashless windows ([Erste Croatia branch and ATM locator](https://local.erstebank.hr/api/v1/atms)).

OTP Croatia lists 459 ATMs, of which 350 are withdrawal-only. It added 16 machines and closed three branches in six months. Replacing branches with machines is now confirmed across three half-years in a row ([OTP banka Hrvatska ATM locator feed](https://www.otpbanka.hr/sw/json/atms.json)).

The act published as Narodne novine 105/2025 sets the next date. From 01/01/2027, package and basic-account holders may withdraw free twice a month at any other Croatian bank's ATMs. Free deposits are also part of the package ([Ministry of Finance — free basic services package](https://mfin.gov.hr/vijesti/od-1-sijecnja-2026-gradjani-mogu-zatraziti-koristenje-paketa-besplatnih-usluga-koji-je-vezan-za-racun-za-placanje-na-koji-primaju-redovita-primanja/4055)).

Coin processing is clearly left out of the free package, as the Ministry confirmed on 04/02/2026. The market has only 45 coin-deposit machines. The Financial Agency's EUR 400,000 coin-counter tender closed with no winner on 25/06/2026 ([TED 435583-2026 — coin-counter, no-winner result](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/435583-2026/xml)).

The 22% first-half ATM growth is coastal, contact-only and from third parties, not a wave of bank recyclers. The four non-bank deployers run 1,094 machines, all withdrawal-only, so deposits still fall back on the banks ([HNB table PI1 — accepting devices](https://www.hnb.hr/documents/20182/5774485/PI1%20ENG)).
outlooks.rationale:
The map is now available. The central bank's registry was downloaded in full for the first time on 27/08/2026. Two days before that, the half-year infrastructure tables showed the national fleet growing 22% without the deposit gap closing at all. The reason is that the growth is seasonal, coastal, contact-only and run by deployers who take no deposits ([HNB table PI1 — accepting devices](https://www.hnb.hr/documents/20182/5774485/PI1%20ENG)).

This gives a bank-by-bank target list four months before the 01/01/2027 free-withdrawal rule starts. From that date, banks will absorb other banks' traffic with no fee to recover ([Ministry of Finance — free basic services package](https://mfin.gov.hr/vijesti/od-1-sijecnja-2026-gradjani-mogu-zatraziti-koristenje-paketa-besplatnih-usluga-koji-je-vezan-za-racun-za-placanje-na-koji-primaju-redovita-primanja/4055)). In the same period, the largest state coin-counting requirement in the country failed to attract a valid bid.
cite_ungrounded: The figure of roughly 2,400 cash-out-only machines at the six largest bank-owned fleets is the registry's own aggregation; it is not a published central-bank statistic and should be presented as derived.
That much of the coastal build-out may be removed after the season is an inference from its geography and specification, not an observed withdrawal of machines.
No re-tender of the failed coin-counter procedure had been published as at 31/08/2026, so its timing is expected rather than dated.
The banking association's shared-network operating models are not public and the decision reported as weeks away dates from 27/04/2026, so its current status is unknown.

outlooks.scope: HPB: card platform change, motorway acceptance win and deposit gap
outlooks.summary:
Three separate developments reached Croatia's largest domestically-owned bank in one week.

Hrvatska postanska banka has a live job advert saying it has set a strategy that requires changes to its card ecosystem. This covers both issuing (giving cards to customers) and acquiring (taking card payments for merchants) ([HPB card business development vacancy](https://karijere.hpb.hr/jobs/visi-specijalist-za-razvoj-karticnog-poslovanjaupravljanje-karticnim-proizvodima-mz-ckuv)).

It has also just won the largest Croatian open-loop card-acceptance tender of 2026. It will handle card payments across the motorway operator's e-commerce and toll-plaza terminal channels at EUR 1,141,358, against a EUR 1,600,000 estimate, from five bidders ([TED 549006-2026 — motorway card-acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/549006-2026/xml)).

The central bank's registry shows it has 288 withdrawal-only machines against 41 that can take deposits. That is the worst deposit ratio of any large Croatian bank.

Printec should aim at one buying centre that covers card software, unattended terminals, key management and deposit-capable machines at once. That buying centre makes its decisions in Zagreb rather than at a group hub.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, concentrated in a single account rather than spread across a market. The bank has said as much itself.

A Senior Specialist job advert for card business development was confirmed live on 31/08/2026. It states that the bank has set a clear vision and strategy to place it among the leading banks in the card segment. It adds that this also requires changes to its card ecosystem, across both issuing and acquiring ([HPB card business development vacancy](https://karijere.hpb.hr/jobs/visi-specijalist-za-razvoj-karticnog-poslovanjaupravljanje-karticnim-proizvodima-mz-ckuv)). That is close to platform-replacement language at Croatia's largest domestically-owned bank.

The duty to deliver arrived at the same time. The motorway operator awarded acceptance of Visa, Mastercard and Maestro across its e-commerce and toll-plaza terminal channels at EUR 1,141,358, against a EUR 1,600,000 estimate. The contract is dated 07/04/2026 and the award notice was published on 07/08/2026, with five bidders ([TED 549006-2026 — motorway card-acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/549006-2026/xml)).

The bank now has to install and run a fleet of unattended terminals on the motorway network. That means outdoor enclosures, remote key injection, terminal management and field service on toll plazas, where downtime has to be kept to a minimum.

The third strand is the cash gap. The central bank's registry gives HPB 288 withdrawal-only ATMs against just 41 that can take deposits. That is a 12.5% deposit share and the worst gap-to-fleet ratio of any large Croatian bank. It also has 65 branches, none of them cashless, plus a partner network of 219 machines run by an external deployer and 973 post-office counter locations ([HNB cash-point registry, devices endpoint](https://www.hnb.hr/o/info-cash-point/v1.0/devices?page=1&pageSize=20000)).

A fourth, smaller strand sits alongside and is unique in the footprint. HPB is the only entity whose crypto-asset activity is supervised by a central bank. It enters through a notification rather than a licence. The supervisor confirmed on 03/07/2026 that institutions already under supervision use that route ([HANFA — provision of crypto services from 1 July 2026](https://www.hanfa.hr/vijesti/pruzanje-kriptousluga-od-1-srpnja-2026-za-drustva-obvezna-kriptolicenca-i-upis-u-hanfine-registre-a-korisnike-se-poziva-na-oprez/)).

Each notification needs an evidence pack covering internal controls, asset segregation, custody, money-laundering controls and technology resilience. That maps onto key-management hardware, documented key ceremonies, crypto-aware transaction monitoring and remote identity verification.

The wider Croatian Post relationship is worth reading alongside it. The post office buys card acceptance as a service from a bank rather than terminals from a vendor. It has a EUR 1,150,000 technical-protection maintenance tender that closed for bids on 17/08/2026 with no award published ([TED 490123-2026 — technical-protection maintenance](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/490123-2026/xml)).

Where to aim:
- HPB directly, on card issuing and acquiring software.
- Unattended terminal supply with terminal management for the toll-plaza rollout.
- Key-management hardware.
- Deposit-capable machines, against the 288-machine gap.
- The compliance evidence layer behind the crypto notification.
- A place inside an acquirer's stack for the next Croatian Post cycle, rather than bidding to the post office directly.

In short: this is the best-qualified single Croatian buying centre this cycle. Unlike the foreign-owned banks, the decision is taken in Zagreb.
drivers: HPB's own live job advert states the bank has set a strategy that requires changes to its card ecosystem, across both issuing and acquiring ([HPB card business development vacancy](https://karijere.hpb.hr/jobs/visi-specijalist-za-razvoj-karticnog-poslovanjaupravljanje-karticnim-proizvodima-mz-ckuv)).

HPB won the largest Croatian open-loop card-acceptance tender of 2026. It covers motorway e-commerce and toll-plaza channels at EUR 1,141,358 against a EUR 1,600,000 estimate, from five bidders, with the contract dated 07/04/2026 ([TED 549006-2026 — motorway card-acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/549006-2026/xml)).

The central bank's registry puts HPB at 288 withdrawal-only machines against 41 that can take deposits. That is a 12.5% deposit share and the worst ratio of any large Croatian bank, with 65 branches and none cashless ([HNB cash-point registry, devices endpoint](https://www.hnb.hr/o/info-cash-point/v1.0/devices?page=1&pageSize=20000)).

HPB is the only entity in the footprint whose crypto-asset activity is supervised by a central bank. It enters through a notification that requires a full evidence pack on controls, custody and resilience ([HANFA — provision of crypto services from 1 July 2026](https://www.hanfa.hr/vijesti/pruzanje-kriptousluga-od-1-srpnja-2026-za-drustva-obvezna-kriptolicenca-i-upis-u-hanfine-registre-a-korisnike-se-poziva-na-oprez/)).

Croatian Post, HPB's counter partner network, buys card acceptance as a service from a bank. It has a EUR 1,150,000 technical-protection maintenance award still pending since bids closed on 17/08/2026 ([TED 490123-2026 — technical-protection maintenance](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/490123-2026/xml)).
outlooks.rationale:
Three separate strands came together at one bank in a single cycle. The first is a public statement that the card platform has to change, confirmed live on 31/08/2026 ([HPB card business development vacancy](https://karijere.hpb.hr/jobs/visi-specijalist-za-razvoj-karticnog-poslovanjaupravljanje-karticnim-proizvodima-mz-ckuv)). The second is an acquiring win published on 07/08/2026 that requires the bank to deploy and run a fleet of unattended terminals it does not have today ([TED 549006-2026 — motorway card-acceptance award](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/549006-2026/xml)). The third is a regulator-published registry showing the weakest deposit-capable fleet of any large Croatian bank.

Declared intent, a delivery duty and a measured gap have arrived together. That makes this the moment to act, rather than a general prospect.
cite_ungrounded: Reading the vacancy text as evidence of a card platform replacement is an interpretation of recruitment language; HPB has published no procurement, budget or programme for it.
That the motorway award forces new unattended terminal hardware onto toll plazas is inferred from the awarded channels; the notice does not specify a device replacement.
The Croatian Post technical-protection award had not been published as at 27/08/2026, so its outcome and timing are unknown.

outlooks.scope: RBI's Addiko takeover brings two Croatian fleets into one integration programme
outlooks.summary:
Raiffeisen Bank International won the contested takeover of Addiko Bank, and the result was confirmed on 03/08/2026. Acceptances covered 56.16% of the shares subject to the offer, equal to 55.55% of total share capital. The rival bid reached only 31.22% and will not go through ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

RBI keeps Croatia, Slovenia and Austria, would become Croatia's fourth-largest bank, and has budgeted a one-off integration cost of about EUR 75m across 2027-2028.

The Croatian opportunity can be measured. Addiko Croatia's own locator, checked across all 94 towns on 27/08/2026, shows 35 branches and 144 ATMs. Not one of them carries any deposit or recycler wording. Next to it sits Raiffeisenbank Austria's Croatian fleet of 286 withdrawal and 150 deposit machines.

Printec should aim at the integration planning now, in Vienna and Zagreb, not at Addiko.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, on a funded and dated bank merger inside Printec's own footprint.

The official result under the Austrian takeover rules records acceptances for 10,831,435 shares. That is 56.16% of the shares subject to the offer, or 55.55% of total share capital. RBI had cut its own minimum threshold from 75% to 55%.

The rival offer, raised twice to EUR 37.00 a share, took only 31.22% against a condition of half the capital plus one share. It will not go through or be extended.

The extended acceptance period runs to 03/11/2026. Completion is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. All closing conditions fall due by 14/05/2027 ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

RBI has budgeted a one-off integration cost of about EUR 75 million across 2027 and 2028, against roughly EUR 60m of extra profit in 2028. It would become the fourth-largest bank in Croatia and re-enter Slovenia. Its own offer document calls full operational, technological and organisational integration of the Croatian subsidiary a key success factor.

The estate to be merged has been counted. Addiko Croatia shows 35 branches and 144 ATMs, with no deposit or recycler wording anywhere in its own locator. Raiffeisenbank Austria has 286 withdrawal plus 150 deposit machines and 41 branches, of which 17 are cashless. That is the largest cashless-branch programme in the market and the likely template for the merged network (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Slovenia is smaller and shaped differently, with 20 branches and 31 ATMs in express and mall formats and no published deposit product. It is therefore a new channel built from scratch rather than a trimming of an existing one.

Addiko itself is short of money. It has a Swiss-franc loan provision of EUR 33.1m to EUR 48.8m, a half-year loss of EUR 23.0m, a 71.7% cost-to-income ratio and suspended guidance. That sets the commercial split: sell service-based offers to Addiko today and capital-heavy hardware to RBI.

A second budget point in the same window makes the timing tighter. Every significant institution must file an action plan with its supervisory team by 31/10/2026. One named focus area is modernising infrastructure by replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies. Another requires accurate identification of technology assets, and a third brings supplier contract terms and service levels into scope ([ECB Banking Supervision letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

The same expectation was extended down to nationally supervised banks on 31/07/2026. Ageing machines on unsupported operating systems sit squarely inside that inventory. The money to fix them has to be named in a plan a supervisor reads.

Behind both sits the national shared-ATM-network question, due 01/01/2027. It is procured privately through the banking association, with no notice to answer ([Government statement on ATM withdrawal fees](https://vlada.gov.hr/primorac-o-naknadama-za-podizanje-novca-na-bankomatima-gradjani-su-potpuno-zasticeni-imat-ce-besplatne-pakete/44479)).

Where to aim: RBI group procurement in Vienna and the Zagreb integration office, on the following:
- the 144 Addiko machines that appear unable to take deposits, as an upgrade-or-replace group;
- merging two fleets onto one set of driving software and one managed-service contract;
- card and acquiring migration;
- key migration;
- combining money-laundering and transaction-monitoring systems.

All of this sits inside the EUR 75m envelope.

In short: pre-sales has to run through the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2027 while the programme is being scoped, not when it is announced.
drivers: The takeover result published on 03/08/2026 records acceptances of 56.16% of the shares subject to the offer, equal to 55.55% of total capital. The rival bid sits at 31.22% and will not go through. The extended acceptance period runs to 03/11/2026, and closing conditions fall due by 14/05/2027 ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

RBI has budgeted a one-off integration cost of about EUR 75m across 2027-2028, against roughly EUR 60m of extra profit in 2028. It calls full operational and technological integration of the Croatian subsidiary a key success factor (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Addiko Croatia's own locator, checked across all 94 towns on 27/08/2026, shows 35 branches and 144 ATMs. None of them carries any deposit or recycler wording (findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md).

Raiffeisenbank Austria's Croatian network already runs 17 cashless branches, the most in the market, alongside 286 withdrawal and 150 deposit machines. This is the template the merged estate will be standardised on ([HNB cash-point registry, devices endpoint](https://www.hnb.hr/o/info-cash-point/v1.0/devices?page=1&pageSize=20000)).

Significant institutions must file an action plan with their supervisory team by 31/10/2026, naming how they will replace legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies. Asset inventory and supplier service levels are also in scope ([ECB Banking Supervision letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
The uncertainty ended on 03/08/2026. Until then, Croatia had a contested takeover with two bidders and no integration budget anyone could plan against.

There is now a declared winner and a stated EUR 75m envelope for 2027-2028. The extended acceptance period runs to 03/11/2026, and completion is expected inside this quarter ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

The estate on both sides was then counted from the banks' own locators and the central-bank registry on 27/08/2026, so the merged network can be argued in concrete terms. The supervisory action-plan deadline of 31/10/2026 also forces the same institutions to write down their end-of-life technology in the same weeks ([ECB Banking Supervision letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).
cite_ungrounded: That Addiko Croatia's 144 machines cannot take deposits rests on the absence of any deposit or recycler wording in the bank's own locator, not on a statement by the bank; it should be described as apparently deposit-incapable.
No integration workplan, vendor decision or estate-standardisation choice has been published; the consolidation workstreams listed are derived from RBI's stated intent to integrate fully.
Whether ageing machines at either bank actually run unsupported operating systems is not evidenced here — the supervisory letter creates the disclosure duty, not the finding.

outlooks.scope: Sense Bank puts both device estates out to contract in one fortnight
outlooks.summary:
Ukraine's Sense Bank has put both of its device channels out to contract within two weeks, and the larger one has already been awarded. Its UAH 29.8m self-service servicing contract drew a single domestic bidder when bids closed on 28/08/2026, and it starts on 01/09/2026. A UAH 18.4m post-warranty card-terminal contract in three lots still had no bids recorded as at 31/08/2026 ([Prozorro UA-2026-08-21-002726-a](https://prozorro.gov.ua/tender/UA-2026-08-21-002726-a)).

The reading is mixed rather than negative. The card-terminal work is on card-reading hardware that is already Printec's home ground in Ukraine. A small physical-security maintenance requirement at the same bank has also failed twice, because no acceptable bid came in.

The complication is governance. The bank's management-board chair was suspended in August 2026 and its supervisory board is incomplete. That makes it hard for the bank to sign a long managed-service contract this year.
outlooks.projected:
Mixed, with one opportunity closing and two staying open.

The self-service half of this account has just been taken without competition. Servicing of self-service banking terminals plus their communications equipment went to a single domestic bidder when bids closed on 28/08/2026. It is worth UAH 29,777,476.47 excluding VAT (about EUR 573k) on a twelve-month term from 01/09/2026 ([Prozorro UA-2026-08-19-010667-a](https://prozorro.gov.ua/tender/UA-2026-08-19-010667-a)).

The card-terminal half is the live one. It covers post-warranty service of the POS estate at UAH 18,395,006.43 excluding VAT, split into three lots and closing 01/09/2026 with zero bids recorded. The largest lot, at UAH 9,631,912.05, covers Verifone and Castles Saturn 1000F2 terminals. These are the same terminal families supplied into the Ukrainian market at 39,000-unit scale ([tender.privatbank.ua PB-2026-06-26-3070719](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-06-26-3070719)).

Alongside it sits a physical-security maintenance lot that has failed twice. It is worth UAH 722,530 including VAT and covers time-delay cash safes and deposit lockers. It drew two bidders in May 2026 and was declared unsuccessful. Its 12/06/2026 re-run drew none at all.

Where to aim:
- The three post-warranty terminal lots at Sense Bank, led by the Verifone and Castles lot.
- The twice-failed safe and locker maintenance lot, where a direct quote can be priced against a known UAH 137k to 525k range rather than an empty field.
- Peter Novak, the career banking-operations executive who joined the supervisory board on 24/08/2026, as the patient relationship route while the board is rebuilt.

In short: treat Sense Bank as a card-terminal and physical-security services account for the next two quarters rather than a self-service one. Approach the self-service scope again ahead of its 31/08/2027 expiry.
drivers: The UAH 29.8m self-service servicing contract closed on 28/08/2026 with a single domestic bidder and runs from 01/09/2026 to 31/08/2027. The largest device-service scope at this bank is therefore spoken for ([Prozorro UA-2026-08-19-010667-a](https://prozorro.gov.ua/tender/UA-2026-08-19-010667-a))

A UAH 18.4m post-warranty card-terminal contract in three lots — Verifone and Castles, Ingenico, and PAX — closed on 01/09/2026 with no bids recorded as at 31/08/2026 ([Prozorro UA-2026-08-21-002726-a](https://prozorro.gov.ua/tender/UA-2026-08-21-002726-a))

A UAH 722,530 physical-security maintenance requirement, covering time-delay cash safes and deposit lockers, has failed twice. It drew two bidders in May 2026 and none on the June re-run ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md))

Governance is the brake. The management-board chair was suspended and a supervisory-board member removed by Cabinet decision on 22/08/2026. The National Bank publicly asked the government on 27/08/2026 to restore the bank's governing bodies ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md))

Ukraine now has domestic vendors that sell the whole self-service stack — central device management, cash-cycle software, monitoring and field service — and also build their own machines. That is why the self-service lot drew one bid and closed at list price ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md))
outlooks.rationale:
Both of this bank's device channels came to market in the same fortnight, and that is unlikely to happen again. The self-service lot was settled on 28/08/2026 and is committed for a year. The card-terminal lots were still empty three days later.

That is the one point at which a supplier can enter a scope on its own terms rather than against an incumbent's renewal price ([Prozorro UA-2026-08-21-002726-a](https://prozorro.gov.ua/tender/UA-2026-08-21-002726-a)). The twice-failed safe and locker lot adds a second, much cheaper way in, which the local market has already turned down twice ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).
cite_ungrounded: The claim that the Verifone and Castles lot 1 hardware matches terminals already supplied in Ukraine is drawn from a separate PrivatBank supply record, not from Sense Bank's own tender documents.
No bid was recorded on the POS lots as at 31/08/2026, but the slice does not confirm the outcome after the 01/09/2026 closing date.

outlooks.scope: PrivatBank recycler tender moves to its stage-2 commercial round
outlooks.summary:
The largest single cash-machine procurement in the region has restarted. PrivatBank's recycler tender PB-2026-03-17-3068329 closed stage-1 qualification on 25/08/2026. It now waits for the stage-2 commercial round, so a procurement that had been parked since spring is live again ([tender.privatbank.ua PB-2026-03-17-3068329](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-03-17-3068329)).

Two factors add risk. First, the bank does not publish a shortlist for this procurement, so it is not known which suppliers passed stage one. On the parallel banknote-sorter tender at the same bank, where the shortlist is published, four other firms are named.

Second, the specification is written against a Diebold Nixdorf software baseline. Any offer built on a different device-control stack has to certify against it, or get the clause challenged before stage two is frozen. The commercial question this quarter is qualification and specification, not price.
drivers: Stage-1 qualification closed on 25/08/2026 and the record moved to the stage-2 waiting state. The commercial round is therefore the next event on the largest ATM-hardware programme in the footprint ([tender.privatbank.ua PB-2026-03-17-3068329](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-03-17-3068329))

The requirement is written to a Diebold Nixdorf software baseline: ProFlex 4.x, VCP Pro 7 and Vynamic View monitoring across every module. All adaptation is at the vendor's cost, and no budget is published ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md))

PrivatBank publishes no shortlist for this procurement, so no supplier's stage-1 clearance is known. On its parallel sorter round, where the list is published, the four named firms are Glory Global Solutions, Bankivski Tekhnolohii, DIIP 2000 and I.B.S. ([tender.privatbank.ua PB-2026-08-20-3072069](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-08-20-3072069))

The bank's own 2025 recycler contract of 1,140 NCR machines carries a 24-month warranty. That puts the service and warranty change point at around November 2027 rather than 2026 ([Prozorro UA-2025-01-17-010779-a](https://public-api.prozorro.gov.ua/api/2.5/tenders/91535417b84240648f1dabd4a3fd1e22))

Second-line maintenance of the bank's Diebold Nixdorf recycler estate is still unsourced after two failed attempts at UAH 4,080,000 including VAT. No third attempt appeared in the five months to 27/08/2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md))
outlooks.rationale:
This programme was parked for four months and is now active again. The qualification window shut on 25/08/2026, and the commercial round is the next step ([tender.privatbank.ua PB-2026-03-17-3068329](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-03-17-3068329)).

What changed alongside it is the evidence about the qualification gate rather than about the contract itself. The same bank published a stage-1 qualified list on its sorter contest three days later. The four names on it are the local and manufacturer field, which makes the two-stage qualification process itself the thing to fix ([tender.privatbank.ua PB-2026-08-20-3072069](https://tender.privatbank.ua/commercial/tender/PB-2026-08-20-3072069)).
cite_ungrounded: No unit count for the current recycler tender is supported by the portal record; the 1,140-machine figure quoted here belongs to the separate 2025 contract, not to this procurement.
The expectation that the stage-2 commercial round follows within weeks is the collector's read, not a date published on the tender portal.
Which suppliers cleared stage-1 qualification on this procurement is not published and is not established either way.

outlooks.scope: New UAH 2,000 note requires nationwide device reconfiguration
outlooks.summary:
Ukraine gets a new highest-value banknote on 04/09/2026, and every machine in the country that handles cash has to be taught to recognise it. The National Bank's own data file puts the estate at 38,721 self-service devices at 01/07/2026 — 15,768 ATMs and 22,953 self-service payment kiosks. For the first time, the bank has released free technical configuration materials before a note's circulation date ([NBU PC_table_1.xlsx](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx)).

This is a fixed-date, market-wide field-services and firmware event rather than a single tender. It means note templates on every acceptor, dispenser and recycler, cassette re-planning, and a changed mix of denominations that forces cash forecasting to be re-tuned.

Because 59% of the fleet is independent payment kiosks rather than bank ATMs, the work lands heaviest on operators with the smallest engineering teams. The work continues after 04/09 rather than ending on that date.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, on a date that cannot be moved.

The UAH 2,000 note enters circulation on 04/09/2026 as an entirely new highest denomination. The National Bank's own banknotes-in-circulation page still lists only the 1000 down to the 20, confirming it is not yet in issue ([NBU — UAH 2000 banknote page](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/uah/obig-banknote/2000_2026_2026)).

The population of devices is exact rather than estimated. There were 38,721 self-service devices at 01/07/2026, made up of 15,768 ATMs and 22,953 self-service payment kiosks. That is up from 38,685 a month earlier ([NBU PC_table_1.xlsx](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx)).

Through August 2026 the regulator gave banks, cash-in-transit firms and device service companies free technical configuration capability. It stated that this is the first time it has run such a procedure ahead of a circulation date. The materials cannot be released until the note is declassified at its presentation.

A second, separate piece of work opened on 26/08/2026. The National Bank put changes to the bank cash-operations instruction out to consultation expressly because of the new denomination. The changes add it to the list of notes banks must surrender and refine packaging specifications. Written comments close on 04/09/2026 ([NBU cash-operations draft consultation 26/08/2026](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/news/all/proponuyutsya-zmini-do-poryadku-organizatsiyi-kasovoyi-roboti-bankiv)).

The scope should be stated honestly. That resolution covers surrender lists and packaging. The validator, recycler and sorter work is therefore a commercial consequence of the new note, not something the resolution itself requires.

The structural backdrop supports the same argument twice over. Only 2,785 of the 15,768 ATMs, or 17.7%, can take deposits, and that share has barely moved since 2024. Meanwhile currency in circulation rose to UAH 921,808m at 01/08/2026, up 6.3% in seven months ([NBU H1-2026 card-market release](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/news/all/bezgotivkovi-rozrahunki-platijnimi-kartkami-dominuyut--rezultati-pershogo-pivrichchya-2026-roku)).

Where to aim:
- The independent kiosk operators, led by EasyPay, iBox and City24, which run the 22,953-device majority of the fleet with small engineering teams.
- The cash-in-transit and device-service firms that need verified coverage of every device and cannot staff it.
- Bank cash centres, for cassette re-planning and denomination-mix changes in cash forecasting.
- The same kiosk operators again, for the separate screen-flow and one-time-password work that Resolution No. 67 has required at every cash-in kiosk since 26/06/2026 ([NBU Постанова № 67 of 16/06/2026](https://bank.gov.ua/admin_uploads/law/16062026_67.pdf?v=19)).

In short: sell speed and verified per-device coverage rather than a deadline. The machines still not updated after 04/09 are the retrofit pipeline, and that pipeline runs for the whole following year.
drivers: The UAH 2,000 note enters circulation on 04/09/2026, the first new highest denomination in the currency, and configuration materials were released free during August 2026 ([NBU — UAH 2000 banknote page](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/uah/obig-banknote/2000_2026_2026))

The device population is confirmed from the regulator's own data file at 38,721 machines on 01/07/2026. Of these, 22,953 are independent self-service payment kiosks rather than bank ATMs ([NBU PC_table_1.xlsx](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx))

A separate cash-operations consultation opened on 26/08/2026 and closed on 04/09/2026. It adds the new note to bank surrender lists and refines packaging specifications ([NBU cash-operations draft consultation 26/08/2026](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/news/all/proponuyutsya-zmini-do-poryadku-organizatsiyi-kasovoyi-roboti-bankiv))

Only 17.7% of Ukrainian ATMs can accept cash, and that share has been flat since 2024. Notes in circulation keep rising, so a fixed estate is handling a growing volume of notes ([NBU PC_table_1.xlsx](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx))

The same kiosk fleet is also carrying a mandatory one-time-password identity check at every cash-in, in force since 26/06/2026. One field visit can therefore do two pieces of work ([NBU Постанова № 67 of 16/06/2026](https://bank.gov.ua/admin_uploads/law/16062026_67.pdf?v=19))
outlooks.rationale:
The device count stopped being an estimate this cycle. The regulator published the file, and it records 38,721 machines, 59% of them independent kiosks ([NBU PC_table_1.xlsx](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/file/download?file=PC_table_1.xlsx)).

Against that, a brand-new highest denomination lands on 04/09/2026, with configuration materials released only weeks before. That is the shortest preparation window the market has ever had for a note change ([NBU — UAH 2000 banknote page](https://bank.gov.ua/ua/uah/obig-banknote/2000_2026_2026)).
cite_ungrounded: No contract value, buyer list or procurement route for the reconfiguration work is published anywhere; the commercial scale is inferred from the device count alone.
The naming of EasyPay, iBox and City24 as the operators most exposed reflects the collector's read of the kiosk market rather than a published operator-by-operator device split.

outlooks.scope: Banca Intesa's outsourced ATM estate approaches its stated 36-month term
outlooks.summary:
Serbia's largest bank handed 122 of its off-site cash machines to an outside operator in 2023 on a stated 36-month contract. That term points to a window around December 2026. The arrangement was re-checked at source on 27/08/2026. It is still live and unchanged, with no renewal or re-tender notice from either side ([Payten — Banca Intesa Belgrade ATM outsourcing](https://www.payten.com/en/news-events/news/banca-intesa-d-belgrade-atm-outsourcing/)).

Underneath it, the bank runs 434 self-service devices, of which only 123 can take cash in as well as pay it out. It also has a separate 135-unit fleet of machines for merchant takings. It keeps four permanent teller-recruitment pipelines open across roughly 74 locations, which is manual cash handling it has not managed to automate away.

The direction is growth. The expiry date is an inference rather than a disclosure, so the approach is to be in the room early rather than wait for a notice.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, on the clearest managed-services entry point in Serbia.

The 2023 arrangement covers 122 cash machines at Banca Intesa external locations on a stated 36-month contract. Every machine is to be replaced with latest-generation Diebold Nixdorf dispensing and recycling devices. The scope also includes the security suite, site-lease negotiation and all ATM operational duties, moving the bank to a fixed-cost model with no investment. It was re-checked at its original address on 27/08/2026 and remains live and unchanged, with no replacing, renewal or re-tender notice anywhere ([Payten — Banca Intesa Belgrade ATM outsourcing](https://www.payten.com/en/news-events/news/banca-intesa-d-belgrade-atm-outsourcing/)).

The bank's own 2025 report, published 12/05/2026, discloses 434 self-service devices. Only 375 of them dispense dinar and only 123 are multifunction cash-in and cash-out units, installed over five years. It also has 135 specialised machines for merchant takings across 123 of its 134 branches, carrying 2.3m deposits worth almost RSD 315bn a year ([Banca Intesa — Godišnji izveštaj 2025](https://www.bancaintesa.rs/document/publications/BIB/Godi%C5%A1nji-izve%C5%A1taji/godisnji_izvestaj_2025/Godisnji%20izvestaj%202025%20SRB.pdf)).

Migration is already proven inside this bank. 86% of dinar deposits and 73% of euro deposits happen on machines, and 24% of branches now run cashless. In 2025 the bank added 14 machines and replaced 26 in-branch units, which is scope explicitly outside the external-locations deal.

A second, independent type of evidence backs the cost case. The bank's real applicant-tracking system shows four standing teller pipelines open continuously since 31/01/2025 across roughly 74 locations, plus a Belgrade regional pipeline opened 03/04/2026 ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

Market conditions favour the approach this autumn. The national estate grew to 3,412 machines at 30/06/2026, the fastest yearly growth in the published series back to 2016. Cash deposited at machines rose 31.9% by count and 53.6% by value year on year, while teller withdrawals fell 3.9% ([NBS — Acceptance network statistics](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/platni-sistem/statistika/el_novac/prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)).

Where to aim:
- The in-branch estate, which sits outside the external-locations contract and where the bank replaced 26 units on its own account in 2025.
- The 135-unit merchant-takings fleet, as a third and separate refresh cycle.
- The external-locations scope itself, as its stated term approaches.

Keep compliance and onboarding out of the pitch, because those decisions are made in Milan, not Belgrade.

In short: build the in-branch and merchant-deposit case now on the bank's own published migration numbers. The external-locations conversation then starts from delivered work rather than from a cold approach.
drivers: The 2023 outsourcing of 122 external-location machines on a stated 36-month term was re-verified unchanged on 27/08/2026, with no renewal or re-tender notice published by either party ([Payten — Banca Intesa Belgrade ATM outsourcing](https://www.payten.com/en/news-events/news/banca-intesa-d-belgrade-atm-outsourcing/))

Only 123 of the bank's 434 self-service devices are multifunction cash-in and cash-out units, even though the bank itself discloses that 86% of dinar deposits already happen on machines ([Banca Intesa — Godišnji izveštaj 2025](https://www.bancaintesa.rs/document/publications/BIB/Godi%C5%A1nji-izve%C5%A1taji/godisnji_izvestaj_2025/Godisnji%20izvestaj%202025%20SRB.pdf))

Four teller-recruitment pipelines have stood open continuously since 31/01/2025 across about 74 locations, showing manual cash handling the bank cannot staff away ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

The in-branch estate can be contested separately: the bank replaced 26 in-branch machines in 2025 on scope explicitly outside the external-locations deal ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md))

Serbia is one of very few European markets adding machines, with 3,412 at 30/06/2026 and machine deposit value up 53.6% year on year while teller withdrawals fell ([NBS — Acceptance network statistics](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/platni-sistem/statistika/el_novac/prihvatna_mreza.xlsx))
outlooks.rationale:
Two independent types of evidence landed on the same account on 31/08/2026. The first is a competitor-held outsourcing scope, re-verified as still running against a stated 36-month term. The second is a permanent teller-hiring programme, which shows that branch cash handling at this bank is still manual and still expensive ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

Neither on its own would move a plan. Together they indicate that the window to shape the next arrangement is the next two quarters, because silence from both parties is just as consistent with a quiet renewal ([Payten — Banca Intesa Belgrade ATM outsourcing](https://www.payten.com/en/news-events/news/banca-intesa-d-belgrade-atm-outsourcing/)).
cite_ungrounded: The December-2026 window is inferred from the 36-month term announced in 2023; neither Banca Intesa nor the operator has ever disclosed a start or end date.
Continued silence from both parties is equally consistent with a quiet renewal having already happened.

outlooks.scope: National Bank of Serbia procurement plan for cash and payment systems
outlooks.summary:
The National Bank of Serbia adopted version 9 of its 2026 procurement plan on 26/08/2026. The plan is unusually wide. It covers hardware security modules, which are secure boxes that hold a bank's payment keys. It also covers joining the European payments area and its instant-payment platform. The remaining lines are load-balancing hardware for instant-payment participants, cyber-protection and a card-system upgrade ([NBS — Plan javnih nabavki za 2026, verzija 9](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/propisi/propisi-tend/2026/plan_nabavki_2026_v9.pdf)).

Five procedures ran in the same period. One is still open and closes 11/09/2026. A banknote-processing maintenance contract closed 28/08/2026. It gives 40 of its 100 award points to service rates rather than list price.

The central bank also accepts bids in Serbian or English. That removes the usual objection about language and the need for a local company. No euro values are published. So treat this as a pipeline of contests won on qualifications, rather than a revenue line with a known size. Forecast conversion with a buffer for review risk.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, and the pipeline is unusually easy to read because the buyer publishes everything. The National Bank of Serbia adopted version 9 of its 2026 procurement plan on 26/08/2026 and posted it the next day.

The plan lists these open procedures ([NBS — Plan javnih nabavki za 2026, verzija 9](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/propisi/propisi-tend/2026/plan_nabavki_2026_v9.pdf)):

- Hardware security modules, the tamper-proof boxes that hold a bank's payment keys and encrypt card PINs.
- Joining the single euro payments area and its instant-payment settlement platform. This includes a payment-systems software upgrade that links the central bank's systems to the European one.
- Load-balancing hardware for instant-payment participants.
- A cyber-protection solution and a combined information-security risk-management solution.
- An upgrade to the stand-in processing module of the card system, for domestic and UnionPay chip cards.
- A chip-embedding machine for ID-format cards.
- Terminals with printer consumables.

Five procedures ran alongside the plan. Maintenance of the automatic banknote-processing system at the Novi Sad cash centre closed on 28/08/2026. It is an 18-month contract, scored price 60, spare parts 20, call-out charge 10 and engineer hourly rate 10. So 40 of the 100 points sit on service rates. A credible managed-services bidder can win that scoring without being the maker of the machine. The winner becomes the service incumbent on that machine until roughly February 2028 ([UJN — JN 201/2026 Glory UW-F4 maintenance](https://jnportal.ujn.gov.rs/tender-eo/378545)).

A hot-application machine for optically variable security elements, JN 397/2026, is still open and closes 11/09/2026. It is an openly international procedure. Two awards landed in the period, one for card-personalisation spares and one for heavy vault-door maintenance. Both went to specialists, so the competition is not weak.

The central bank's automatic banknote sorting and packing systems are held under two contracts dated 05/02/2024. They are worth a combined RSD 213.6m, about EUR 1.8m, and are held by a local bidder group. A second local firm holds the state Treasury's counting, sorting and vault equipment ([UJN — Registar ugovora, CPV 30132200](https://jnportal.ujn.gov.rs/contracts)).

Around all of this sits the payments programme. Serbia joined the single euro payments area on 22/05/2025. Of 19 banks, 18 went live on credit transfers on 4 and 5 May 2026. But every Serbian bank takes part indirectly through a parent bank abroad. There is still no Serbian date for instant euro payments ([NBS — SEPA u Republici Srbiji](https://www.nbs.rs/sr/scripts/showcontent/index.html?id=21465&konverzija=no)).

Where to aim:

- The hardware security module line and the payments software upgrade. A central-bank reference is what opens doors at the private commercial banks that never tender at all.
- The banknote-processing maintenance contract and the ones that follow it, where service rates decide the score.
- The open procedure closing 11/09/2026, while it is still open.
- The move of banks from indirect to direct scheme participation.
- The move of the Serbia–Bosnia–Montenegro foreign-exchange clearing platform off old message formats to the ISO 20022 standard. It forces 20 banks and three central banks to remap flows and retune screening.

Two rules apply. Do not sell against a Serbian instant-euro deadline, because the regulator confirms there is none. Do not sell payment-regulation compliance built on the newest European directive, because Serbia is a full cycle behind.

In short: bid for the service-weighted maintenance work to win the reference. Use the published plan as a twelve-month calendar rather than a single deal.
drivers: Version 9 of the 2026 procurement plan was adopted on 26/08/2026. It lists hardware security modules, payments-platform accession, instant-payment load balancing, cyber-protection and a card-system upgrade as open procedures ([NBS — Plan javnih nabavki za 2026, verzija 9](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/propisi/propisi-tend/2026/plan_nabavki_2026_v9.pdf))

The banknote-processing maintenance contract that closed 28/08/2026 puts 40 of 100 award points on spare parts, call-out charge and engineer hourly rate. This favours real in-country field capability ([UJN — JN 201/2026 Glory UW-F4 maintenance](https://jnportal.ujn.gov.rs/tender-eo/378545))

The central bank accepts bids in Serbian or English, and ran JN 397/2026 as an openly international procedure closing 11/09/2026. This removes the usual objection about language and needing a local company ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md))

The current suppliers are technically qualified rather than a price-only dealer layer. One local bidder group holds the central bank's automatic sorting and packing systems on contracts worth about EUR 1.8m ([UJN — Registar ugovora, CPV 30132200](https://jnportal.ujn.gov.rs/contracts))

The payments backdrop is credit transfer only, with indirect participation and no Serbian date for instant euro payments. So the work that can be bought is connectivity, message migration and screening, not a licence sale driven by a deadline ([NBS — SEPA u Republici Srbiji](https://www.nbs.rs/sr/scripts/showcontent/index.html?id=21465&konverzija=no))
outlooks.rationale:
A central bank is rewiring its cash processing, card systems and payments infrastructure in a single year. It has just published the whole list. That came two days after one of its service-weighted maintenance contracts closed, and two weeks before another closes ([NBS — Plan javnih nabavki za 2026, verzija 9](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/propisi/propisi-tend/2026/plan_nabavki_2026_v9.pdf)).

The planning correction that came with it matters as much as the pipeline. One request for protection of rights, which is a bidder's legal challenge, added eight months between bid deadline and signature on a single procedure. So Serbian public conversion has to be forecast with a buffer for review risk, not a 30-to-60-day award window ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).
cite_ungrounded: No euro value is published for any line in the procurement plan, so nothing here can be sized.

The contract values, winner names and signature dates for the incumbent-held central-bank sorting contracts could not be independently re-verified this cycle because the portal serves a JavaScript shell and refuses its data paths without credentials.
The proposition that a central-bank reference unlocks the private commercial banks is commercial judgement, not evidenced in the signals.

outlooks.scope: AikBank branch refits and its 457 dispense-only machines
outlooks.summary:
AikBank is renovating a branch roughly every two weeks. It uses a specification that its own annual report calls the basis for creating the network. So the device standard is copied at each site instead of being tendered again each time.

Its published machine feed, re-counted on 27/08/2026, shows 570 machines. Of those, 457, or four in five, only pay out cash and cannot take a deposit at all ([AikBank public ATM/branch locator feed](https://www.aikbank.rs/data/maps-formated.json)). That gap sits in a market where cash deposited at machines grew 31.9% by count and 53.6% by value in a year. A dispense-only machine therefore serves a shrinking part of demand.

Two of the bank's four August renovation notices send customers to a rival's dispense-only network while the branch is closed. That is a warning, and it is also the argument for putting a deposit-capable machine inside the branch. Winning a place in the standard is worth more than winning any single site.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, and this is still the largest measured pool of deposit upgrades in Serbia. We re-counted the bank's own machine-readable feed on 27/08/2026. It shows 570 machines, of which 457 are dispense-only and physically cannot take cash. The other 113 are multifunction units that can take deposits. Alongside these are 63 automated teller safes and 113 branches ([AikBank public ATM/branch locator feed](https://www.aikbank.rs/data/maps-formated.json)).

The refurbishment programme has sped up, not paused. The bank's own sitemap now holds 20 separate branch-renovation notices for 2026, on top of 19 branches renovated during 2025. Four came in August alone:

- Bor, announced 03/08.
- Požarevac, announced 07/08. Works run 14/08 to 18/09.
- Belgrade-Rakovica, announced 24/08. Works run 28/08 to 02/10.
- Subotica, announced 26/08. Works run 03/09 to 07/10/2026.

The source for those notices is the bank's own site ([AikBank — Obaveštenje o renoviranju filijale Subotica](https://www.aikbank.rs/vesti/obavestenje-o-renoviranju-filijale-subotica/)).

The 2025 annual report says in its own words that the 2025 renovation standard is now the basis for creating the network. So the device specification is copied site by site, not competed each time. That is why the commercial target is the standard rather than the individual site.

There is also a new development this cycle. Two of the four August notices send customers to third-party dispense-only machines run by an independent deployer. Those machines do not appear in the bank's locator, so they sit outside the 570. A rival's cash-out-only network is filling the gap that the bank's own estate leaves.

The market case beneath this is the strongest in the region. Nationally, cash deposits at machines reached 3,406,129 transactions worth RSD 173.9bn in the second quarter of 2026. That is up 31.9% by count and 53.6% by value year on year. Withdrawal value was flat and withdrawal count fell ([NBS — Payment transactions in the acceptance network](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/platni-sistem/statistika/el_novac/trans_prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)).

One related opening is a funding line. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development approved a EUR 30m dinar factoring credit line on 04/08/2026. It will run through a new digital factoring platform with online applications and real-time status tracking. So a funded digital-channel project sits on the same bank's roadmap ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Where to aim:

- The renovation standard itself, ahead of the next wave of 2026 and 2027 notices.
- The 457 dispense-only machines, as a staged conversion to recycling and deposit machines rather than a single fleet replacement.
- The in-branch device at every renovated site, so that the rival's network only ever carries withdrawals.
- The 63 automated teller safes, as the back-office half of the same conversation.

In short: get the device specification written into the renovation standard this autumn. While that standard goes unchallenged, another site is built to a competitor's specification every two weeks.
drivers: 457 of 570 machines, 80.2%, only pay out cash and cannot take a deposit. This was re-counted from the bank's own feed on 27/08/2026 ([AikBank public ATM/branch locator feed](https://www.aikbank.rs/data/maps-formated.json))

20 branch-renovation notices for 2026 sit in the bank's sitemap, on top of 19 renovations in 2025. Four of them were posted in August alone, with works running into October 2026 ([AikBank — Obaveštenje o renoviranju filijale Subotica](https://www.aikbank.rs/vesti/obavestenje-o-renoviranju-filijale-subotica/))

The bank's own FY2025 report calls the 2025 renovation standard the basis for creating the network. So the device specification is copied at each site rather than tendered again ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md))
Two of the four August notices send customers to a rival's third-party dispense-only machines. These do not appear in the bank's own locator ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md))

Nationally, cash deposited at machines grew 31.9% by count and 53.6% by value year on year in the second quarter of 2026 ([NBS — Payment transactions in the acceptance network](https://www.nbs.rs/export/sites/NBS_site/documents/platni-sistem/statistika/el_novac/trans_prihvatna_mreza.xlsx))
outlooks.rationale:
The refurbishment programme was expected to slow. Instead it sped up. Four new branch notices were posted inside August 2026, taking the year to 20. Each one builds another site to a standard set in 2025 ([AikBank — Obaveštenje o renoviranju filijale Subotica](https://www.aikbank.rs/vesti/obavestenje-o-renoviranju-filijale-subotica/)).

The new fact this cycle is that a competitor's dispense-only network is now being recommended to the bank's own customers during those closures. That changes the argument from a slow upgrade case to defending the branch ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).
cite_ungrounded: The month-on-month conversion run-rate at this bank is a single-observer claim, because the bank's machine feed is overwritten in place rather than archived.
A previously reported supply of 75 machines to this bank remains uncorroborated by any primary source and is deliberately excluded from this call.

outlooks.scope: ZiraatBank BH hiring for card acceptance with its security post unfilled
outlooks.summary:
ZiraatBank BH was the only Bosnian bank with a readable list of job vacancies on 31/08/2026. It is hiring a merchant card-acceptance specialist, and its head of information security and ICT risk post is unfilled ([ZiraatBank BH d.d. — Oglasi](https://ziraatbank.ba/bs/oglasi)). So the bank is building an acquiring business, meaning taking card payments for merchants, while the team that must meet the Federation regulator's binding ICT-risk rules is short of staff.

It has also just published a customer notice announcing cash deposits at its machines. So deposit-capable hardware is already in the estate or has just arrived. The bank holds 74 machines and 1,570 card terminals, and it is not yet on the domestic instant-payment rail. Terminals, terminal management, key management as a service and an instant-payment joining package therefore all point at the same account at the same time.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, from the earliest and most reliable kind of signal: what a bank is hiring for. ZiraatBank BH's own careers page listed nine live vacancies on 31/08/2026. They include a merchant card-acceptance role and an unfilled head of information security and ICT risk. The others are a data-protection officer, a finance director and two branch roles, including a teller ([ZiraatBank BH d.d. — Oglasi](https://ziraatbank.ba/bs/oglasi)).

Separately, the bank published a customer notice titled Nova funkcionalnost – Cash IN na bankomatima. This confirms it has switched on cash deposits at its machines, rather than withdrawals only. So deposit-capable or recycling hardware is already installed or newly upgraded. That makes this bank a live, in-country proof point for the same conversion pitch at its peers. The regulator records it with 74 machines and 1,570 card terminals at 30/06/2026, and it is not an instant-payment participant ([FBA preliminary data 30.06.2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/copy_of_preliminarni_podaci_za_objavu_30062026_GMN.xlsx)).

Two structural facts frame the opportunity. The first is that seven of the thirteen banks headquartered in the Federation report zero card terminals of their own. So acquiring in this market is being built from scratch, not taken from someone else. Card acceptance grew by 3,079 terminals in six months, against just 30 more cash machines. Already 70% of card transactions are contactless ([FBA — Preliminarni podaci o subjektima bankarskog sistema FBiH](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/copy_of_preliminarni_podaci_za_objavu_30062026_GMN.xlsx)).

The second is the Federation Banking Agency's binding decision on ICT-system and ICT-risk management, which has applied since 31/12/2025. Among much else, it requires measures to protect the cryptographic keys that encrypt data at rest and in transit. It also requires incident reporting, resilience testing and oversight of third parties. And it requires a separate external ICT-system audit report, filed with the regulator by 31 March each year. The next one is due 31/03/2027, for all thirteen Federation banks ([FBA — Supervizorska očekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf)). A bank with that duty and no head of information security is the textbook case where key management and security operations get bought as a managed service.

Where to aim:

- The acquiring build: terminals, terminal management and software-based acceptance on merchants' own phones.
- Remote key injection and encryption-key management, framed against the regulator's cryptographic-key requirement.
- The external ICT audit lane. Fieldwork runs from the fourth quarter of 2026 into the first quarter of 2027, and findings land in 2027 budgets.
- An instant-payment joining package, since the bank is still outside the scheme.

In short: lead with acquiring. Attach key management and audit-evidence services to it. Use the bank's own cash-deposit launch as the reference when the same pitch goes to the other six banks with no terminals.
drivers: The nine live vacancies listed on 31/08/2026 include a merchant card-acceptance role. At the same bank, the post of head of information security and ICT risk is unfilled ([ZiraatBank BH d.d. — Oglasi](https://ziraatbank.ba/bs/oglasi))
A published customer notice confirms that cash deposits have been switched on at the bank's machines. So deposit-capable hardware is already in the estate ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

Seven of the thirteen banks headquartered in the Federation report zero card terminals of their own. So acquiring here is a build rather than a fight to displace a rival ([FBA — Preliminarni podaci o subjektima bankarskog sistema FBiH](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/copy_of_preliminarni_podaci_za_objavu_30062026_GMN.xlsx))

The Federation Banking Agency's binding ICT-risk decision has applied since 31/12/2025. It names protection of cryptographic keys explicitly. It also requires a separate external ICT audit report, to be filed by 31/03/2027 ([FBA — Supervizorska očekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf))

Card acceptance is the fastest-growing payment measure in the country. It is up 3,079 terminals in six months, against 30 more cash machines. Terminals in Republika Srpska grew 23.5% year on year ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md))
outlooks.rationale:
Bosnian commercial banks are private and buy outside the public procurement feed. So hiring is often the only forward-looking evidence available. On 31/08/2026 this was the one bank in the country with a countable vacancy list, and it named two buying lanes at once ([ZiraatBank BH d.d. — Oglasi](https://ziraatbank.ba/bs/oglasi)).

The regulatory timetable behind it is fixed, not optional. Audit fieldwork runs into the first quarter of 2027 for a 31 March filing. So positioning has to happen this autumn ([FBA — Supervizorska očekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/1supervizorska_ocekivanja_u_vezi_sa_postupanjem_banaka_u_2026_godini_jzR.pdf)).
cite_ungrounded: Whether acquiring at the seven zero-terminal banks is genuinely absent or quietly outsourced to the domestic card processor is not established.
No procurement, budget or timetable for this bank's acquiring build has been published; the read rests on the vacancy list and the customer notice.

outlooks.scope: Sixteen Bosnian banks still outside the instant-payment scheme before January
outlooks.summary:
Bosnia's domestic instant-payment system went live on 20/07/2026 with three banks and has reached five. That leaves roughly sixteen of the country's twenty-one or so licensed banks outside a scheme they must join by 01/01/2027 ([CBBiH — Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant plaćanja](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

The technical limits are tighter than first understood. Article 15 sets a maximum execution time of 5 seconds, a 7-second scheme timeout and a 10-second hard timeout. So fraud and sanctions screening has to finish inside roughly five seconds. A mobile or electronic-banking app is the only permitted way to start a payment, and single orders are capped at BAM 5,000.

A rolling trigger widens the set of banks that must join every year, rather than closing it in January. Bosnian banks have small in-house change teams and buy from outside. That makes this the largest single opportunity in the market.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, on the shortest deadline in the footprint. The domestic instant-payment rail went live on 20/07/2026 with three banks. It has since added two more, Nova banka on 28/07/2026 and ATOS Bank on 17/08/2026, both from Republika Srpska. So about sixteen of the country's licensed banks are still outside it, four months before the legal date ([CBBiH — Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant plaćanja](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf)).

Two rules in the central bank's rulebook define the work. Article 15 caps the maximum execution time for an instant payment at 5 seconds. It also sets a 7-second scheme timeout and a 10-second hard timeout. This means fraud, sanctions and money-laundering screening must finish inside roughly five seconds, not at batch speed.

Article 13 makes a mobile or electronic-banking app the only permitted way to start a payment. It caps a single order at BAM 5,000. It also reserves QR-code payments to a central-bank specification that has still not been published. So publication would open a second, merchant-facing wave on top of the first connection.

Article 7(2) adds a rolling trigger. Any bank that passes 500,000 combined settlement and giro-clearing transactions in a calendar year must join from 1 July of the following year. So the set of banks that must join widens every year.

Under the platform is a copy of the Italian central bank's instant settlement service. Bosnia and Montenegro are the first two central banks on it. A second onboarding window follows in November 2026 for Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia.

In parallel, and strengthening every conversation, the central bank formally filed Bosnia's application to join the single euro payments area on 06/08/2026. The last precondition had been met on 28/07/2026. It says plainly that commercial banks must align their systems, and that much of that work can only be done after formal admission. It expects first transactions at the earliest six months after admission ([CBBiH — CBBiH zvanično aplicirala za pristupanje SEPA području](https://www.cbbh.ba/press/ShowNews/1808?lang=bs)).

One domestic detail should set the urgency. High-value settlement is still legally tied to old message formats. The Governor may switch it to the ISO 20022 standard on fifteen days' written notice, once all participants are ready. That is the shortest lead time to a live cutover anywhere in the footprint, and far too short to start selling after the notice lands.

Where to aim:

- The sixteen banks outside the scheme. The central bank's joiner announcements are a free, dated pipeline tracker that can be checked monthly.
- The named laggards that are large enough to matter and are confirmed as non-participants. They include the Federation's largest card acquirer, and both units of the group whose Sarajevo bank has the worst cost-to-income ratio among its peers.
- Screening and fraud engines that can answer inside five seconds.
- Hardware security modules, which are secure devices that hold payment keys, plus key management and round-the-clock liquidity monitoring.
- A readiness assessment sold to the slowest banks and to the central bank itself. Every laggard sits on the critical path of the fifteen-day trigger.

In short: package connection, screening and key management as one fixed-scope joiner offer. Sell it monthly against the published joiner list. Be in position before the QR specification lands, not after.
drivers: Roughly sixteen of about twenty-one licensed banks are still outside the scheme, against a legal participation date of 01/01/2027. Only five had joined as at 17/08/2026 ([CBBiH — Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant plaćanja](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf))

Article 15 sets a 5-second maximum execution time, a 7-second scheme timeout and a 10-second hard timeout. So screening must finish inside about five seconds ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md))

Article 7(2) is a rolling trigger. Any bank passing 500,000 settlement and giro-clearing transactions in a calendar year joins from 1 July of the following year. So the set of banks that must join widens every year ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md))

The central bank filed the country's application to join the single euro payments area on 06/08/2026. First transactions are expected at the earliest six months after admission ([CBBiH — CBBiH zvanično aplicirala za pristupanje SEPA području](https://www.cbbh.ba/press/ShowNews/1808?lang=bs))

High-value settlement can be switched to the ISO 20022 message standard on fifteen days' written notice once all participants are ready. That is far too short a runway to begin selling after the notice ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md))

Several sizeable banks are confirmed non-participants. They include the Federation's largest card acquirer, with 265 machines and 11,131 terminals. They also include both units of the group whose Sarajevo bank has the worst cost-to-income ratio among its peers, at 53.8% ([FBA preliminary data 30.06.2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/copy_of_preliminarni_podaci_za_objavu_30062026_GMN.xlsx))
outlooks.rationale:
A full reading of the central bank's rulebook this cycle changed two things that decide what can be sold. The screening budget is 5 seconds under Article 15, not ten. That rules out anything that cannot answer in real time. Article 7(2) also turns a one-off January deadline into a recurring annual intake ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Meanwhile the joiner count moved from three to five in under a month, and the euro-area application was filed on 06/08/2026. So the same small change teams are about to be asked for two programmes at once ([CBBiH — CBBiH zvanično aplicirala za pristupanje SEPA području](https://www.cbbh.ba/press/ShowNews/1808?lang=bs)).
cite_ungrounded: The central bank's QR-code specification has not been published, so the size and timing of the second, merchant-facing wave is not evidenced.

Whether the domestic card processor builds the participant-side gateways for joining banks — and is therefore partner or competitor on this pipeline — is assumed by others rather than demonstrated; its own pages make no claim to the instant-payment role.
The count of about sixteen non-participants is derived from a licensed-bank total stated as twenty-one to twenty-two, not from a published list of banks outside the scheme.

outlooks.scope: Bosnia's deposit-machine conversion as cash in circulation rises
outlooks.summary:
Bosnia's central bank has published the number that makes the case. Of 1,868 installed cash machines, 1,281 only pay out and 567 can take cash in. The deposit-capable count jumped 64% in a single year ([CBBiH — Kartičarstvo u BiH u 2025. godini](https://www.cbbh.ba/content/Archive/1244?lang=bs)).

That conversion is running while the branch network has been frozen at exactly 749 units for two years. Cash outside banks rose 8.56% to KM 7.46bn.

The regulators have now also published fleets bank by bank. That turns market sizing into account planning. Four Federation banks hold 864 of that entity's 1,400 machines, and the two Addiko banks being sold to a new owner have among the widest deposit gaps in the country. Republika Srpska is where to lead, because one payment in five there is still cash, against roughly one in ten in the Federation.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, on a replacement cycle that is already clearly under way, not one that has to be argued for. The central bank's split by device type for 2025 shows 1,868 installed machines. Of those, 1,281 are dispense-only and 567 accept cash in. The deposit-capable count rose from 345 to 567 in a single year, a 64% increase. Bill-payment machines were cut from 128 to 20 ([CBBiH — Kartičarstvo u BiH u 2025. godini](https://www.cbbh.ba/content/Archive/1244?lang=bs)).

Read that last number as a warning, not an opening. Payment kiosks were installed, the mobile app took over the customer journeys, and the fleet was withdrawn. So any kiosk pitch has to beat a proven failure in this market.

Around it, cash outside banks rose 8.56% to KM 7.46bn in 2025. The branch network stayed frozen at exactly 749 units for two years running. Those are the textbook conditions for recyclers, which are machines that pay out the notes customers have just deposited. They cut cash-in-transit journeys and vault holdings.

The fleets are now published bank by bank at 30/06/2026. The Federation's thirteen banks hold 1,400 machines and 28,834 card terminals, with the top four holding 864 machines. Republika Srpska banks hold 490 machines and 12,483 terminals, up from 478 at the end of 2025 ([FBA preliminary data 30.06.2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/copy_of_preliminarni_podaci_za_objavu_30062026_GMN.xlsx)).

Two account-level facts shape the approach. The first is that ownership is changing at four Western Balkans banks. Addiko Bank AD Beograd, Addiko Bank d.d. Sarajevo, Addiko Bank a.d. Banja Luka and Addiko Bank AD Podgorica are being sold to Alta Group d.o.o. of Belgrade, not to Raiffeisen. Closing is expected in the second half of 2027. A transitional-services agreement then runs 12 months from closing, plus a single 12-month extension.
