So services must be re-sourced by roughly the second half of 2028 to the second half of 2029 ([Addiko Group Half-Year Report 1H26](https://www.addiko.com/static/uploads/Addiko-Group-Half-Year-Financial-Report-en-1H26-1.pdf)).

Their deposit gaps are the widest published in the country. Addiko Sarajevo lists 74 machine locations, of which only 25 accept cash. Addiko Banja Luka runs just five cash-accepting machines against roughly 45 cross-listed locations. But buying is frozen until ownership is settled. So this is relationship building now, for a 2027 procurement.

The second fact concerns the country's largest machine operator, with 359 machines and 9,824 terminals in the Federation. It has fresh bond funding on its balance sheet and a network held flat at 85 outlets, inside a group closing branches everywhere else. But its own locator shows 255 machines against the regulator's 359. That gap of 104 must be explained before any estate-sizing proposal goes in front of it. And no published source shows its deposit capability at all ([Raiffeisen Bank dd BiH — Notice to Convene the General Meeting](https://www.raiffeisenbank.ba/content/dam/rbi/retail/eu/ba/Notice%20to%20Convene%20the%20GSM_eng.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

Where to aim:

- Republika Srpska banks first, where 20.0% of payment transactions by count are still cash, against 9.5% in the Federation.
- The 1,281 dispense-only machines, as staged conversion rather than fleet replacement.
- The two Addiko banks, as a relationship built now for a procurement after the sale.
- Republika Srpska's postal operator. Its requirement for money-counting and vacuum banknote-counting machines was tried twice in 2025 and cancelled both times, and it is still unfilled. That is a cheap, shapeable entry before a third attempt is specified ([BiH Public Procurement Portal — Hrvatska pošta Mostar award](https://docs.ejn.gov.ba/Award/1a6b34c6-492b-478b-b609-4fce1f0fc57c.pdf)).

In short: lead the conversion argument on cash-handling economics in Republika Srpska. New deposit capability is spend that does not require displacing anyone's service contract.
drivers: Of 1,868 installed machines, 1,281 are dispense-only and 567 accept cash. The deposit-capable count is up 64% in one year, so the conversion cycle is already running ([CBBiH — Kartičarstvo u BiH u 2025. godini](https://www.cbbh.ba/content/Archive/1244?lang=bs))
Cash outside banks rose 8.56% to KM 7.46bn in 2025, while the branch network stayed frozen at exactly 749 units for two years running ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md))
Republika Srpska is roughly twice as cash-heavy as the Federation, with 20.0% of payment transactions by count still cash, against 9.5% ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md))

Fleets are now published bank by bank at 30/06/2026. Thirteen Federation banks hold 1,400 machines, four of those banks hold 864 of them, and Republika Srpska holds 490 ([FBA preliminary data 30.06.2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/copy_of_preliminarni_podaci_za_objavu_30062026_GMN.xlsx))

The four Western Balkans Addiko banks, including both Bosnian ones, are being sold to Alta Group of Belgrade rather than to Raiffeisen. A transitional-services agreement of 12 months plus one 12-month extension follows a closing expected in the second half of 2027 ([Addiko Group Half-Year Report 1H26](https://www.addiko.com/static/uploads/Addiko-Group-Half-Year-Financial-Report-en-1H26-1.pdf))

The regional rival that services most of the country's machine estate has reported Bosnian revenue down 5% and operating profit down 20%. It is the only footprint country going backwards on both lines ([ASEE Group — Management Report H1 2026](https://asee.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Management-report-on-business-operations-of-ASEE-Group-2026.pdf))
outlooks.rationale:
Two regulators and the central bank published their numbers within a week of each other in August 2026. Together they turn a market-sizing argument into an account plan. The split by device type says 1,281 machines still cannot take a deposit, and the bank-level tables say exactly who owns them ([FBA preliminary data 30.06.2026](https://www.fba.ba/upload/docs/copy_of_preliminarni_podaci_za_objavu_30062026_GMN.xlsx)).

The ownership correction landed in the same window. The Bosnian Addiko banks go to Alta Group, not Raiffeisen. The services timetable is written into the deal documents rather than guessed ([Addiko Group Half-Year Report 1H26](https://www.addiko.com/static/uploads/Addiko-Group-Half-Year-Financial-Report-en-1H26-1.pdf)).
cite_ungrounded: Deposit capability at the country's largest machine operator cannot be derived from any published source, and its own locator disagrees with the regulator by 104 machines.
The incumbent servicer's claim to maintain approximately 1,200 machines in the country rests on vendor copy dated 2020-2021 rather than a current disclosure.
The device-type split of 1,281 dispense-only against 567 cash-accepting is a 2025 national figure and does not map to the bank-level fleet tables published for 30/06/2026.

outlooks.scope: Slovakia's one-euro cashless acceptance duty and the micro-merchant tail
outlooks.summary:
Payment acceptance in Slovakia should grow through the next year, driven by law rather than by bank budgets. Since 1 May 2026 every trader must let a customer pay cashlessly on any sale above one euro. The penalty ladder now runs from a formal instruction, through fines of EUR 3,000 to 40,000, up to the loss of a trade licence ([Slov-lex, Act 384/2025 Z. z.](https://www.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2025/384/20260228.html)).

The catch is that the smallest traders can meet the duty with a QR code and no hardware at all. So the money sits in software and service, not in a mass sale of terminals. That means acceptance software running on ordinary phones. It also means the payment-confirmation layer that the law expressly allows a third party to run. And it means the recurring swaps of credentials and data stores behind the installed base.

Behind that, the tax authority has said the whole national sales-recording platform will be replaced by a new system called SAFE. No go-live year has been published ([Finančná správa SR](https://www.financnasprava.sk/sk/podnikatelia/dane/ekasa)). Aim the line at the acquiring banks and the sales organisations that own merchant books, not at the state.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, but in software and recurring service rather than in hardware. The acceptance duty in section 15(1) of Act 384/2025 Z. z. took effect on 1 May 2026, after Act 30/2026 Z. z. postponed it from 1 March.

The penalty ladder behind it is harder than previously reported. A first detection brings a formal instruction only. A second brings EUR 500-15,000, and each further detection EUR 3,000-40,000. The worst cases count as a particularly serious breach that can cost the merchant its trade licence ([Slov-lex](https://www.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2025/384/20260228.html)).

Section 15(3) expressly allows a third party to supply the technical means that confirms a QR-code payment back to the cash register. The Financial Directorate had still not published the technical specification that duty requires as at 27 August 2026. The service can only start once that specification is published.

Certification is a qualifier to compete, not an advantage. The register of valid certifications at 19 August 2026 carried 65 decisions across 38 companies. Diebold Nixdorf holds two decisions of its own. It also supplies the protected data store, the tamper-evident memory that stores receipts, into a third party's certified stack ([FR SR register](https://www.financnasprava.sk/_img/pfsedit/Dokumenty_PFS/Podnikatelia/eKasa/2026/2026.08.20_Cert_eKASA.pdf)).

Where to aim:

- The small merchants with no terminal, with software-based acceptance on standard phones plus terminal management.
- The acquirers and independent sales organisations who own those merchant books.
- A certified QR payment-confirmation service, ready for the day the specification lands.
- A managed service around the two recurring merchant-side cycles the regulator confirms. Credentials expire every two years, and the protected data store fills up and needs replacement every two to six years.

Watch the competitor tier that never appears in tender data. SONET Slovakia is the Payten presence in this market, rather than Asseco Central Europe. It signed seven public-sector terminal frameworks in the three months to 10 August 2026. Most were published at EUR 0.00 because they are paid per transaction.

Also get a seat at the SAFE consultation table before the specification freezes. The Financial Directorate said on 27 August 2026 only that SAFE will not enter operation in 2026, and named no replacement year.

In short: sell compliance software, the QR confirmation layer and a recurring credential-and-data-store service. Do not let anyone price this as a national terminal refresh.
drivers: The duty to accept a cashless payment on any sale above one euro has been live since 1 May 2026. Repeat breaches now carry EUR 3,000-40,000 fines, with the trade licence at risk in the worst cases ([Slov-lex, Act 384/2025 Z. z.](https://www.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2025/384/20260228.html)).

Section 15(3) lets a third party run the technical means that confirms a QR-code payment back to the cash register. Yet the Financial Directorate had not published the required technical specification as at 27 August 2026. That is a clear legal opening waiting on one document.

Certification is a ticket to compete, not a differentiator. The register held 65 valid decisions across 38 companies at 19 August 2026 ([FR SR register of valid eKasa certifications](https://www.financnasprava.sk/_img/pfsedit/Dokumenty_PFS/Podnikatelia/eKasa/2026/2026.08.20_Cert_eKASA.pdf)).

A full replacement of the national sales-recording platform, called SAFE, is confirmed but has no date. The regulator says only that it is not expected to enter operation in 2026 ([Finančná správa SR eKasa portal](https://www.financnasprava.sk/sk/podnikatelia/dane/ekasa)).

The competitor that quietly wins Slovak public terminal work is SONET Slovakia, the Payten company here. It signed seven frameworks in the three months to 10 August 2026, most at nil published value on a pay-per-transaction model ([Centrálny register zmlúv](https://www.crz.gov.sk/2171273-sk/centralny-register-zmluv/?art_zs2=sonet&art_datum_zverejnenia_od=2025-01-01&art_datum_zverejnenia_do=2026-08-31)).
outlooks.rationale:
Enforcement and architecture moved in the same month. The duty itself has been live since May, but the penalty ladder was only pinned down in the primary legal text this cycle. That is what turns merchant compliance from advisory into urgent.

At the same time, section 15(3)'s explicit permission for a third-party payment-confirmation layer turns a compliance rule into a service somebody has to be paid to run. And the regulator has signalled that the whole national platform is to be rebuilt as SAFE. So the specifications that decide who integrates with what are being written now, not after a tender is published ([Finančná správa SR](https://www.financnasprava.sk/sk/podnikatelia/dane/ekasa)).
cite_ungrounded: No go-live year exists for SAFE, so treating it as a multi-year re-integration and re-certification wave is inference from the signal's implication rather than a published programme.

Describing the micro-merchant tail as un-terminalised follows from the QR-code exemption rather than from any counted figure — the reported rise in the national POS terminal count could not be verified this cycle and is deliberately not quoted anywhere in this outlook.

outlooks.scope: Slovak banks are removing branch cash desks across the market
outlooks.summary:
This is the strongest hardware and managed-service cycle in Slovakia, and it is speeding up. As at 17 August 2026 all five large Slovak banks are removing cash desks from branches. Branches that now have no cash desk:

- Slovenská sporiteľňa: 93 of 128
- Tatra banka: 48 of 69
- ČSOB: 47 of 120
- VÚB: 25 of 121
- UniCredit: 16 of 47

The banks themselves name security rules, staff training and vault equipment as the cost they are escaping ([Techbyte.sk](https://www.techbyte.sk/2026/08/banky-na-slovensku-rusia-hotovostne-pokladnice/)). Every closed desk has to be answered by a machine in the branch lobby that can take money in, not just pay it out.

The base number is now firm. Slovenská sporiteľňa published 733 ATMs, including 296 deposit machines, at the half year. So roughly 437 of its machines are cash-out only, while its branches fell from 140 to 128 in six months ([SLSP v číslach](https://cdn.erstegroup.com/content/dam/sk/slsp/www_slsp_sk/Aktuality/slsp-infografika-2q-2026.pdf)).

None of this is bought through public procurement. So aim the line straight at the least-converted networks, with VÚB and UniCredit first. Aim it also at coin handling, where neither of the two largest banks publishes a product at all.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, and the best-evidenced cycle in the Slovak set. The trigger is dated. As at 17 August 2026 cash desks are being removed across all five large banks. Branches already without a cash desk:

- Slovenská sporiteľňa: 93 of 128
- Tatra banka: 48 of 69
- ČSOB: 47 of 120
- VÚB: 25 of 121
- UniCredit: 16 of 47

The banks name security, training and vault costs as their reason ([Techbyte.sk](https://www.techbyte.sk/2026/08/banky-na-slovensku-rusia-hotovostne-pokladnice/)).

The counts published alongside change how the market should be worked. Slovenská sporiteľňa's half-year figures of 30 July 2026 give 733 ATMs including 296 deposit machines, the largest network in the country. So deposit penetration is already about 40%, and roughly 437 machines are cash-out only. The fleet itself shrank from 752 to 733 in six months, while branches fell from 140 to 128. So branches are shrinking around three and a half times faster than machines ([SLSP v číslach](https://cdn.erstegroup.com/content/dam/sk/slsp/www_slsp_sk/Aktuality/slsp-infografika-2q-2026.pdf)).

VÚB publishes 150 deposit ATMs, banknotes only, inside a network held exactly flat at 163 outlets while headcount falls. That is automation inside the branch rather than closure. Its split between 50-note and 200-note deposits is a clear sign of the hardware generation.

ČSOB Slovakia lists 124 deposit machines at 99 addresses. Of those addresses, 66 accept coins and only 23 are away from a branch. Tatra banka runs 355 deposit machines, handling around 450,000 deposits a month. Seven Slovak banks now operate deposit machines, across a national estate of roughly a thousand.

Where to aim:

- VÚB at 25 of 121 and UniCredit at 16 of 47 are the least converted, so they carry the largest remaining retrofit pipelines. ČSOB Slovakia is third at 47 of 120.
- At Slovenská sporiteľňa the conversation is different. At 40% deposit penetration it is about refresh, managed services and the roughly 437 cash-out-only machines, not new deposit capability.
- Coin deposit is open ground. It is absent from both Slovenská sporiteľňa's and VÚB's published offers, so a coin offer has no existing product to displace.

In short: this is a direct commercial sale of recyclers, deposit machines and the managed cash service around them. It is invisible on the procurement portal because Slovak retail banks sit outside procurement law. Work it account by account on the conversion percentages above.
drivers: All five large Slovak banks were removing branch cash desks as at 17 August 2026. The banks name security rules, staff training and vault equipment as the costs they avoid by doing so ([Techbyte.sk](https://www.techbyte.sk/2026/08/banky-na-slovensku-rusia-hotovostne-pokladnice/)).

Slovenská sporiteľňa's half-year numbers give 733 ATMs, including 296 deposit machines. Its branches fell from 140 to 128, so the fleet is shrinking far more slowly than the branch network ([SLSP v číslach, 1. polrok 2026](https://cdn.erstegroup.com/content/dam/sk/slsp/www_slsp_sk/Aktuality/slsp-infografika-2q-2026.pdf)).
VÚB publishes 150 banknote-only deposit machines while holding its network exactly flat at 163 outlets and cutting headcount. That is automation inside the branch rather than closure.
Neither of the two largest banks publishes a coin-deposit product. A coin-handling offer therefore has no existing product to displace.
Slovak retail banks are private and sit outside procurement law. So none of this pipeline appears in any tender register, and it has to be reached commercially.
outlooks.rationale:
The cycle stopped being a theory and got a base number this month. Until now the argument was that branch closures would eventually force cash automation. What changed on 17 August 2026 is that cash desks are being counted out of branches bank by bank.

On 30 July 2026 the market leader also published fleet and deposit-machine counts precise enough to size the remaining gap at each account ([SLSP v číslach](https://cdn.erstegroup.com/content/dam/sk/slsp/www_slsp_sk/Aktuality/slsp-infografika-2q-2026.pdf)). That turns a general trend into a named retrofit list for each bank. And it lands just as the banks set their 2027 branch-operating budgets.
cite_ungrounded: The framing that every closed cash desk must be answered by a lobby recycler is the signal's own implication, not a bank commitment: no Slovak bank has published a one-for-one replacement plan or a machine order.
The 2027 budget-round timing is a commercial judgement, not a dated fact in any cited signal.

outlooks.scope: ČSOB and 365.bank merger: shared withdrawals, no shared deposits
outlooks.summary:
Slovakia's largest self-service consolidation is under way, and cross-bank deposits are still not part of it. KBC confirmed in its second-quarter report of 6 August 2026 that it completed the EUR 708m purchase of 365.bank on 15 January 2026. It justified the deal partly by cost savings in the branch network ([KBC 2Q2026 quarterly report](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-quarterly-report-en.pdf)).

From 1 July 2026, ČSOB, 365.bank and Poštová banka already share a network of nearly 600 machines. The old EUR 200 cross-bank withdrawal cap has been removed. But that sharing covers withdrawals only, and deposits stay closed to the other banks' customers.

Across the whole market, no Slovak customer can pay cash into an account at another bank. The banks say they are still analysing how to remove the barrier, with no vendor chosen and no date set. Two fleets must now be merged onto one platform ahead of a legal merger in autumn 2026. The software layer that would switch deposits between banks has not yet been specified.
outlooks.projected:
Mixed, and by design: the machine count comes down while spending on integration and software goes up.

ČSOB Slovakia announced on 3 June 2026 that the three banks would share a network of nearly 600 machines from 1 July 2026. Customers of ČSOB, 365.bank and Poštová banka can use it on their own bank's terms. ČSOB contributes 428 machines and 365.bank 176, and the previous EUR 200 cross-bank withdrawal cap was removed. The arrangement covers withdrawals only, and ČSOB's deposit machines stay closed to the other two banks' customers.

The corporate side is now confirmed by the owner. KBC's own second-quarter report of 6 August 2026 records the 98.45% purchase of 365.bank from J&T Finance Group completing on 15 January 2026 for EUR 708m. It created EUR 176m of goodwill and added EUR 3,647m to the Slovak loan book, and integration costs were booked as exceptional in the quarter. The report also notes that 365.bank's distribution rests on a long-standing partnership with Slovak Post ([KBC 2Q2026 quarterly report](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-quarterly-report-en.pdf)).

A legal merger of the two banks was planned for autumn 2026. The target operating model for the combined estate is therefore being decided now.

The unsolved half is market-wide. A Slovenská sporiteľňa spokesperson says on the record that a customer cannot deposit cash to an account at another bank through another bank's machine. VÚB confirms Slovak banks are already analysing how to remove the technical barrier, with no date for doing so ([Finsider.sk](https://www.finsider.sk/ucty/vkladomaty-maju-jednu-nevyhodu-vyuzit-ich-mozu-len-klienti-danej-banky-mohlo-by-sa-to-zmenit/)).

Where to aim: the ČSOB, 365.bank and Poštová banka integration office. The work there is slimming the estate, removing duplicate sites, standardising the surviving machines onto one driving platform, and bringing the postal counter channel onto it.

A separate opportunity is the analysis work behind a national shared-deposit scheme. That needs cross-bank switching, deposit reconciliation, dispute handling and recyclers across the estate. Recyclers are machines that take in deposited notes, check them and pay the same notes back out. Czechia already runs two live shared deposit networks and is one to two years ahead, so it is a ready reference design to put on the table.

The commercial conclusion: engage the merger integration office on the combined estate now, and the wider bank analysis group on deposit switching in parallel. The scheme is still being scoped and nobody has been appointed.
drivers: KBC's second-quarter report of 6 August 2026 confirms the EUR 708m purchase of 365.bank completed on 15 January 2026. It names branch-network cost savings as part of the case ([KBC 2Q2026 quarterly report](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-quarterly-report-en.pdf)).

The shared network of nearly 600 machines has been live since 1 July 2026, with ČSOB contributing 428 and 365.bank 176, and the EUR 200 cross-bank cap removed. It covers withdrawals only ([ČSOB Slovakia press releases](https://www.csob.sk/o-nas/pre-media/tlacove-spravy)).
A legal merger of ČSOB Slovakia and 365.bank was planned for autumn 2026. That puts the target operating model for the combined fleet in play this quarter.

Across the whole Slovak market, deposits remain closed to other banks' customers. VÚB confirms the banks are still analysing how to remove the barrier, and no date is set ([Finsider.sk](https://www.finsider.sk/ucty/vkladomaty-maju-jednu-nevyhodu-vyuzit-ich-mozu-len-klienti-danej-banky-mohlo-by-sa-to-zmenit/)).
365.bank's distribution rests on a partnership with Slovak Post. So a counter channel as well as a machine fleet has to be brought onto the surviving platform.
outlooks.rationale:
The integration timetable started in January, and the owner has now put it on the record. KBC's 6 August 2026 report is the first independent confirmation of the completed purchase, the price and the branch cost-saving motive. It lands while the shared withdrawal network is only weeks old and the legal merger is still ahead ([KBC 2Q2026 quarterly report](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-quarterly-report-en.pdf)).

The commercially useful part is what the banks chose to leave out. Deposit sharing was excluded from the shared network on purpose, and it is still at the analysis stage across the market. So the specification for it has not been written, and no supplier sits inside it yet.
cite_ungrounded: That a national shared-deposit scheme would require cross-bank switching, reconciliation, dispute handling and estate-wide recycler capability is the signal's stated implication, not a published Slovak scheme design — no such programme has been announced.
The autumn 2026 legal merger is reported as planned rather than confirmed as completed, so any sequencing built on it is provisional.

outlooks.scope: Czech regulator orders banks to fix sanctions screening
outlooks.summary:
Demand for financial-crime software in Czechia is clear and funded. The money is there, the regulator has ordered the work, and banks are hiring for it.

The central bank tested 88 sanctions-screening systems at 37 institutions. Sanctions-screening software checks customer names against sanctions lists. The test fed in ten thousand records, both spelled correctly and deliberately misspelled. The central bank reports that the institutions scoring below the market standard are now carrying out the fixes it ordered. Weak screening is treated as breaking the law ([ČNB supervision report 2025](https://www.cnb.cz/export/sites/cnb/cs/dohled-financni-trh/.galleries/souhrnne_informace_fin_trhy/zpravy_o_vykonu_dohledu/download/dnft_2025_cz.pdf)).

At the same time, 38 financial-crime vacancies were open on 31 August 2026 at seven institutions plus the regulator itself. Nearly all were posted in August ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=AML)).

Behind both sits the EU anti-money-laundering regulation. It applies directly from 10 July 2027, but not one binding technical text has been published yet.

The commercial conclusion: aim at the newest institutions, which are building this function from scratch. Sell a rules layer that can be re-pointed once the official text finally arrives.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, and unusually the spend is required rather than optional.

Between March and June 2025 the Czech National Bank ran a market-wide test of 88 sanctions-screening systems at 37 institutions. It fed in ten thousand records, both spelled correctly and deliberately altered. It then sorted the institutions into three categories by how serious the problems were.

In its 2025 supervision report the central bank says the institutions below market standard are now carrying out fixes it ordered. Weak screening is explicitly treated as breaking the law. The common failure was fuzzy name matching, which means catching a sanctioned name even when the spelling is slightly changed. There were also weaknesses in customer due diligence, which means checking who a customer is. Looking into transaction-monitoring alerts and screening the full ownership structure of corporate clients were also weak ([ČNB supervision report 2025](https://www.cnb.cz/export/sites/cnb/cs/dohled-financni-trh/.galleries/souhrnne_informace_fin_trhy/zpravy_o_vykonu_dohledu/download/dnft_2025_cz.pdf)).

The market is hiring to match. A search on 31 August 2026 found 38 open anti-money-laundering vacancies, nearly all posted that month. Fio banka had three financial-crime roles. Penta Bank's Czech branch posted both a Head of AML and Fraud Monitoring and an anti-fraud team leader on the same day. Banka CREDITAS, ČSOB, UniCredit Czechia, PAYMONT and the central bank itself were also hiring ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=AML)).

A second wave is waiting behind this. The regulator assessed 251 crypto-licence applications and granted only 11 on 1 July 2026. Most failed on governance, anti-money-laundering and technology controls.

The European layer makes the sale stronger, not weaker. The Anti-Money-Laundering Regulation applies directly from 10 July 2027. Yet no Commission delegated or implementing act had reached the Official Journal as at 27 August 2026. The customer-due-diligence and occasional-transaction standards are still unfinished, against a legal deadline the new authority has already missed.

Four more consultations are still open. Two of them close on 3 and 20 September 2026. A third closes on 27 September 2026, and the last on 6 October 2026 ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

Where to aim: the smaller and newer institutions building the function from nothing, such as Penta Bank's Czech branch and Banka CREDITAS. They buy a platform, not just staff. The established banks are a tuning-and-fixing conversation instead.

Sell screening, transaction monitoring and case management as one configurable rules layer that can be re-pointed when the binding text arrives. Every bank is currently planning against drafts.

In short: the budget is committed and the people are already hired, so the tooling decision falls within the next two quarters. Go in on fuzzy-matching quality and alert handling, which is exactly what the regulator measured.
drivers: Institutions that scored below market standard in the central bank's screening test are now carrying out the fixes it ordered. Weak screening is treated as breaking the law ([ČNB supervision report 2025](https://www.cnb.cz/export/sites/cnb/cs/dohled-financni-trh/.galleries/souhrnne_informace_fin_trhy/zpravy_o_vykonu_dohledu/download/dnft_2025_cz.pdf)).

The measured weakness was fuzzy name matching across ten thousand correctly and deliberately misspelled records. Investigating alerts and screening corporate ownership structures were also weak. All of these are product problems a vendor can solve directly.

38 financial-crime vacancies were open on 31 August 2026 at seven institutions plus the regulator, nearly all posted that month. Penta Bank's Czech branch hired both a financial-crime head and an anti-fraud team lead on the same day ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=AML)).

The EU Anti-Money-Laundering Regulation applies directly from 10 July 2027. Not one binding technical text had reached the Official Journal as at 27 August 2026, so every bank is planning against drafts ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

A second licensing wave is waiting behind the 251 crypto applications the regulator assessed and the 11 it granted on 1 July 2026. Most rejections were about governance, anti-money-laundering and technology controls.
outlooks.rationale:
Two separate pieces of evidence arrived in the same week and point the same way. The regulator's own supervision report turns a market survey into written orders that named institutions must carry out. That is funded demand, not a guess.

The jobs market confirms it from the other side. Seven institutions plus the central bank were staffing financial-crime teams within a single month ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=AML)). Tooling decisions follow the hiring by a quarter or two, and the 2027 planning round that pays for them opens now.
cite_ungrounded: The institutions under imposed remedial measures are not named by the regulator, so no specific bank can be said to be under order — the link between a named hiring institution and the test results is inference.
That tooling purchases follow hiring by one to two quarters is a commercial rule of thumb, not something any cited signal states.

outlooks.scope: ČSOB is hiring for an international card-acquiring platform in Prague
outlooks.summary:
A new buying centre for card acceptance has appeared in Czechia, and it is being built quickly. ČSOB posted five card-acceptance vacancies in August 2026, all in Prague and all at a senior level. They are a business architect for international acquiring on 28 August, an IT process manager, a business development manager, an application engineer and a card-scheme manager. That is five of the fifteen hits for this skill across the whole Czech job market ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=acquiring)).

Its owner KBC raised its full-year guidance on 6 August 2026 and named higher technology costs as a driver. It has set 11 February 2027 for an investor event on its digital transformation ([KBC 2Q2026 company presentation](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-company-presentation.pdf)).

The Czech state rents card acceptance instead of buying terminals. The route to market is therefore the acquirer, which is the bank that processes card payments for merchants, and never the ministry. Vendor choices are usually settled once the architects are in post, so the time available to engage is short.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, concentrated in one account and on a short timetable.

ČSOB has five open card-acceptance vacancies at once, every one posted in August 2026 and every one in Prague:
- business architect for international acquiring, 28 August
- IT process manager for international acquiring, 21 August
- business development manager for acquiring, 24 August
- application engineer for acquiring, 14 August
- card-scheme manager, 6 August

An anti-money-laundering process manager is posted alongside them. That is a third of all national demand for the skill inside one bank ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=acquiring)).

Hiring a business architect and an IT process owner together means a platform is being built, not a gap being filled. The work touches card acceptance end to end: the acquiring platform, the merchant terminal estate, terminal management and remote update, and the security modules behind the stack.

The owner's numbers frame the budget. KBC reports the Czech unit at 4.3m clients and 196 branches at 30 June 2026, essentially unchanged for four quarters and carrying 24% of group assets. It raised full-year guidance on 6 August 2026 and named higher technology costs as a driver of rising costs. It has fixed 11 February 2027 for a dedicated investor event on digital transformation that will reset guidance ([KBC 2Q2026 company presentation](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-company-presentation.pdf)).

Two market facts shape how anything terminal-shaped is sold here.

First, the Czech state does not buy terminals. The Interior Ministry bought electronic banking through loaned terminals from Česká spořitelna against a CZK 48,000,000 framework ceiling on 30 June 2026. The Ministry of Defence's framework for card acceptance through loaned terminals lists 88 terminals in service and closed on 14 August 2026. Prague Castle's four-year card-acceptance contract, estimated at CZK 40,000,000, was still unawarded on 27 August 2026. So hardware and terminal management must be sold to the acquiring bank, never to the agency ([NEN — Prague Castle cashless payments solution](https://nen.nipez.cz/verejne-zakazky/detail-zakazky/N006-26-V00015946)).

Second, the tax deadline that everyone is selling against is not a hardware requirement. The sales-recording law known as EET 2.0 passed its third reading on 15 July 2026. Cash-register certificates will be generated in the tax portal from 1 November 2026. A pilot month runs from 1 January 2027, and full operation starts from 1 February 2027. Yet the Finance Ministry says in its own words that no new cash-register equipment is needed, and it is giving the smallest traders a free application ([Finanční správa ČR](https://www.financnisprava.cz/cs/financni-sprava/media-a-verejnost/tiskove-zpravy-gfr/tiskove-zpravy-2026/financni-sprava-zahajuje-technickou-pripravu-k-eet)).

Where to aim: first, ČSOB's acquiring build, for terminals, terminal management, remote over-the-air update and the security modules. Second, the acquirers and independent sales organisations whose existing terminal estates must be made compliant by February 2027. Third, as competitor intelligence rather than pipeline, the Prague city ICT operator's CZK 250,000,000 payment-gateway procurement, whose winner becomes a first-rank Czech payments competitor.

In short: get in front of the architects during the next two quarters. Compete on remote update and fleet compliance, not on the price of a box, because a local rival is already giving the hardware away.
drivers: Five Prague-based card-acceptance vacancies at ČSOB were all posted within four weeks in August 2026. They are led by a business architect for international acquiring on 28 August, and together they make up a third of national demand for the skill ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=acquiring)).

KBC raised full-year guidance on 6 August 2026 and named higher technology costs. It holds the Czech unit flat at 196 branches and has set 11 February 2027 for an investor event that resets group targets ([KBC 2Q2026 company presentation](https://wcmassets.kbc.be/content/dam/kbccom/doc/investor-relations/Results/2q2026/2q2026-company-presentation.pdf)).

The Czech state rents card acceptance rather than buying terminals. Loaned-terminal awards at the Interior Ministry and a closed Defence framework listing 88 terminals show this. So the acquirer, not the public buyer, is the customer for hardware ([NEN — Prague Castle cashless payments solution](https://nen.nipez.cz/verejne-zakazky/detail-zakazky/N006-26-V00015946)).

The EET 2.0 tax timetable is fixed. Certificates start on 1 November 2026. A pilot month runs from 1 January 2027, and full operation begins on 1 February 2027. But the Finance Ministry says no new equipment is needed, so the money is in compliance software and remote fleet update ([Finanční správa ČR](https://www.financnisprava.cz/cs/financni-sprava/media-a-verejnost/tiskove-zpravy-gfr/tiskove-zpravy-2026/financni-sprava-zahajuje-technickou-pripravu-k-eet)).
A local challenger is already competing on free hardware. Its terminal-plus-cash-register campaign of 17 July 2026 offers free rental, a built-in printer, a data SIM and automatic remote updates.
outlooks.rationale:
The buying centre did not exist a month ago. ČSOB posted five acquiring roles within four weeks, the most senior on 28 August 2026. That is the clearest sign in the Czech market this cycle that a merchant-acquiring platform is being designed rather than maintained ([Jobs.cz](https://www.jobs.cz/prace/?q%5B%5D=acquiring)).

It comes at the same time as a fixed tax deadline that forces every existing terminal estate to be made compliant by February 2027. The owner has also publicly accepted higher technology costs and booked an investor event to explain them.
cite_ungrounded: That vendor and platform choices freeze once the architects are in post is a commercial judgement about how such programmes run, not a statement in any cited signal.
No published scope, budget or timetable exists for the ČSOB acquiring programme itself — the evidence is entirely the five vacancies and the owner's cost commentary.

outlooks.scope: 944 shared Czech ATMs still cannot accept a deposit
outlooks.summary:
Czechia's four-bank shared ATM network has been measured machine by machine for the first time, and the gap it shows is the target base. A fresh pull of the scheme's own map feed on 27 August 2026 returns 1,913 pooled machines. Of these, 969 can take deposits and 944 can only pay cash out. The worst-covered fleets are at MONETA, where 311 of 541 machines are cash-out only, and Air Bank, at 254 of 373 ([Komerční banka](https://www.kb.cz/cs/o-bance/tiskove-zpravy/ke-sdilenym-vkladovym-bankomatum-se-pripojuje-unicredit-bank-klienti-komercni-banky-nove-vlozi)).

Demand is clearly there. January 2026 alone carried over 155,000 shared deposits worth nearly two billion koruna. In the rival three-bank camp, the number of deposits is growing roughly twice as fast as their value. That means more, smaller deposits per machine, which strains cassette capacity and refilling.

This is a retrofit and recycler-replacement population reachable through four owners at once. Recyclers are ATMs that re-use deposited notes. It is not a programme anyone has announced. Sell cash forecasting and the managed cash service alongside the machines, not after them.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, spread across four owners rather than concentrated in one tender.

The scheme's own map data feed, pulled again on 27 August 2026, returns 1,913 pooled machines. 969 accept deposits and 944 can pay out but not take in. The split by owner is:
- Komerční banka: 740 machines, 475 deposit and 265 cash-out
- MONETA: 541 machines, 230 deposit and 311 cash-out
- Air Bank: 373 machines, 119 deposit and 254 cash-out
- UniCredit: 259 machines, 145 deposit and 114 cash-out

Komerční banka's own half-year report separately gives 1,916 shared machines at 30 June 2026, down 31 year on year, and 745 of its own, down 19. So the pool is shrinking slightly while deposit capability spreads across it. The programme to move duplicate machines is nearly finished, with 119 of 124 target municipalities served ([Komerční banka H1 2026 results](https://www.kb.cz/getmedia/efba2b93-dcc9-4284-ab1f-ef48426b0c3e/KB-Results-2Q2026-CZ.pdf)).

UniCredit joined the deposit side on 16 February 2026 with 144 machines, and the network-wide limit for a single deposit rose to CZK 350,000. January 2026 alone carried over 155,000 shared deposits worth nearly CZK 2bn.

The rival camp of Česká spořitelna, ČSOB and Raiffeisenbank went fully live with its own cross-bank deposit service on 16 September 2025 across more than a thousand machines. It credits an account at another bank typically within thirty minutes. There, the number of deposits is rising far faster than their value: up 15% against 8% at one bank and 12.5% against 4.5% at the other. That means more and smaller deposits per machine. It puts direct pressure on cassette capacity, note-handling reliability and refill scheduling.

Where to aim: MONETA first. It has the largest measured gap, and it is the Czech bank whose stated plan of automating first and removing tellers second matches the offer. But its reported 2026 hardware programme rests on a single unattributed article of 16 August 2026. That programme covers sixteen machines re-mixed to dispense the CZK 5,000 note, about twenty more coin machines, and more than half its branches without over-the-counter cash. It must be checked with the bank before it is used in a pitch. Air Bank comes next, on the same retrofit logic.

Treat the Czech ATM estate as actively contested. Komerční banka hosted the first installation of a competitor's newest dispenser generation at its own headquarters in December 2025. It is cutting branches at 8.6% a year while finishing a core-banking migration. It also loses the board member who owns digitalisation and technology on 30 September 2026. That makes the following two quarters the right time to approach ([Diebold Nixdorf DN Series launch](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/diebold-nixdorf-unveils-dn-series-300-and-350-transforming-self-service-banking-302630180.html)).

One correction to carry into planning: the central bank does publish its cash-machinery contracts openly on its own E-ZAK register. Coin-processing technology is held by Giesecke+Devrient and maintenance of its coin machines by KMX BT Praha. So monitoring that portal is worthwhile, and the maintenance contract is the nearest realistic re-tender ([ČNB E-ZAK contracting profile](https://ezak.cnb.cz/contract_index.html)).

In short: work the 944 named cash-out-only machines as a retrofit list through four owners in parallel. Lead with cash forecasting and managed refilling, because the deposit-mix data says the operating problem is already here.
drivers: The scheme's map feed, pulled again on 27 August 2026, shows 1,913 pooled machines, of which 944 cannot accept a deposit. The gap is concentrated at MONETA (311 of 541) and Air Bank (254 of 373) ([Komerční banka](https://www.kb.cz/cs/o-bance/tiskove-zpravy/ke-sdilenym-vkladovym-bankomatum-se-pripojuje-unicredit-bank-klienti-komercni-banky-nove-vlozi)).

Shared deposits are already at scale: over 155,000 deposits worth nearly CZK 2bn in January 2026 alone. The network-wide limit for a single deposit was raised to CZK 350,000 when UniCredit joined on 16 February 2026.

In the rival three-bank camp the number of deposits is growing roughly twice as fast as their value. So machines are handling more and smaller deposits, which is the pattern that strains cassette capacity and refill scheduling.

Komerční banka is cutting branches 8.6% year on year and its own fleet by 19 machines while finishing a core-banking migration. Its digitalisation and technology board seat falls vacant on 30 September 2026 ([Komerční banka H1 2026 results](https://www.kb.cz/getmedia/efba2b93-dcc9-4284-ab1f-ef48426b0c3e/KB-Results-2Q2026-CZ.pdf)).

A competitor placed its newest dispenser generation at Komerční banka's headquarters as a launch installation in December 2025. It is pitching monitoring, predictive maintenance and cash forecasting rather than the machine itself ([Diebold Nixdorf DN Series launch](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/diebold-nixdorf-unveils-dn-series-300-and-350-transforming-self-service-banking-302630180.html)).
outlooks.rationale:
The single biggest open question about the Czech shared network was how many pooled machines can actually take money in. This cycle it was answered by counting them. That turns a general point about deposit automation into a named, located retrofit population of 944 machines under four owners.

It arrives alongside evidence that deposit volumes per machine are already straining the cash cycle. The timing is also unusually clear. Komerční banka's technology board seat falls vacant on 30 September 2026, and whoever fills it resets the vendor picture ([Komerční banka H1 2026 results](https://www.kb.cz/getmedia/efba2b93-dcc9-4284-ab1f-ef48426b0c3e/KB-Results-2Q2026-CZ.pdf)).
cite_ungrounded: The MONETA 2026 hardware programme — the CZK 5,000 denomination re-mix on sixteen machines, roughly twenty additional coin machines and the branch cash-desk withdrawal — rests on a single unattributed article of 16 August 2026 and was not re-verified by any other agent; it is flagged as untested in the outlook itself.
That a launch pilot at a top-tier bank normally precedes a fleet rollout within one to two years is an industry rule of thumb carried from the signal's implication, not a stated Komerční banka plan.
No shared-network deposit-retrofit programme has been announced by any of the four owners; the 944 machines are an addressable base, not a pipeline.

outlooks.scope: Slovenia's money-laundering evaluation and the data spending it drives
outlooks.summary:
Slovenia is under international follow-up for financial-crime weaknesses whose root cause is data, and its banks are hiring for exactly that. The Council of Europe evaluation body published Slovenia's sixth-round assessment on 7 July 2026 and placed the country in enhanced follow-up. It found some improvement in risk assessment, but significant remaining gaps on terrorism financing, held back by missing data.

Two European deadlines now fall within a year. National supervisors, including Banka Slovenije, had to send data to the new EU anti-money-laundering authority by 15 August 2026. The provisional list of entities eligible for direct European supervision is expected at the end of September 2026 ([AMLA](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

Meanwhile Addiko Slovenia has been running a cluster of three data roles, and Delavska hranilnica posted a data-governance specialist on 25 August 2026. The commercial conclusion: sell one combined fix-it programme into the 2027 budget round, not two.
outlooks.projected:
Growth through the 2027 budget round, with the buying decision still ahead of the spend.

The evaluation published on 7 July 2026 placed Slovenia in enhanced follow-up. It recorded moderate improvement in risk assessment but significant remaining gaps on terrorism financing, all held back by missing data. That is a statement about the quality of evidence, not about policy.

The European layer now has dates from the source. National supervisors, Banka Slovenije included, had to send their data to the EU anti-money-laundering authority by 15 August 2026. The provisional list of eligible obliged entities is expected to be final at the end of September 2026. The first selection for direct European supervision must start by 1 July 2027 and finish within six months, with supervision itself from 2028. The eligibility test is operating in at least six Member States including the home state, which catches the cross-border groups active in Slovenia ([AMLA](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

Slovenia has reported full transposition measures for the 2025 tranche. So unlike some neighbours it is not fighting a late national rulebook. But the directly applicable EU regulation still takes effect on 10 July 2027.

No binding technical text had reached the Official Journal as at 27 August 2026. Further consultations close on 3 and 20 September 2026. Two more close on 27 September and 6 October 2026 ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

The demand evidence is on the hiring side. Addiko Slovenia ran three data roles at the same time: a data engineer, a data-governance analyst and a data analyst. It also ran two group risk roles. Delavska hranilnica posted a data-governance specialist on 25 August 2026.

Three data roles at once is a platform build, not a gap being filled. It is also happening inside a bank whose new owner will plan a data-estate migration in 2027. NLB's own technology deck names artificial intelligence at scale for anti-money-laundering as a board-level programme.

Where to aim: transaction monitoring and sanctions screening with evidence of calibration. Also electronic know-your-customer to close onboarding data gaps, and the management reporting that produces the evidence the evaluators say is missing.

Sell this at NLB, Addiko Slovenia and Delavska hranilnica as a single regulation-plus-evaluation fix-it programme in the September to December 2026 planning window. Because no binding technical standard exists yet, the offer that survives the final text is a configurable rules layer, not a hard-coded monitoring flow.

In short: one programme, one budget line, pitched now while the banks are still hiring rather than buying.
drivers: Slovenia was placed in enhanced follow-up by the sixth-round mutual evaluation of 7 July 2026. It found significant gaps on terrorism financing, with missing data named as the underlying cause.

The EU anti-money-laundering authority's selection pipeline has dates. Supervisor data was due on 15 August 2026, and a provisional list of eligible entities is expected at end-September 2026. The first selection starts by 1 July 2027 ([AMLA](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

Slovenian banks are hiring for exactly the capability the evaluators found missing. Addiko Slovenia ran three data roles at once, and Delavska hranilnica posted a data-governance specialist on 25 August 2026.

The directly applicable EU regulation lands on 10 July 2027, while no binding technical text had been published as at 27 August 2026. So any tool bought now must be re-pointable when the standards arrive ([AMLA regulatory instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

NLB names artificial intelligence at scale for anti-money-laundering as a board-level programme in its own technology material. So the largest bank has already chosen a direction, if not yet a supplier.
outlooks.rationale:
The evaluation has now been joined by firm European dates and by visible hiring. That is what turns a compliance finding into a purchase.

Supervisors filed their data on 15 August 2026, and the list of entities facing direct European supervision is expected within weeks. So cross-border groups operating in Slovenia are being sorted right now ([AMLA](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)). Banks are still building teams rather than platforms, so a combined programme can still be shaped rather than merely answered.
cite_ungrounded: No Slovenian bank has published a procurement, budget or timetable for financial-crime tooling; the demand evidence is hiring plus a regulatory calendar, which is a leading indicator rather than a pipeline.
Reading three simultaneous data roles as a platform build rather than backfill is the signal's own interpretation and is not confirmed by the bank.

outlooks.scope: NLB's cash-light branch format and the equipment it needs
outlooks.summary:
Slovenia's largest bank has a funded, board-level programme to move cash out of its branches, and it is already doing it. In the first half of 2026 NLB opened three new branches in Slovenia on its cash-light concept. One has a deposit system that lets companies pay in their daily takings. The bank says the self-service deposit network was expanded further ([NLB Group interim report](https://www.nlbgroup.com/content/dam/nlb/nlb-group/documents/investor-relations/financial-reports/2026/h1/NLB-Group-Interim-Report-January%E2%80%93June-2026.pdf)).

Cash transactions in branches have fallen from 32% at the end of 2023 to 13.5% in March 2026, against a target below 10% by 2030. The number of Slovenian branches went up, not down. So this is an estate being refitted, not closed. The economics back this up: group card and ATM fee income grew 6% while the matching cost grew 11%.

The commercial conclusion: aim at the repeatable branch specification, at a managed-service answer to that margin squeeze, and at the accessibility evidence now required in every Slovenian public tender.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, because the cash-light branch format is itself an equipment specification that the bank keeps repeating.

NLB's investor material states verbatim an ATM and cash-deposit-system network upgrade at group level driving cash out of branches. Upgraded machines and more deposit systems give customers instant sight of what they pay in. Alongside this is a cash-at-point-of-sale rollout that moves withdrawals to merchant tills ([NLB Investor Day payments deck](https://www.nlbgroup.com/content/dam/nlb/nlb-group/documents/investor-relations/dan-vlagateljev-2026/NLB%20IRD%20PAYMENTS.pdf)).

Retail cash transactions in branches fell from 32% at the end of 2023 to 15.1% at the end of 2025 and 13.5% in March 2026. The 2030 target is below 10%.

In the first half of 2026 in Slovenia specifically, the bank opened three new cash-light branches, one with a deposit system for company daily takings. It reported the corporate deposit network further expanded. Slovenian branches went from 69 to 70, even as the south-east European subsidiaries lost sixteen. This is a stable estate being refitted, not closed ([NLB Group interim report](https://www.nlbgroup.com/content/dam/nlb/nlb-group/documents/investor-relations/financial-reports/2026/h1/NLB-Group-Interim-Report-January%E2%80%93June-2026.pdf)).

The commercial pressure shows in the accounts. Group card and ATM fee income rose 6% to EUR 71.965m in the first half, while the matching expense rose 11% to EUR 48.851m. So net income on that line actually fell about 1.5%. That is the usual trigger for an outsourcing or managed-services conversation. It sits against a stated technology budget of EUR 160-200m under the bank's 2030 strategy, and a clear preference for vendors that fit into its own delivery model.

There is a costed proof point on the demand side. NLB won a three-year contract to receive a pharmacy chain's daily cash takings at EUR 102,028.50, 48% below the estimate. It holds similar cash-handling and day-and-night-safe lots elsewhere. So it has taken on third-party cash duties at prices it must now defend behind the counter.

Where to aim: first, the repeatable cash-light branch specification, as a recurring order for recyclers, deposit systems and teller automation. Recyclers are ATMs that re-use deposited notes. Second, a managed-service and monitoring offer aimed squarely at the 11%-against-6% cost line.

Third, the merchant side of the same account. NLB has enabled fully online paperless ordering of any terminal type, completed a single-terminal multi-activity set-up for a large merchant, and is partnering with fiscal cash-register providers. But the acquiring core is run by the shared processor Bankart, so entry is through hardware, cash-register integration and value-added services. NLB's part in the European digital-euro pilot from the second half of 2027 also gives a dated reason to open a terminal-readiness conversation.

Two boundaries to respect. The accessibility act amended in February 2026 makes accessibility a mandatory technical specification in Slovenian public tenders, and it can even be added to a tender already running. So every machine offered to a public or state-owned buyer must carry the evidence ([Uradni list RS 14/2026](https://www.uradni-list.si/glasilo-uradni-list-rs/vsebina/2026-01-0563)).

The central bank's banknote-sorter maintenance was awarded elsewhere on 21 August 2026 for six years. So the central-bank cash-processing tier is closed and must not be chased ([TED 495378-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/495378-2026/xml)).

In short: treat NLB as a recurring equipment-plus-service account with a published cost problem, and bring the accessibility documentation to every conversation.
drivers: NLB opened three cash-light branches in Slovenia in the first half of 2026, one with a deposit system for company daily takings. It reports the self-service deposit network further expanded ([NLB Group interim report](https://www.nlbgroup.com/content/dam/nlb/nlb-group/documents/investor-relations/financial-reports/2026/h1/NLB-Group-Interim-Report-January%E2%80%93June-2026.pdf)).

Branch cash transactions fell from 32% at the end of 2023 to 13.5% in March 2026, against a 2030 target below 10%. This sits under a group programme the bank calls a cash transition ([NLB Investor Day payments deck](https://www.nlbgroup.com/content/dam/nlb/nlb-group/documents/investor-relations/dan-vlagateljev-2026/NLB%20IRD%20PAYMENTS.pdf)).

Card and ATM fee income grew 6% to EUR 71.965m while the matching expense grew 11% to EUR 48.851m. That squeezed the net line by about 1.5%, which is the standard precondition for an outsourcing or managed-services tender.
The bank has a stated technology budget of EUR 160-200m under its 2030 strategy. It also has a clear preference for vendors that fit into its cross-functional delivery model.

Accessibility became a mandatory technical specification in Slovenian public procurement when the amended act took force on 25 February 2026. It can be applied to tenders already under way ([Uradni list RS 14/2026](https://www.uradni-list.si/glasilo-uradni-list-rs/vsebina/2026-01-0563)).
outlooks.rationale:
The half-year report of 6 August 2026 moved this from a strategy slide to a completed fact. Three cash-light branches opened in Slovenia in six months, a corporate deposit system was installed in one of them, and the deposit network grew. All of this happened while the Slovenian branch count rose ([NLB Group interim report](https://www.nlbgroup.com/content/dam/nlb/nlb-group/documents/investor-relations/financial-reports/2026/h1/NLB-Group-Interim-Report-January%E2%80%93June-2026.pdf)).

At the same time the accounts show the cost of running cards and machines growing nearly twice as fast as the income from them. That is the point at which a bank starts listening to a service offer rather than only a hardware quote.
cite_ungrounded: NLB has published no per-branch equipment order, unit count or timetable for the cash-light format; reading each new branch as a recurring machine order is the signal's implication rather than a disclosed plan.

The draft Slovenian cash-access bill is in negotiation with the banks and could add cash points, but its density parameters are contested between agents and none is quoted here or usable with a customer.
The fleet figure of roughly 508 machines circulating for NLB in Slovenia is press-tier rather than bank-disclosed, so it is not relied on in this call.

outlooks.scope: Card skimming reported at OTP Slovenija's 384-machine fleet
outlooks.summary:
Slovenia's second-largest bank has told its own customers that criminals are copying cards at its machines. That creates reactive budget available now.

On 6 August 2026 OTP banka Slovenija published a security notice saying it has recently detected card abuse at its ATMs through skimming. Skimming is a device fitted over the card slot that copies the magnetic stripe, while a hidden camera or a doctored keypad captures the PIN ([OTP banka](https://www.otpbanka.si/v-otp-banki-v-zadnjem-obdobju-zaznavamo-primere-zlorab)).

The same week, its group half-year figures showed the Slovenian bank cutting branches from 74 to 69 in six months, the largest absolute cut anywhere in the group. Its fleet barely moved, from 390 to 384 machines.

The estate is a merged Nova KBM and SKB fleet running two legacy vendor stacks, with branches closing far faster than machines. That is the standard precondition for a deposit and recycler upgrade programme. There is a named board owner for digital and operational business to take both to.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, with two spend triggers arriving at the same account in the same week.

On 6 August 2026 the bank published a public security notice. It says it has recently been detecting payment-card abuse at its machines through skimming. It describes both the card-slot copying device and the hidden camera or overlaid keypad used to capture the PIN, and tells customers to check the slot and keypad before use. It says it monitors card security together with partners, and it names no locations, machine models or case numbers ([OTP banka](https://www.otpbanka.si/v-otp-banki-v-zadnjem-obdobju-zaznavamo-primere-zlorab)).

That is reactive budget: anti-skimming detection modules, card-slot and keypad hardening, camera shielding, and card-fraud transaction monitoring. There is also a consulting angle on switching off magnetic-stripe fallback and hardening chip-based authorisation, because skimming only pays where the stripe still works.

The second trigger is structural. The group half-year network table shows the Slovenian bank going from 74 to 69 branches and 390 to 384 machines between 31 December 2025 and 30 June 2026. Point-of-sale terminals fell from 13,001 to 12,830 and headcount from 2,117 to 2,100. That is the largest absolute branch cut in the whole group, against a fleet that barely moved ([OTP half-year report](https://www.otpbank.hu/apps05/capital-market/api/getPublicationFile?token=72F1DFA1AEDBB713B47C000000000079F847A02D44BC72F1DFA1AEDB)).

The bank reports first-half net profit of EUR 128m on total assets of EUR 15.7bn. It also reports the integration of its asset-management arm and a new operating model based on value streams. So the organisation is being redesigned at the same time.

A merged Nova KBM and SKB fleet carries two legacy vendor stacks. Branches closing at nearly 7% in six months while machine numbers hold is exactly the pattern that comes before a recycler and cash-deposit upgrade. A decommissioning and redeployment workstream normally sits behind it.

Where to aim: Vojko Božiček has been on the management board for digital and operational business since 14 January 2025. He is the single entry point who owns both the fraud response and the estate. Lead with the skimming hardening, because it is immediate and undeniable. Use it to open the fleet standardisation and deposit-capability conversation behind it.

The supervisory backdrop helps that second conversation. The European supervisor's letter of 7 July 2026 requires significant institutions to file an action plan with their supervisory team by 31 October 2026. Among other things, the plan must name replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies. The European supervisory authorities extended the same governance expectation to nationally supervised banks on 31 July 2026 ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

In short: go in this quarter on anti-skimming and stripe hardening, and turn it into the two-stack consolidation and deposit-upgrade discussion while the operating model is still being redrawn.
drivers: The bank publicly confirmed on 6 August 2026 that it is detecting card skimming at its own machines. It advised customers to check the card slot and keypad before use ([OTP banka](https://www.otpbanka.si/v-otp-banki-v-zadnjem-obdobju-zaznavamo-primere-zlorab)).

Its network went from 74 to 69 branches and 390 to 384 machines in six months, the largest absolute branch cut in the whole OTP group. So the fleet is being kept while the branches go ([OTP half-year report](https://www.otpbank.hu/apps05/capital-market/api/getPublicationFile?token=72F1DFA1AEDBB713B47C000000000079F847A02D44BC72F1DFA1AEDB)).
The estate is a merged Nova KBM and SKB fleet that carries two legacy vendor stacks. That is a standardisation and decommissioning problem before it is a purchasing one.
At the same time, the bank is redesigning itself around a new value-stream operating model. It reported first-half net profit of EUR 128m on total assets of EUR 15.7bn.
A single named board member has owned both digital and operational business since 14 January 2025. So the fraud response and the estate decision sit with the same person.

The European supervisor's 31 October 2026 action-plan deadline explicitly names replacing legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technology. It was extended to nationally supervised banks on 31 July 2026 ([ECB letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
A bank that publishes a skimming warning to its own customers has already accepted that its machines are the problem. That is a different conversation from a planned refresh.

The notice landed on 6 August 2026. It came within a day of the group network table. That table shows the same bank cutting branches faster than anywhere else in its group, while holding its machine count almost flat ([OTP half-year report](https://www.otpbank.hu/apps05/capital-market/api/getPublicationFile?token=72F1DFA1AEDBB713B47C000000000079F847A02D44BC72F1DFA1AEDB)).

Reactive fraud money is available immediately. It opens the door to the larger two-stack consolidation while the operating model is still being redrawn.
cite_ungrounded: The bank names no locations, machine models or case numbers in its skimming notice, so the scale of the affected population is unknown and no fleet-wide retrofit size can be inferred from it.
That skimming only pays where magnetic-stripe fallback remains enabled, and the resulting stripe-disable consulting angle, is the signal's own reasoning rather than a statement by the bank.

Whether OTP banka Slovenija falls inside the significant-institution population addressed by the 31 October 2026 letter, or inside the nationally supervised tier the supervisory authorities extended it to, is not established in the cited signals.

outlooks.scope: Montenegro: instant payments live at all eleven banks
outlooks.summary:
Montenegro moved its whole banking sector onto instant payments in one step on 20 July 2026. The same obligations now apply to all eleven banks. They must run a free, compulsory check that the payee's name matches the account number. They must settle within ten seconds, and as a rule those payments cannot be recalled. A regulator-imposed cap of five euro-cents applies to domestic transfers up to EUR 200. The cap removes the fee income those payments used to earn ([CBCG — Instant placanja, TIPS Clone](https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/instant-placanja-tips-clone)).

A second wave already has dates. It covers QR acceptance at the till, payment to a mobile number instead of an account number, and request-to-pay, from March 2027 to March 2028.

Expect strong growth in real-time fraud and sanctions screening, payee-name matching and round-the-clock managed operations. The same package can be sold eleven times in a market of 633,000 people. Aim at the small banks with thin in-house technology teams, and at the dated phase-two channel builds. Lead with cost to serve, because the five-cent cap has removed the margin on small payments.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, and unusually predictable because the regulator has published the calendar.

The Central Bank of Montenegro put the TIPS Clone platform into production on 20/07/2026. This is a national copy of the European Central Bank's instant settlement service. It was built with Banca d'Italia on an EUR 8m World Bank credit. Every one of the eleven licensed banks went live at once: Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Lovcen, NLB, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad banka and Ziraat ([CBCG — Instant placanja](https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/instant-placanja-tips-clone)).

Three obligations came with it. Verification of Payee, a check that the name on a transfer matches the account it is going to, is compulsory and free to the customer. It is enforced by fines of EUR 10,000 to EUR 40,000, in line with EU Regulation 2024/886. The rail cannot be reversed and must deliver funds within ten seconds. That is why the central bank had to warn the public about a phishing wave pretending to be the central bank only two days after go-live. An overnight batch review cannot stop a payment that has already settled.

A Council Decision of 17/07/2026 capped the fee on a domestic instant transfer up to EUR 200, started by mobile or internet banking. The cap is five cents on each side, against a previous average of 32 cents.

First official volumes, published 13/08/2026, were 56,678 transfers worth EUR 21.53m in twelve days of July. The average ticket was EUR 380. The regulator reported a five-fold rise from launch day to month end.

The next wave has published dates. The programme's own terms of reference commit to phase III adoption across Q4-2026 to Q1-2027. Phase IV overlay services follow from March 2027 to March 2028. They name QR merchant acceptance and request-to-pay, with a mobile-number alias directory and preparation for cross-border SEPA Instant alongside.

Where to aim: the four smaller banks the signals name as thin on in-house capacity are Adriatic, Zapad banka, Universal Capital and Ziraat, with Lovcen alongside them. Offer them a packaged real-time monitoring, payee-matching and 24/7 operations service. Approach CKB, NLB and Erste for the phase-two QR and alias builds, since their own mobile apps rate below 2.8 out of 5. The licensed non-bank PrestoPay, authorised since 14/10/2024 for payment initiation and account information, already outranked every bank app in the country on 31/08/2026 ([CBCG — Registar platnih institucija](https://www.cbcg.me/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_platni_promet/registar/platne/reg_prestopay.pdf)). Approach the whole sector for the permanent operations load of running three national payment systems side by side, one of which has no maintenance window at all.

Conclusion: sell the same instant-payments compliance and operations package eleven times before the March 2027 overlay window opens. Use the five-cent cap as the cost-to-serve argument under every self-service conversation in the market.
drivers: All eleven banks went live on the same day, 20/07/2026, so every institution carries the same obligation on the same clock ([CBCG — Instant placanja](https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/instant-placanja-tips-clone)).
Verification of Payee is compulsory and free, enforced by fines of EUR 10,000-40,000. Funds must reach the payee within ten seconds or be returned without delay.
The Council Decision of 17/07/2026 caps the fee on sub-EUR-200 instant transfers at five cents each side, against a previous average of 32 cents. That removes fee income on small payments.
A regulator-committed overlay window runs March 2027 to March 2028 for QR merchant acceptance and request-to-pay. Phase III adoption runs in Q4-2026 to Q1-2027.

Bank mobile channels score poorly. Four domestic incumbents rate below 2.5 out of 5. The licensed payment institution PrestoPay outranked every bank app on 31/08/2026 ([CBCG — Registar platnih institucija](https://www.cbcg.me/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_platni_promet/registar/platne/reg_prestopay.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
Montenegro has moved from preparing instant payments to operating them. Until 20/07/2026 instant payments here were a programme. Since then they are a live, irreversible, round-the-clock obligation at every bank at the same time. There is also a price cap that makes the old fee model unrecoverable, and a published date for the next wave of overlay services ([CBCG — Instant placanja](https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/instant-placanja-tips-clone)).

So one compliance deadline has already passed, one revenue line has already been removed, and a second deadline is already dated. That is why the next two quarters are the buying window rather than 2027.
cite_ungrounded: The description of Adriatic, Zapad banka, Universal Capital, Ziraat and Lovcen as thin on in-house technology capacity is the signal's own characterisation, not a disclosed headcount or budget figure from those banks.
The claim that an overnight batch review cannot stop an already-settled instant payment is our own explanation of the mechanism rather than a sourced statement by the regulator.

outlooks.scope: Montenegro: 538 cash machines cannot accept deposits
outlooks.summary:
Montenegro's central bank counted 664 cash machines at the end of March 2026, and only 126 of them can accept a deposit. The gap sits mainly at five named banks ([CBCG — device census Q1-2026](https://www.cbcg.me/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_platni_promet/usluge_e-novac/2026/broj_uredjaja_prihvatanje_platnih_kartica_q1-2026.zip)).

Demand is growing quickly on the deposit side. Deposits at machines grew 47% by count year on year, while withdrawals grew 5%. Roughly EUR 2.9bn of business cash a year still arrives at a bank counter.

Banks have started acting on their own. CKB has removed cash from the counters of a flagship Podgorica business centre. Prva banka has switched on its first seventeen deposit machines and says more phases are coming. Hipotekarna has hired a specialist specifically to plan ATM expansion.

Expect strong growth in recyclers (ATMs that re-use deposited notes), deposit-module retrofits, multivendor machine software and managed field services. Work it as five bank conversations, not a market campaign.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, and the sizing is unusually solid because the regulator's count and a bottom-up rebuild from the banks' own locators agree to within 3.5%.

The Q1-2026 device census published 07/05/2026 counts 664 cash machines, of which only 126 accept a deposit, leaving 538 withdrawal-only. Deposit-capable machines have risen every single quarter since end-2024. Unlike the total fleet, they never fall back in winter. So deposit capability is permanent estate rather than seasonal ([CBCG — device census Q1-2026](https://www.cbcg.me/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_platni_promet/usluge_e-novac/2026/broj_uredjaja_prihvatanje_platnih_kartica_q1-2026.zip)).

Rebuilt from nine banks' own published locators on 27/08/2026, four-fifths of the national gap sits at five institutions. NLB Podgorica has 124 withdrawal-only machines of 153, Prva banka 92 of 109, CKB about 87 of roughly 117, Erste 69 of 81 and Hipotekarna all 49.

Deposit demand is building underneath them. Machine deposits ran at 127,719 worth EUR 42.7m in Q1-2026, against 86,798 worth EUR 28.9m a year earlier. Withdrawals grew 5% over the same period.

The largest volume is still at the counter. Over-the-counter cash orders were still worth EUR 5.77bn in 2025, of which companies and entrepreneurs deposited EUR 2.95bn. That is roughly seventy times the value machines took in a quarter.

The named triggers have dates. CKB reopened its Podgorica Business Point on 24/07/2026 with no cash at the counters at all, and a transition window closing around 24/01/2027. It had already paid EUR 20 each to the first 500 customers who deposited at a machine and never used a teller ([CKB — Business Point](https://www.ckb.me/opste/novosti-detalj?nid=723)). Prva banka launched deposits at seventeen named sites on 09/06/2026, and its digital transformation director said publicly that further phases follow ([Prva banka CG](https://www.prvabankacg.com/saopstenja_detalji.php?id=244)). Hipotekarna advertised a dedicated ATM specialist on 17/06/2026, whose published duties include planning network expansion and renewing vendor contracts. The post appears to have been filled ([Hipotekarna banka](https://hipotekarnabanka.com/oglas-za-posao-atm-specijalista-u-sluzbi-za-prihvat-platnih-kartica-eftpos-atm-i-ecommerce/)).

NLB Podgorica sits inside a group-level ATM and cash-deposit-system upgrade named at NLB's Investor Day of 07/05/2026. It is the subsidiary with the group's second-worst cost-to-income ratio, at 51.5% ([NLB Group Investor Day 2026](https://www.nlbgroup.com/content/dam/nlb/nlb-group/documents/investor-relations/dan-vlagateljev-2026/NLB%20IRD%20PAYMENTS.pdf)).

Competitive timing matters. ASEE reported on 31/07/2026 that its Payten cash-machine deliveries fell in the half specifically in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro. So the contest is over the refresh cycle rather than the whole relationship ([ASEE Group H1-2026 management report](https://asee.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Management-report-on-business-operations-of-ASEE-Group-2026.pdf)).

Where to aim: NLB Podgorica and the group transformation office together, since the mandate is group-level. CKB for lobby capacity to absorb the counter cash it has just moved out. Prva banka for phase two of a rollout the bank has already announced. Hipotekarna as a straight deposit-module upsell on an entirely withdrawal-only estate. Erste for extending its branded Smart Cash format beyond the eleven sites where it exists. And NLB and Erste jointly for the 23 surviving day-and-night safes, a small self-contained replacement that does not require winning a whole fleet first.

Conclusion: work the recycler gap as five named conversations, anchored on the counter cash each bank is trying to move. Also settle the open question of whether Lovcen's 78 Euronet-branded locations are an outsourced fleet or merely acceptance partners before spending effort there.
drivers: 538 of 664 machines cannot take a deposit, and the gap is concentrated at five named banks: NLB, Prva banka, CKB, Erste and Hipotekarna ([CBCG — device census Q1-2026](https://www.cbcg.me/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_platni_promet/usluge_e-novac/2026/broj_uredjaja_prihvatanje_platnih_kartica_q1-2026.zip)).
Machine deposits grew 47% by count year on year, against 5% for withdrawals, all handled by 126 machines.

Businesses still deposit about EUR 2.95bn of cash a year at bank counters. CKB has begun removing counter cash outright, with a transition closing around 24/01/2027 ([CKB — Business Point](https://www.ckb.me/opste/novosti-detalj?nid=723)).
Prva banka switched on seventeen deposit machines on 09/06/2026 and has said further phases are planned ([Prva banka CG](https://www.prvabankacg.com/saopstenja_detalji.php?id=244)).
The fleet swings by roughly 90 to 110 machines between the winter low and the summer peak. That suits a recurring deploy, service and remove contract rather than a one-off sale.

ASEE said on 31/07/2026 that Payten cash-machine deliveries fell in Montenegro in the first half, opening a refresh-cycle window ([ASEE Group H1-2026](https://asee.io/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Management-report-on-business-operations-of-ASEE-Group-2026.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
