Three things came together this cycle. The regulator's own count and an independent rebuild from nine bank locators now agree on the size of the gap and, for the first time, on where it is. Three banks have taken dated, public actions in the same quarter that all create deposit demand they cannot currently absorb.

The third change is the five-cent cap on small instant transfers, imposed on 17/07/2026. It means no bank in the market can protect margin by pricing. It can only cut the cost to serve, which is the automation case stated in the regulator's own terms.
cite_ungrounded: The comparison that counter cash deposits are roughly seventy times the value machines took in a quarter is our own arithmetic on the two sourced figures (EUR 2.95bn a year at the counter against EUR 42.7m at machines in Q1-2026), not a ratio published by the central bank.

Whether Lovcen banka's 78 Euronet-branded locations are an outsourced fleet or merely fee-free acceptance partners is explicitly unresolved in the underlying evidence and is stated here as an open question.

outlooks.scope: Albania: counter cash deposits are eleven times the ATM estate
outlooks.summary:
The Bank of Albania's own forms show that branch counters took cash deposits worth ALL 783.7bn in the first half of 2026. The whole ATM estate took ALL 68.6bn. Businesses made up 73% of the counter deposit value ([Bank of Albania — teller cash form](https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/F3_dhe_F4_T2_shqip_34625.xlsx)).

Banks are still opening branches, not closing them, so this is demand for branch fit-out. The largest banks are already converting. Raiffeisen runs 30 self-service zones with dual-currency deposit machines inside the country's biggest branch network, and has committed in writing to modernise its fleet further. BKT renewed its fleet in 2018, so its normal replacement window falls in 2026-2028.

One regulatory condition governs the whole opportunity. No customer-operated machine certified for the lek is yet approved to check note fitness, which is whether a note is in good enough condition to re-use. So nothing on the market can legally recycle Albanian banknotes.

Expect growth in teller recyclers, self-service zone build-out and assisted kiosks. Submitting a machine for fitness certification is the step that unlocks it.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, but dependent on one certification that can be submitted.

The demand evidence is primary data from the regulator, not inference. Over-the-counter cash transactions in H1-2026 reached 3,357,815 items worth ALL 1,170.8bn. Deposits alone were 2,279,914 items worth ALL 783.7bn. ATM deposits in the same half were 1,378,900 items worth ALL 68.6bn. So the counter takes 11.4 times the cash-deposit value of the whole machine estate, and businesses are 73% of it ([Bank of Albania — Form 3 teller cash transactions](https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/F3_dhe_F4_T2_shqip_34625.xlsx)).

Paper transactions are the other half of the same counter workload. In H1-2026, 3,250,200 paper credit transfers worth ALL 2,477.9bn crossed counters. That is a third of transfers by count but 62% by value.

The branch estate this lands on grew to 408 branches at end-2025 from 400, the highest since 2021. About 46% of them are in Tirana, so a single-city pilot is cheap.

Named catalysts are already moving. Raiffeisen's 2025 annual report, re-read on 27/08/2026, records 197 machines after 14 additions and the largest branch network in the country at 74 outlets. It has 30 self-service zones with cash-deposit machines and dual-currency lek and euro machines. Hybrid branches with reduced cash hours make up 28% of the network, and branch payments fell 16% year on year. The report also contains a word-for-word commitment to keep investing in modernising the fleet and expanding self-service centres in urban areas ([Raiffeisen Bank Shqiperi, Raporti Vjetor 2025](https://www.raiffeisen.al/content/dam/rbi/retail/eu/al/about-us/annual-reports/RBAL-Annual_Report-2025_Final.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf)).

BKT, the largest bank with a 24% share, installed 164 machines across 2025, including 30 off-site. It reports that machine deposits are four-fifths of all its cash deposits. It has completed 35 branches under its Project EASY rebuild across 2024-2025, and states a 2026 aim of removing routine cash transactions from branches. Its fleet was fully renewed in 2018, which puts the replacement decision in the 2026-2028 window ([BKT Annual Report 2025](https://www.bkt.com.al/assets/uploads/documents/AR-2025-EN/mobile/index.html)).

The regulatory condition is explicit and dated. The Bank of Albania's list of customer-operated banknote-handling machines tested for the lek, republished on 10/07/2026, carries only two entries. Both are marked as unable to sort notes by fitness. Fitness checking is the regulatory condition for returning deposited lek to circulation. So today every deposit must be re-sorted on a staff-operated machine, and no customer machine in Albania can lawfully recycle notes ([Bank of Albania — tested banknote-handling machines](https://www.bankofalbania.org/Paraja/Qarkullimi_i_parase/Makinerite_e_trajtimit_te_kartemonedhave/)).

Where to point it: Raiffeisen first, because it has itself named further self-service expansion. It is also looking for a qualified digital-signature provider to close its last paper step, a gap it has described publicly and which is contested. Then BKT, for the branch rebuild and the 2026-2028 fleet decision. Also approach BKT about the arrangement with the state postal operator that it discloses, which would be a public procurement. Then Credins, for the ATM and terminal modernisation it names as a 2025-2026 focus.

The Bank of Albania itself is the fourth target. Its procurement register carries maintenance lots closing on 09/09/2026 and 11/09/2026, and it openly invites foreign bidders on its equipment buys ([Bank of Albania — tender notices](https://www.bankofalbania.org/Rreth_Bankes/Njoftime_p_e_r_tendera/)).

Conclusion: put a fitness-capable customer-operated machine through central-bank testing as the first move. That certification is what turns an ALL 783.7bn counter-deposit argument into a recycler proposal that is legal to make.
drivers: Counter cash deposits reached ALL 783.7bn in H1-2026, against ALL 68.6bn at the whole ATM estate. Businesses made up 73% of counter value ([Bank of Albania — Form 3](https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/F3_dhe_F4_T2_shqip_34625.xlsx)).
Paper credit transfers still ran at 3,250,200 items worth ALL 2,477.9bn in H1-2026. That is 62.1% of transfer value crossing a counter on paper.
Branch numbers are rising, not falling: 408 at end-2025 from 400, with about 46% in Tirana. So this is demand for fit-out, not for closing branches.

Raiffeisen commits in its own annual report to further fleet modernisation and self-service expansion, across 197 machines and 30 existing self-service zones ([Raiffeisen Bank Shqiperi 2025](https://www.raiffeisen.al/content/dam/rbi/retail/eu/al/about-us/annual-reports/RBAL-Annual_Report-2025_Final.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf)).

BKT's fleet was fully renewed in 2018, which puts replacement in the 2026-2028 window. A branch rebuild already covers 35 sites ([BKT Annual Report 2025](https://www.bkt.com.al/assets/uploads/documents/AR-2025-EN/mobile/index.html)).

No customer-operated machine on the central bank's tested list can check note fitness. So recycling lek notes is currently blocked at the regulatory level ([Bank of Albania — tested machines list](https://www.bankofalbania.org/Paraja/Qarkullimi_i_parase/Makinerite_e_trajtimit_te_kartemonedhave/)).
outlooks.rationale:
The measurement changed this cycle. Until now the case for branch automation in Albania rested on inference. The Bank of Albania's H1-2026 forms, published on 14/08/2026, now measure the counter flow directly. They show it is more than eleven times the machine estate, while branches keep opening.

At the same time, the central bank's certified-machine list, republished on 10/07/2026, shows the fitness column empty for every customer-operated entry. That turns a general product ambition into one clear, submittable regulatory step. That step unlocks the whole recycler conversation.
cite_ungrounded: The statement that no customer-operated machine in Albania can lawfully recycle lek is our reading of the central bank's tested-machine list combined with the fitness requirement; the list itself records only that both certified entries lack fitness capability.
Whether Bank of Albania's scanning-systems maintenance lot covers cheque or banknote imaging is explicitly unknown in the source and is not asserted here.

outlooks.scope: North Macedonia: digital identity re-verification and the 2027 wallet duty
outlooks.summary:
North Macedonia's national mobile electronic identity, OneID, is now live at seven banks. On 25/08/2026 it was reported to be issuing consumer loans of up to about EUR 42,000 from start to finish with no branch visit ([OneID — Novosti](https://www.oneid.mk/news.nspx)).

The scheme's own rules create permanent work that banks cannot avoid. The identity expires after two years, can live on only one device, and allows a customer data update only once a month. So every bank that adopts it faces a recurring wave of re-verification across its whole customer base.

Behind that sits a legal duty, from 1 June 2027, for banks to accept registered European digital identity wallets. That is six months ahead of the EU's own derived date.

Expect growth in remote onboarding, electronic know-your-customer checks, liveness checks (proof that a real person is present) and audit trails, relying-party verification and the screening behind it. Three named banks are still outside the national scheme, and they are the target list.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, with a legal backstop that makes the budget non-optional.

OneID was built by the clearing house KIBS with Nextsense under the KibsTrust qualified-trust brand. It was registered as the first Macedonian electronic identity scheme in December 2021.

It has since moved through the top tier of the market. Komercijalna and Halkbank joined in October 2022, and Sparkasse in November 2022. ProCredit and Triglav followed in April 2024, then Silk Road Bank in September 2024. NLB Banka joined in March 2025 and the state Central Register in June 2025. Stopanska followed in January 2026. That leaves UNIBanka, TTK Banka and ALTA banka Bitola outside it as at 27/08/2026 ([OneID — Novosti and Partneri](https://www.oneid.mk/news.nspx)).

The scheme's mechanics are what create recurring demand. The electronic identity is valid for two years and must be renewed. It can be active on only one device, and it needs biometric authentication on a reasonably recent handset. Updates through it are capped at once per month. That cap limits throughput, and is itself the argument for assisted in-branch and self-service re-verification capacity. Stopanska already runs client updates with OneID as a standing free service and accepts no other identity app ([Stopanska banka](https://www.stb.com.mk/naselenie/digitalno-bankarstvo/azuriranje-na-klient-so-oneid/)).

The commercial ceiling moved on 25/08/2026. Komercijalna was reported to be issuing fully remote consumer loans up to MKD 2,600,000, roughly EUR 42,000, with an immediate decision. That is a competitive floor every peer now has to match.

The legal layer sits behind that. The law transposing the EU's second electronic identification regulation applies from 1 June 2027. Mirroring the EU text, it applies to private relying parties, meaning businesses that rely on the identity check. Micro and small enterprises are excluded. Those that demand strong authentication for online identification must accept registered European digital identity wallets when the user asks. Banking and financial services are named expressly.

Implementing bylaws are due within six months of entry into force ([European Commission — North Macedonia Report 2025](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/267b368e-6b55-4a42-bb72-6395593de4da_en?filename=north-macedonia-report-2025.pdf)). Only the draft bill text was verified, so the adopted gazette wording is not proven to carry the date unchanged. The penalty schedule in that law falls on wallet issuers, not on banks, so do not pitch on the fines.

A parallel identity-related workload is already binding. Since 1 March 2026 banks must apply strong customer authentication to online card payments through an in-app approval rather than an SMS code. Tokenised cards rose 137.5% year on year to 353,863 by March 2026 ([NBRSM — safer online payments from 1 March 2026](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-27022026.nspx)).

Where to point it: Komercijalna, Stopanska and NLB Skopje for re-verification capacity at scale, since they have the largest customer bases against a once-a-month update cap. ProCredit Skopje is a separate case, because its banking app is built in-house by the group's own IT subsidiary. Identity, electronic signature and liveness are bought from local qualified providers market by market, so that slot is a genuine vendor selection.

UNIBanka, TTK Banka and ALTA banka Bitola are the three banks with no national identity scheme at all. UNIBanka's extraordinary shareholders' meeting of 24/09/2026 on the use of 2025 profit is a dated moment to time an approach. Also approach the Ministry for Digital Transformation during the six-month bylaw window, when the technical requirements are shaped.

Conclusion: sell the recurring re-verification wave now, and the wallet-acceptance layer into H1-2027 budgets. Treat the three banks outside OneID as the short list rather than the whole market.
drivers: OneID is live at seven banks and the state Central Register. Its two-year expiry, one-device rule and once-a-month update cap force recurring re-verification ([OneID — Novosti and Partneri](https://www.oneid.mk/news.nspx)).
Komercijalna was reported on 25/08/2026 to be issuing fully remote consumer loans up to roughly EUR 42,000 through OneID. That sets a competitive floor for peers.

A legal duty on bank relying parties to accept European digital identity wallets applies from 01/06/2027. Bylaws are due within six months of entry into force ([European Commission — North Macedonia Report 2025](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/267b368e-6b55-4a42-bb72-6395593de4da_en?filename=north-macedonia-report-2025.pdf)).

In-app strong customer authentication has been mandatory since 01/03/2026. Tokenised cards grew 137.5% year on year to 353,863, pulling key management and fraud analytics with them ([NBRSM](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-27022026.nspx)).
UNIBanka, TTK Banka and ALTA banka Bitola are the three banks still outside the national scheme. UNIBanka has a dated capital-allocation meeting on 24/09/2026.
outlooks.rationale:
The scheme has moved from adoption to operation. With Stopanska joining in January 2026, it covers almost the whole top tier. The 25/08/2026 report of end-to-end remote lending at EUR 42,000 tickets shows banks are now pushing real value through it, not just piloting.

That turns the scheme's own expiry, single-device and monthly-update rules into a permanent operating load. It arrives just as the 1 June 2027 wallet-acceptance duty forces the same teams to build a second identity path. So the design decisions are being taken in the next two quarters, not in 2027.
cite_ungrounded: The 01/06/2027 application date and the wallet-acceptance article were verified only in the draft government bill; the adopted gazette text was not obtained, so it is not proven the provision survived unchanged.
The description of the three non-participating banks as a target list is our framing; none of them has published an intention to join OneID.

outlooks.scope: Kosovo: 292 dispenser-only machines and a 45% rise in terminals
outlooks.summary:
Kosovo's central bank published card-usage data on 14/08/2026. It shows the card-acceptance estate jumping 45% in a year to about 30,300 terminals. The ATM fleet grew only 8% to 686 machines, and just 394 of them can accept a deposit. So the deposit-capable share actually fell, and the cash-in gap widened to 292 machines ([CBK — Perdorimi i kartelave ne Kosove](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf)).

The value split matters as much as the counts. Deposits at machines carry 32.1% of all card-transaction value on those 394 units, while terminal payments carry 17.8%. So the highest-value work in a euroised, cash-heavy economy runs on the smallest and least-equipped part of the estate. Branch building has stopped at 234 units, which turns a build market into a refit market.

Expect strong growth in recyclers and deposit retrofits, terminal estate management and key injection (loading security keys into terminals), and managed field services. Work it bank by bank against a firm machine-certification requirement.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth on two fronts, each sized separately.

The central bank's August-2026 card report, covering data to 31/12/2025, shows card-accepting terminals reaching about 30,300 from 20,913 a year earlier. That is roughly 9,400 deployed in twelve months, the largest single movement in Kosovo's payment infrastructure.

The machine fleet grew only 8% to 686. Of these, 394 accept a deposit and just 57 can start a credit transfer. Because dispensers were added faster than deposit-capable units, the deposit-capable share fell from 59.4% to 57.4% ([CBK — card usage report](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf)).

Monthly data to June 2026, published 07/08/2026, show both flows still speeding up. Machine deposit counts were up 14.0% year on year, withdrawals up 10.5% and terminal payments up 47.0% ([CBK Monthly Statistics Bulletin](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CBK_MSB_297_En.pdf)).

The same bulletin confirms the branch estate flat at 234 units since March 2026, after peaking at 237 in August 2025. So the roughly 35 units opened since 2022 are a refit base for teller recyclers rather than a build pipeline. Teller recyclers are machines at or behind the counter that accept notes and pay them out again, so tellers stop counting by hand.

One qualification requirement governs every machine proposal here and must be checked before any bid. The Regulation on Cash Operations has been in force since 01/02/2024. It says machines used to check the authenticity and fitness of euro banknotes may only be put into use once they have passed Eurosystem testing. They must also appear on the European Central Bank's published list, and the requirement extends explicitly to customer-operated machines. About 20.65 million banknotes, 33.23% of everything banks deposited in 2025, were classified unfit ([CBK — Rregullore per operacionet me para te gatshme](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Rregullore-per-operacionet-me-para-2023.pdf)).

Where to point it: BKT Kosova first. It already runs deposit-capable machines with a cardless code-based cash-in flow for businesses, and shows the only rising property-and-equipment line in the peer set. Then TEB, whose 83 to 87 machines against 35 branches carry no deposit language anywhere on its own estate pages. TEB also buys cash-handling machines on an annual cycle reopening around May-June 2027.

Raiffeisen Kosovo is the country's largest bank by loans, with 185 machines against 37 branches. There, getting deposit-capability data is a first step rather than a refinement, because its locator shows no such field. ProCredit Kosovo has a 29-site estate, small enough to replace in one or two awards. It already buys uninterruptible power supplies and cash bags that a single availability contract would absorb. Banka per Biznes shortens counter hours at its North Mitrovica branch from 14/09/2026, and buys guarding, cash-in-transit and ATM management as one outsourced bundle.

The central bank itself is also a target. Its cash-processing machine maintenance procedure was cancelled on 10/08/2026 after its single bid failed the responsiveness test. That leaves the machine without a contracted provider, and a re-tender is expected ([BQK cancellation notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/DPK_Njoftim_anulim_Furnizim_Mirembajtje_BQK26057234.pdf)).

There is a counter-pressure to note. A national tap-to-phone programme run by the Banking Association with Visa is steering micro-merchant acceptance onto ordinary Android phones. That reduces demand for terminal hardware, but not for onboarding, device management, key injection or hardware-security-module protection behind a phone-based PIN.

Conclusion: lead with the 292-machine deposit gap and the refit case at 234 frozen branches. Sell the terminal wave as estate management rather than boxes. Confirm Eurosystem testing for every machine before it is proposed.
drivers: 292 of 686 machines cannot take a deposit and 629 cannot start a transfer. The deposit-capable share is falling year on year ([CBK — card usage report](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Perdorimi-i-kartelave-ne-Kosove.pdf)).
Machine deposits carry 32.1% of all card-transaction value, against 17.8% for terminal payments. So the highest-value flow runs on the least-equipped estate.
About 9,400 terminals were added in twelve months, a 45% expansion. They all start their refresh clock together and need estate management, key injection and monitoring now.

The branch estate has been flat at 234 units since March 2026, after peaking at 237. That turns a build market into a refit market ([CBK Monthly Statistics Bulletin](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CBK_MSB_297_En.pdf)).

Under the Regulation on Cash Operations, every proposed machine must already appear on the Eurosystem's tested-machine list. That is a qualification step before any bid ([CBK cash operations regulation](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Rregullore-per-operacionet-me-para-2023.pdf)).

The central bank's cash-processing maintenance procedure was cancelled on 10/08/2026 because no bid was responsive. The machine is left unmaintained and a re-tender is expected ([BQK cancellation notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/DPK_Njoftim_anulim_Furnizim_Mirembajtje_BQK26057234.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
The numbers moved hard, and in opposite directions, in the same publication cycle. Acceptance grew 45% in one year, while the fleet added dispensers faster than deposit-capable units. So the cash-in gap is widening even as deposit demand grows 14% a year. The branch series confirms the estate stopped expanding in March 2026.

Two dated openings landed on top of that in August 2026. Banka per Biznes shortens counter service from 14/09/2026. A central-bank cash-machine maintenance procedure was left with no provider. That is why the conversation is now about converting a countable installed gap rather than forecasting one.
cite_ungrounded: Raiffeisen Kosovo's locator exposes no deposit-capability field, so the national cash-in-gap argument cannot yet be aimed at that specific bank; the 185-machine figure is a first-party locator count, not a bank disclosure.
TEB publishes no budgets and no award notices, so its cash-handling and ATM-services cycle is dated but unsized.
Whether the national tap-to-phone roadshow continued past 25/05/2026 is contested between agents and is not asserted here.

outlooks.scope: Albania: instant payment go-live moved to November 2026
outlooks.summary:
Albania was due to join the Western Balkans instant-payment platform in July 2026. It is now in the second onboarding window in November. The Governor restated this on 05/08/2026 as fully operational within November at the latest ([Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone goes live](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

The delay does not reduce the work, so it is the selling window rather than relief. Every bank must fund round-the-clock payment operations, plus sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening at instant speed. Each also needs real-time fraud monitoring, hardware security module capacity, and a phone-number-to-account lookup with a payee-name check. All of this must land inside one quarter.

A newly adopted electronic identity and digital wallet law removes the legal blocker behind remote enrolment and qualified signature. Expect strong growth in payments integration, screening and channel work, aimed at banks whose 2026 budget is not yet committed.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, squeezed into a single quarter.

Banca d'Italia announced on 20/07/2026 that its TIPS Clone platform went live with Bosnia and Montenegro first. TIPS Clone is a standalone copy of the European Central Bank's instant settlement service, built for the Western Balkans. A second onboarding window in November 2026 is expected to bring in the central banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia ([Banca d'Italia](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

Governor Gent Sejko said at the 05/08/2026 monetary-policy briefing that the project is in its closing implementation phase. He said it should be fully operational within November, at the latest by end-November. He put the savings at up to ALL 35bn a year for the financial system and ALL 38bn for the economy. The Bank of Albania's own National Payment System Committee minutes of 16/12/2025 record Banca d'Italia's original July 2026 target, so November is a slip of roughly four months.

Two design features drive most of the work. Transfers can be addressed by mobile phone number instead of account number, which needs an alias directory. And a Verification of Payee check confirms the account belongs to the named payee before the payer confirms. The platform settles in local currency in central-bank money and in euro in commercial-bank money, so there are two separately screened flows to reconcile.

Be honest about the limits of the deadline. There is no Bank of Albania press release, no day-level date, and no published list of participating commercial banks or bank-side legal obligation. So this is Governor-driven urgency rather than a legal duty on banks.

The surrounding volumes show the rails already loading. Euro customer payments rose from 31,545 in January to 49,005 in July 2026. The retail clearing house hit a record 237,974 transactions in July alone, up 46.2% in seven months. All three national systems moved to the international ISO 20022 message standard during 2025.

The related legal unlock landed on 07/05/2026, when Parliament adopted the law on electronic identification, trusted services and the digital identity wallet. It is stated to be fully aligned with the EU framework. Implementing acts and the accreditation route for qualified trust-service providers are still pending ([AKSK announcement](https://aksk.gov.al/miratohet-ligji-per-identifikimin-elektronik-sherbimet-e-besuara-dhe-portofolin-e-identitetit-digjital/)).

Where to point it: OTP Bank Albania first, since it switched card platforms at the end of May 2026 and reports rising IT costs. The three-to-twelve-month window after a switch migration is when terminal re-certification, machine software, monitoring and screening get bought. Then Raiffeisen Albania, which needs a qualified signature to finish a digital account opening it has already started. Then Credins, whose chief executive names instant payments and SEPA as 2026 items carrying significant implementation cost and fee compression, alongside a cybersecurity investment priority.

The fifteen licensed non-bank payment and electronic-money institutions are the fourth group, led by the two the central bank names as driving sector expansion. They must connect to the same rail while their card issuing jumps from 235 cards at end-2023 to 17,059 at Q1-2026.

Conclusion: treat September 2026 as the practical commitment point, because budget not committed by then becomes 2027 remediation. Sell the screening, alias and payee-verification layer rather than the rail itself, which is bought centrally.
drivers: The platform has been live since 20/07/2026 and Albania is named for the November 2026 window. The Governor restated this on 05/08/2026 as operational within November at the latest ([Banca d'Italia](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).
The original July 2026 target, recorded in the National Payment System Committee minutes of 16/12/2025, has slipped. That squeezes bank-side integration into one quarter.
Phone-number addressing and a Verification of Payee check are design features of the rail, and each is a separate build. The dual-currency settlement model creates two separately screened flows.
Existing rails are already loading fast. Euro customer payments rose from 31,545 in January to 49,005 in July 2026, and retail clearing hit a record 237,974 transactions in July.

Parliament adopted the electronic identification, trusted services and digital identity wallet law on 07/05/2026. That removes the legal blocker to remote enrolment and qualified signature ([AKSK](https://aksk.gov.al/miratohet-ligji-per-identifikimin-elektronik-sherbimet-e-besuara-dhe-portofolin-e-identitetit-digjital/)).

OTP Albania switched card platforms at end-May 2026 and reports rising IT costs. That is the usual window for terminal re-certification and monitoring spend ([OTP half-year report 2026](https://www.otpbank.hu/apps05/capital-market/api/getPublicationFile?token=72F1DFA1AEDBB713B47C000000000079F847A02D44BC72F1DFA1AEDB)).
outlooks.rationale:
The date moved, and that is the main point. A programme originally targeted for July 2026 is now a November go-live, confirmed by the Governor in August. That means integration, screening and channel work that banks had planned across two quarters has to land in one.

Alongside it, the electronic identity law adopted in May 2026 removed the legal precondition for remote enrolment and qualified signature. So the identity work that would otherwise have waited can now be specified in the same budget cycle.
cite_ungrounded: There is no Bank of Albania press release, no day-level go-live date and no published commercial-bank participation list, so the November window is Governor-stated urgency rather than a statutory bank obligation.
The characterisation of September 2026 as the practical budget-commitment point is our own inference from the November window, not a date published by any institution.

outlooks.scope: North Macedonia: two instant payment systems arriving together
outlooks.summary:
North Macedonia is the only market in the region facing two real-time payment systems at the same time. One is the regional TIPS Clone platform, which it is expected to join in the November 2026 window. The other is the domestic KIBS Instant service behind the Strela app, where trade reporting says two banks were preparing to start sending payments by 15/09/2026 ([Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone go-live](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

Underneath both sits the rebuilt MIPS system. The national bank confirmed on 04/08/2026 that it completed the first test cycle. Most messages ran in the ISO 20022 standard, the international payment-message format.

The central bank's own connectivity tender is on a second attempt after the first drew no acceptable bid. It closes 18/09/2026, which gives the bank-side conversation extra months. Expect strong growth in message mapping, round-the-clock operations, real-time screening and QR acceptance across seven banks that each face two integrations.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, and structurally larger here than anywhere else in the bloc, because the work happens twice.

The regional platform went live on 20/07/2026 with Bosnia and Montenegro. A second joining window in November 2026 is expected to bring in North Macedonia alongside Albania and Kosovo. The European Central Bank president referred to the accession on 24/07/2026 and the national bank repeated it. Both say expected, and no day has been named ([Banca d'Italia](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

In parallel, the national bank confirmed on 04/08/2026 that during July it completed the first testing cycle of the rebuilt MIPS national payment system with the banks. Most project messages were processed in ISO 20022, the international payment-message standard ([NBRSM 04/08/2026 release](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-04082026.nspx)).

Separately, KIBS, the private clearing house, already holds an instant-payment operator licence for denar payments settled in under ten seconds around the clock. It runs the Strela app with QR, contactless, an alias register and request-to-pay. Trade press reports two unnamed banks preparing to start sending payments over it by 15/09/2026 ([KIBS instant-payment licence](https://www.kibs.mk/Resources/NewsPromotions/docs/KIBSInstant_Licenca.pdf)).

The baseline is genuinely a standing start. The national bank's own statistics report zero instant payments in every month from January 2024 to March 2026, which makes the before-and-after unusually clean.

Timing intelligence sits in the procurement register. The national bank's connectivity tender, notice 14505/2026, has its bid opening on 18/09/2026 at a second attempt. The identical first notice was cancelled on 28/07/2026 because no acceptable bid was submitted. Eligibility is restricted to a network service provider already authorised for the platform, so this is competitor and calendar intelligence rather than a contest to enter. The register also shows ASEE already holding the support contract for the MIPS and SWIFT equipment inside the institution ([ESJN — NBRM notice dossier](https://www.e-nabavki.gov.mk/PublicAccess/home.aspx#/dossie/56b0e3d2-8430-4f33-958b-404913a73860/1)). A third failed call is a real possibility and would buy further months.

The acceptance layer is the visible follow-on. At the national bank and World Bank forum of 18/06/2026, the vice-governor said more than 90% of payments at small merchants are still cash. Only about 16,700 merchants hold roughly 36,000 accepting devices. The vice-governor named a national interoperable QR code, payment by simple alias, instant confirmation and request-to-pay as the remedies, and the cost of acceptance devices as the barrier ([NBRSM — forum statement](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-18062026.nspx)).

Where to point it: Komercijalna, Stopanska and NLB Skopje first, with the bank-side dual-rail story put in front of them before the connectivity award lands. Take NLB Skopje in particular. It has a EUR 10m Additional Tier 1 loan from its parent disclosed 30/07/2026, plus a EUR 30m parent facility. It also has a named contact-centre modernisation and live real-time transfers to screen. Stopanska has told the market in writing that its suppliers' fees are rising while its own tariffs fall, with a chief executive re-appointed to 2030.

The third target is the acquiring back end behind the QR and softPOS push. There, merchant onboarding, terminal management, key injection and hardware-security-module protection survive whatever the merchant holds in their hand.

Conclusion: sell two integrations as one programme, covering ISO 20022 mapping, 24/7 operations and liquidity, inline sanctions and fraud screening, key management and QR acceptance. Get in front of the three largest banks before the connectivity winner turns a central-bank seat into bank-side accounts, as happened in Kosovo.
drivers: Two separate real-time systems land on the same banks on different calendars. One is the regional platform in the expected November 2026 window. The other is KIBS Instant, with two banks reported preparing to start by 15/09/2026 ([KIBS licence](https://www.kibs.mk/Resources/NewsPromotions/docs/KIBSInstant_Licenca.pdf)).
The national bank completed the first ISO 20022 test cycle of the rebuilt MIPS system in July, confirmed on 04/08/2026 ([NBRSM](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-04082026.nspx)).
Reported instant payments were zero in every month from January 2024 to March 2026. So this is a standing start with a clean baseline.

The central bank's connectivity tender is on a second attempt closing 18/09/2026. The first was cancelled on 28/07/2026 because there was no acceptable bid ([ESJN dossier](https://www.e-nabavki.gov.mk/PublicAccess/home.aspx#/dossie/56b0e3d2-8430-4f33-958b-404913a73860/1)).

The regulator has publicly set a national interoperable QR code, alias payments and request-to-pay as priorities. Only about 16,700 merchants hold roughly 36,000 devices ([NBRSM forum](https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-soopstenie-18062026.nspx)).

NLB Skopje has fresh parent capital, including a EUR 10m Additional Tier 1 loan disclosed 30/07/2026. It names payment-platform upgrades among its forward priorities ([SEINET — NLB Banka Skopje H1-2026](https://seinet.com.mk/document/77993)).
outlooks.rationale:
Three dated events landed within a month, and they point at the same banks. The regional platform went live on 20/07/2026 with North Macedonia named for November. The rebuilt national system passed its first ISO 20022 test cycle in July. And the domestic instant service has banks reported to be starting from 15/09/2026.

On top of that, the central bank's connectivity tender failed once and reopened. That pushes the central procurement later while leaving the bank-side integration work unchanged. So the next two quarters are when banks specify two integrations at once.
cite_ungrounded: The November 2026 accession is described by every source as expected, with no day-level date published by the national bank.
The two banks reported to be initiating on KIBS Instant by 15/09/2026 are not named in any source.
The comparison with Kosovo, where the connectivity core was awarded to Nexi, is drawn from the Kosovo signal set rather than from the North Macedonia rows cited here.

outlooks.scope: Kosovo: central bank instant-payment contracts awarded, bank integration still open
outlooks.summary:
Kosovo's central bank has now bought both pieces it needed for instant payments. A connectivity core was awarded to Nexi Payments SpA at EUR 685,000, published 12/08/2026. A ten-month design and programme-management advisory was awarded to Paylume on 22/07/2026. Onboarding is scheduled for the November 2026 window ([BQK contract award notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Contract_Award_Notice_TIPS-Clone-Connectivity-Services.pdf)).

The core itself is closed to outside bidders. So the remaining money is at the seven commercial banks, none of which has published a connection date. Each must map ISO 20022 messages (the international payment-message standard), offer instant payments through mobile and internet banking, screen a rail that never closes, and build the four named overlays.

Expect growth in channel integration, real-time monitoring, key management and round-the-clock operations. Speed is the deciding factor, because a named competitor now sits inside the central bank for five years.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, with the shape of the opportunity now settled.

Banca d'Italia confirmed that the shared instant-payment platform went live on 20/07/2026, with Bosnia and Montenegro as first joiners. A second onboarding window in November 2026 covers Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia ([Banca d'Italia](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

Kosovo's central bank has completed its own buying. The connectivity layer went to Nexi Payments SpA at a final price of EUR 685,000, for 120 days of delivery plus five years of maintenance. It was notified on 03/06/2026 and published on 12/08/2026. The only rival bid, from SWIFT at EUR 301,138, was declared non-responsive because the bidding forms were not completed ([BQK award notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Contract_Award_Notice_TIPS-Clone-Connectivity-Services.pdf)).

A ten-month advisory for design and programme management went to Paylume SRL of Brussels at EUR 295,000 on 22/07/2026, from a single expression of interest. The funder restricts that core to a network service provider already authorised for the platform, so it was never open to contest. The real consequence is positional. A named competitor now holds a five-year contract and a standing relationship at the central bank, with an obvious path to sell overlay services outward.

The bank-side work carries the spending, and it has no date. Raiffeisen, NLB, TEB, ProCredit, BKT, Banka Ekonomike and Banka per Biznes must each connect to the national system and map ISO 20022 payment messages. They must also offer instant payments through mobile and internet banking, and reconcile a rail that never closes. The chair of the Banking Association's payments committee states the commercial banks' full commitment to join, but no bank connection date is published anywhere.

Round-the-clock irrevocable settlement removes the overnight batch window in which fraud used to be caught. That is what pulls through real-time transaction monitoring, instant sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening, hardware security modules and 24/7 managed operations. The central bank's Annual Report names four overlays being scoped on top of the national system. They are QR code, request to pay, proxy identifier and Verification of Payee. That last one is the check that the name on a transfer matches the account. This is the merchant-acceptance and channel work that follows.

Two funding and compliance currents run alongside. The World Bank operation behind the whole programme, Component 3 of the Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project, is costed at USD 5.0m within a USD 52m operation. It commits eleven institutions to invest private money in fast-payment-ready infrastructure by June 2030. The goods and IT procurement tables are still empty, and open international competition is required at or above USD 1.5m. Four programme-unit consultant contracts are planned for signature on 07/09/2026, which is the signal to start watching ([World Bank implementation status report and procurement plan](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051526174517828/pdf/P507881-c295d365-73e9-4972-93a5-a4072086c160.pdf)).

The second current is a binding cyber-risk rulebook whose compliance date passed on 01/06/2026. It requires a four-hour incident notification and names cash machines as regulated critical infrastructure. It also obliges institutions to hold a cybersecurity budget separate from the general technology budget ([CBK — Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-sistemet-e-informacionit-1-1.pdf?lang=en)).

Where to point it: the seven commercial banks, on channel-side integration, machine and kiosk software change, transaction monitoring and fraud screening. Start with the three that showed live tap-to-phone propositions at the national merchant roadshow, namely Raiffeisen, NLB and ProCredit, as warm back-end entry points. Then TEB, which has failed twice to land a remote-onboarding and qualified electronic-signature stack, most recently on a tender extended twice to 29/06/2026. The World Bank procurement channel is the third route, and it can be monitored from outside without a local portal account.

Conclusion: work the bank-side integration and screening layer across all seven banks now. Watch the empty World Bank goods and IT tables from the 07/09/2026 consultant signatures onward.
drivers: The regional platform has been live since 20/07/2026. Kosovo's central bank is scheduled for the November 2026 onboarding window ([Banca d'Italia](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

The central bank has bought both required pieces: connectivity to Nexi at EUR 685,000, published 12/08/2026, and advisory to Paylume at EUR 295,000 on 22/07/2026. So the remaining spend is bank-side ([BQK award notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Contract_Award_Notice_TIPS-Clone-Connectivity-Services.pdf)).
All seven commercial banks must connect, map ISO 20022 messages and reconcile a rail that never closes. No bank connection date has been published anywhere.
Four overlays are named by the central bank as being scoped: QR code, request to pay, proxy identifier and Verification of Payee. Each is a separate channel build.

The World Bank component funding the programme commits eleven institutions to invest in fast-payment infrastructure to June 2030. The goods and IT procurement tables are still empty, and open international competition is required at or above USD 1.5m ([World Bank procurement plan](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051526174517828/pdf/P507881-c295d365-73e9-4972-93a5-a4072086c160.pdf)).

A binding cyber-risk regulation, whose compliance date passed on 01/06/2026, forces a ring-fenced cybersecurity budget and four-hour incident reporting. It names cash machines as critical infrastructure ([CBK regulation](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-sistemet-e-informacionit-1-1.pdf?lang=en)).
outlooks.rationale:
The central bank finished buying this cycle. With the connectivity award published on 12/08/2026 and the advisory contract awarded on 22/07/2026, the programme moved from planning into delivery. The open question changed from whether the rail happens to when each commercial bank connects to it, and nobody has published that.

That undated bank-side gap sits between a November onboarding window and a competitor newly installed at the central bank on a five-year contract. That is why the next two quarters are the moment to engage all seven banks, rather than wait for a tender to appear.
cite_ungrounded: No commercial-bank connection date has been published anywhere, so the bank-side timetable is inferred from the November 2026 central-bank onboarding window rather than sourced.
The expectation that the connectivity contractor will sell overlay services outward to commercial banks is the analysts' assessment in the underlying signal, not a stated intention by that company.
Kosovo's SEPA application remains blocked by two laws still in constitutional review, so the wider compliance wave behind this programme has no fixed date.

outlooks.scope: Austrian cash automation: public tenders drawing single bids, and the supply-chain routes that remain open
outlooks.summary:
Austrian cash automation should grow modestly but steadily over the next year. Its public buyers attract very little competition.

The national bank has now called off its rural cash-machine framework twelve times in a row to the same supplier on a single offer, most recently on 26/08/2026 ([USP eProcurement — OeNB call-off to PSA](https://ausschreibungen.usp.gv.at/at.gv.bmdw.eproc-p/public/tender-detail?object=a2c49245-23b2-46e1-acc7-c5a78913a090-9f280e64-19e5-4aad-b535-1d48aeb56f6c)). The Austrian Mint has had to re-run a cancelled machine tender on a wider budget with deliberately simpler entry rules.

The country's largest contest is Geldservice Austria's EUR 9.1m framework for recyclers. Recyclers are cash machines that take in deposited notes, check them and pay the same notes back out. The framework is still unawarded nine weeks before its recorded start. Its bidder field closed on 08/06/2026, so unless Printec was already invited this is competitive intelligence rather than a live bid ([TED 305531-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/305531-2026/xml)).

The addressable Austrian money therefore sits one layer down, inside the incumbents' supply chains rather than against them. It has to be pursued while a 60-month contract signed in August 2026 is being mobilised. Sizing is directional only, because no Austrian market statistics and no hiring evidence were filed this cycle.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, but achieved mainly through supply chains rather than through wins in open competition. The dated events run in sequence.

The Austrian Mint's re-run tender for an automated weighing line for coin blanks closes for requests to participate on 14/09/2026. It carries an estimated EUR 280,000, which is EUR 30,000 more than the attempt that was cancelled despite drawing four offers. The published reason for the extension is that the suitability criteria were simplified ([TED 588745-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/588745-2026/xml)). The fit is only partial, because coin-blank weighing is mint machinery rather than branch cash automation. It needs an honest capability check before anything else.

The national bank's tender to draft Generic Threat Landscape reports for the whole Austrian financial sector closes 28/09/2026. It has a 60-month base term that can be extended twice by a year, so as much as seven years of supplier position is being fixed. No value is published ([TED 587224-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/587224-2026/xml)).

Geldservice Austria's EUR 9.1m recycler framework has a recorded contract start of 02/11/2026 and was re-verified as unawarded on 31/08/2026. Its published scoring puts evaluated price at 245 points and banknote recycling at 100, against 74 for coin recycling. Treat it as a signal about where recycler economics are heading in Austria, Slovenia and the Austrian border regions, not as a pipeline entry ([TED 305531-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/305531-2026/xml)).

The national bank's maintenance bridge for security technology, security doors and airlocks with PKE Electronics expires on 31/12/2026. So either a replacement procurement or a further extension has to appear this autumn ([TED 157688-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/157688-2026/xml)).

Where to focus: PSA Payment Services Austria, the banks' jointly owned payments company. It holds the national bank's rural framework and already runs roughly 6,474 machines. The machines themselves, multivendor cash-machine software, device telemetry and the second-line field service that PSA subcontracts rather than performs are all reachable without a tender.

A second target is the regulator FMA as a direct buyer of financial-crime analytics and security tooling. It buys through the resellers SoftwareONE and Arrow ECS, which won its recent single-offer procedures, although its network-security services already sit with Atos. A third is the Austrian coin-handling and smart-safe layer, where a EUR 661,057.35 coin-roll packing award drew one bid and Oesterreichische Post's cash-safe framework has been running since 2015.

Conclusion: treat Austria as a supply-chain and public-buyer market this year. Brief Geldservice Austria to management as intelligence rather than to sales as an opportunity. Get the capability answer on the Mint tender inside two weeks.
drivers: The national bank's rural cash-machine framework was called off again on 26/08/2026 at EUR 382,001.48 for a 60-month term on a single offer. That is the twelfth such award, at roughly six-week intervals. The end-2026 target of up to 120 machines cannot plausibly be funded from what remains inside the EUR 5,544,425.60 parent ceiling. So a framework extension or a fresh procurement has to appear ([USP eProcurement — OeNB call-off to PSA](https://ausschreibungen.usp.gv.at/at.gv.bmdw.eproc-p/public/tender-detail?object=a2c49245-23b2-46e1-acc7-c5a78913a090-9f280e64-19e5-4aad-b535-1d48aeb56f6c)).

Geldservice Austria's EUR 9.1m recycler and coin-depositor framework remains unawarded, with a 02/11/2026 recorded start. Its call-offs may be sited not only in Austria but in Slovenia, Bavaria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary and Italy within 100 km of the Austrian border. So whoever wins gains a platform in up to four further Printec countries ([TED 305531-2026](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/305531-2026/xml)).

The regulator FMA runs open, above-threshold procedures that draw one offer. One example is a cryptocurrency-analytics tool at EUR 126,121.68, concluded 12/03/2026. Another is a round-the-clock security operations centre at EUR 385,600.00, concluded 26/11/2025. Both were awarded on a single bid ([USP eProcurement — FMA Analysetool Kryptowaehrung award](https://ausschreibungen.usp.gv.at/at.gv.bmdw.eproc-p/public/tender-detail?object=009b7802-0b04-4fee-8dac-3922bd5098ae-KD_2294753)).

Loomis is converting cash-in-transit relationships into recycler and smart-safe service contracts on a record 14.0% operating margin. So the Austrian commercial recycler discussion is now contested from the cash-logistics side as well as the machine side ([Loomis AB — Interim Report January–June 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/loomis-interim-report-january--june-2026-302833961.html)).

Erste closed 23 Austrian branches in twelve months, to 714 at 30/06/2026. Underlying group IT spend excluding Poland rose only about 3.5%. So Austrian cash volume keeps moving to self-service, but new spend must be argued as a cost saving rather than as a refresh ([Erste Group H1-2026 conference-call presentation](https://cdn.erstegroup.com/content/dam/at/eh/www_erstegroup_com/en/Investor_Relations/2026/presentations/IR_Pres_CC_260730_H126.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
What changed happened in the last two weeks of August 2026. A 60-month call-off signed on 26/08/2026 means the time to sit inside PSA's supply chain is now, during mobilisation, rather than at a renewal five years away.

On the same day the Mint published a change notice reopening a tender it had already cancelled once, with a wider budget and easier entry rules. That is the behaviour of a buyer that did not get what it wanted from the field it first attracted.

Two research units re-checked the Geldservice Austria framework. They found it still unawarded nine weeks from its recorded start, and established that the candidate field had already closed on 08/06/2026. That makes the country's biggest cash contest a piece of market intelligence rather than a pursuit. It also redirects the Austrian effort onto the supply-chain and public-buyer routes that are actually open ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md); [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).
cite_ungrounded: Whether Printec or NCR Atleos was among the candidates invited to the Geldservice Austria framework from 25/06/2026 is not established by any signal; this whole card is written on the assumption that neither was, which is why the framework is treated as intelligence.

No Austrian market-statistics rows and no hiring or early-intent rows were filed this cycle, so there is no independent evidence of Austrian estate size, installed-base age or bank hiring behind any statement here.

The unresolved reconciliation between the EUR 4,045,406.80 already recorded as called off from the national bank's framework and the 26/08/2026 award is carried forward unexplained; the inference that the 120-machine target cannot be funded inside the EUR 5.54m ceiling depends on it.
The suggestion that PSA subcontracts rather than performs second-line field service comes from a single vendor-side reading and is not evidenced in a procurement document.

outlooks.scope: Raiffeisen Bank International's integration budget and the Vienna timetable before the February Capital Markets Day
outlooks.summary:
The strongest demand signal in Austria over the next twelve months comes from a bank rebuilding itself, not from a tender. Raiffeisen Bank International won the contested takeover of Addiko Bank on 03/08/2026 with 55.55% of the share capital. It keeps Croatia, Slovenia and Austria, and has set aside about EUR 75m of one-off integration cost across 2027 and 2028 ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

At the same time, a new chief executive is running a full reset of strategy. The published timetable puts the strategy in front of senior management at the end of Q3-2026 and starts implementation in Q4-2026. The spending total only becomes public at a Capital Markets Day in February 2027. So the time to talk to procurement is the autumn, before the number is announced.

A new head of Group Retail, with a clear brief for digital work and partnerships, starts on 01/09/2026, just as that strategy is being written. Two more Vienna deadlines fall in the same quarter. The first is an action plan on end-of-life technology, due to the group's supervisors on 31/10/2026. The second is digital-euro pilot duties that name RBI and BAWAG.

Aim the effort at group procurement in Vienna and the Zagreb integration office, not at the bank being bought.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth in addressable scope, meaning the work Printec can bid for. It is concentrated in one decision centre in Vienna and squeezed into two quarters. The triggers have dates, and they follow each other closely.

Curt Chadha takes over Group Retail Banking on 01/09/2026 with a brief for digital development and partnerships. Christine Anwander-Hirsch has run the Generalsekretariat since 01/08/2026, with AI-supported processes among her efficiency priorities ([RBI — Neue Fuehrungskraefte fuer Group Retail Banking](https://www.rbinternational.com/de/raiffeisen/media-hub/presseaussendungen/2026/new_executives.html)).

The strategy goes to senior management at the end of Q3-2026 under three named priorities. One of them is technological transformation, with 'end-to-end process: digitized and operated' spelled out. Implementation starts in Q4-2026, and the Capital Markets Day follows in February 2027.

On the deal itself, the acceptance period runs to 03/11/2026. Completion is expected in Q4-2026, and all closing conditions fall due by 14/05/2027.

The measurable opportunity is in Croatia. Addiko's own branch locator showed 35 branches and 144 machines, with no mention of deposit or recycling. Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d. has 286 cash-out machines plus 150 deposit machines. Slovenia is a re-entry of 20 branches and 31 machines, shaped as a build from scratch rather than a cut-back.

Separately, every significant institution must file an action plan with its Joint Supervisory Team by 31/10/2026. That team is the European Central Bank team that supervises the individual bank, and Erste Group and RBI are expressly named in scope. The plan must name the legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technology the bank will replace ([ECB — letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

Where to focus: RBI group procurement in Vienna and the Zagreb integration office. Offer service-based proposals to Addiko today and capital-based hardware to RBI. That work covers estate consolidation, standard cash automation, card and acquiring migration, key migration and multi-year managed services.

Offer BAWAG P.S.K. and RBI help with digital-euro terminal readiness for the pilot's operating phase in H2-2027. Offer Erste in Vienna cost-cutting managed services rather than new hardware, because its core IT budget is flat.

Also offer the Raiffeisen Bankengruppe and Erste Bank Oesterreich acceptance-side work for the Wero account-to-account payment scheme. Both groups said on 22/06/2026 they would join, still subject to supervisory-board approval, and no Austrian go-live date has been published ([RBI — EPI begruesst Erste Bank Oesterreich](https://www.rbinternational.com/de/raiffeisen/media-hub/presseaussendungen/2026/epi.html)).

Conclusion: make the RBI approach in Q4-2026, timed to the start of implementation rather than to the February 2027 announcement. Keep Addiko and RBI as two different conversations with two different commercial shapes.
drivers: RBI won Addiko on 03/08/2026 with acceptances for 10,831,435 shares. That is 56.16% of the shares covered by the offer and 55.55% of total capital, after RBI cut its own minimum threshold from 75% to 55%. NLB's rival offer reached only 31.22% against a condition of 50% plus one share, and will not go through ([RBI H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

About EUR 75m of one-off integration cost is budgeted across 2027-2028, against roughly EUR 60m of extra profit in 2028. RBI's own offer document calls full operational, technological and organisational integration of the Croatian subsidiary a key success factor ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md); [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

The strategy timetable is published rather than assumed. It starts with a baseline, then sets the ambition and road map. A strategy update goes to senior management at end-Q3-2026. Implementation then begins, and a Capital Markets Day follows in February 2027 ([RBI H1/2026 conference-call presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).

RBI is under contract inside the ECB's digital-euro pilot alongside BAWAG P.S.K. The development phase runs from Q3-2026 and a twelve-month operating phase from H2-2027. That puts terminal firmware, contactless and offline readiness, and remote update capability on a build plan with fixed dates ([ECB — press release naming the 36 pilot payment service providers](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260714~8cd07d9d45.en.html)).

RBI's own count of outlets fell to 1,304 group outlets from 1,368. Addiko is the opposite case: a flat 154 branches, automating inside them rather than closing. These are two different routes that both lead to deposit-capable machines and self-service zones ([Raiffeisen Bank International — H1/2026 results presentation](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/events-and-presentation/presentation-and-webcast/conference-call-presentations/2026-07-31%20Q2%20Presentation%20RBI.pdf.coredownload.pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
The timing matters because of the order of events. Until 03/08/2026 the Addiko outcome was contested and could not be budgeted. It is now settled, funded and dated.

The strategy reset reaches senior management at the end of Q3-2026 and starts implementation in Q4-2026. So the vendor questions inside 'technological transformation' get answered this autumn, while the public number waits until February 2027. Anyone who waits for the Capital Markets Day arrives after the scoping is done.

A new head of Group Retail arrives on 01/09/2026 with a partnerships brief for his first two quarters. A supervisory filing due on 31/10/2026 also forces the same bank to write down which of its technologies are end-of-life. Four dated events therefore fall in one quarter, and they all point to the same organisation in Vienna.
cite_ungrounded: No Austrian market-statistics or hiring rows were filed this cycle, so there is no independent early-intent evidence — job postings, project adverts — behind the claim that RBI's procurement activity actually begins in Q4-2026; that timing is read off the disclosed strategy calendar alone.

That Wero acceptance would extend beyond Austria into RBI's central and south-eastern European subsidiaries is inference and has not been said by RBI; the shareholding itself is still subject to supervisory-board approval and no Austrian consumer go-live date exists.

Addiko's Croatian fleet figures of 35 branches and 144 machines come from enumerating the bank's own public locator rather than from a disclosure, and the absence of deposit or recycling wording on those machines is inferred from the locator text, not confirmed by the bank.

outlooks.scope: Supervisory action plans due by October require banks to name their end-of-life machines
outlooks.summary:
This is the firmest dated trigger for technology spending in the seven supervised markets in the footprint: Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Greece, Croatia, Slovenia and Slovakia. It points straight at ageing self-service estates, meaning a bank's fleet of ATMs and kiosks.

Every significant institution must file an action plan with its Joint Supervisory Team by 31/10/2026. That team is the European Central Bank team that supervises the individual bank. One of the six named focus areas is replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies ([ECB — letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)). Money for fixes therefore has to be written into a document that a supervisor then monitors.

A second named focus area, accurate identification of technology assets, is a sale of device telemetry in its own right. Device telemetry is automatic reporting from each machine. The same letter also brings supplier service-level agreements and contract terms into scope. So this is both an opportunity and a duty to review every managed-service contract Printec already holds.

Two supply-side complications fall in the same fortnight. A competitor is selling banks the opposite answer, keeping old machines alive with virtualisation software. Printec's main machine supplier is also going through a dated regulatory review that would make it part of a direct competitor.
outlooks.projected:
Strong growth, and the clearest funded trigger in the whole book. The order of events is fixed.

Claudia Buch signed the letter on 07/07/2026. The same 31/10/2026 deadline was then repeated in Official Journal text. It came through the European Systemic Risk Board's formal warning of 25/06/2026, published on 16/07/2026. So it is no longer only a letter.

On 31/07/2026 the three European Supervisory Authorities extended the same governance expectation down to smaller banks supervised at national level. That is the mid-market tier where most of Printec's estate sits. The ECB's annual technology-risk questionnaire has also moved from September 2026 to February 2027, which extends the evidence window rather than closing it.

The likely next supervisory step is threat-led penetration testing. That is a controlled attack simulation run against live production systems under Articles 26 and 27 of the digital operational resilience rules. Supervisors recognise each other's tests. So one group-level exercise at Erste, RBI, OTP, NLB or UniCredit can pull Printec-operated estates in several countries into a single window. The repair work afterwards is the actual sale ([Hrvatska narodna banka — Digitalna operativna otpornost](https://www.hnb.hr/-/digitalna-operativna-otpornost)).

Two counterweights must be stated plainly. KAL is marketing a hypervisor, which is software that runs one system inside another. It runs a newer Windows on old machines, even where the hardware maker no longer supports them. It has a named Czech reference, plus a zero-licence pre-install offer that fits under any multivendor software account. The counter-argument is total cost of ownership: a fleet kept alive in software still fails mechanically, and still cannot take deposits or recycle notes.

The UK competition authority opened its Phase 1 inquiry into Brink's purchase of NCR Atleos on 26/08/2026. The statutory decision deadline is 22/10/2026, while both companies moved expected completion forward to early Q1-2027 ([UK CMA — Brink's / NCR Atleos merger inquiry](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry)). Printec's main supplier of dispense, deposit and recycling machines is about to be owned by a company that competes with Printec directly.

Where to focus: the significant institutions filing on 31/10/2026. They include Erste Group and RBI in Vienna, Bank of Cyprus, the Greek banks, the Bulgarian banks now under direct supervision since euro entry, and the Slovenian and Slovak groups. Next come the smaller nationally supervised banks caught by the 31/07/2026 extension.

Internally, the focus is the DORA register of information. Its 31/12/2026 reference date feeds national bank-level cut-offs in February and March 2027. Failing to supply clean register data is a common reason for a service to be put back out to tender.

Conclusion: sell the asset inventory and the deposit-and-recycling refresh against a filing date the customer cannot move. In parallel, put written distributor-continuity terms in place before 22/10/2026, together with change-of-control and price-protection clauses.
drivers: Every significant institution must submit an AI-cyber action plan to its Joint Supervisory Team by 31/10/2026. Focus area 5 requires modernising infrastructure by replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies. Focus area 1 requires accurate inventories of technology assets ([ECB — letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

KAL is pitching its Kalignite hypervisor across Greece, Czechia, Slovakia and Romania precisely so banks can keep ageing machines through the move to Windows 11. It returns to Banktech in Athens on 08-09/10/2026 as a guest of Mellon. This is independent confirmation that the end of life of machine operating systems is the main area of competition in 2026-27 ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

The Brink's purchase of NCR Atleos reached a dated regulatory step on 26/08/2026. A Phase 1 decision is due 22/10/2026, and completion has moved forward to early Q1-2027. Atleos held no Q2 earnings call and published no outlook, so the usual regional commentary has gone quiet for at least two quarters ([UK CMA — Brink's / NCR Atleos merger inquiry](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry)).

Diebold Nixdorf's Q2 filings of 29/07/2026 show European banking product sales down 13.0% to USD 236.6m on lower European volume. Its services base held, and it shipped a record number of teller cash recyclers. Its hardware refresh cycle has stalled, but it is now bundling branch automation, cash management and long-term service agreements ([Diebold Nixdorf Form 10-Q, quarter ended 30/06/2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/28823/000002882326000033/dbd-20260630.htm)).

The ECB has committed in writing to a separate future letter on post-quantum cryptography, which is encryption designed to survive a future large-scale quantum computer. It says adoption must start now, but gives no date. So it is an announced supervisory action, and must never be presented to a customer as a deadline ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).
outlooks.rationale:
The change that matters is enforceability. A supervisory letter became Official Journal text on 16/07/2026. The expectation was pushed down to nationally supervised banks on 31/07/2026. The evidence window was extended to February 2027.

So what was guidance in July is now a dated duty with follow-up monitoring. It lands during the autumn planning round, when 2027 budgets are set. The calendar also adds commercial urgency. The competition decision on Printec's own supply chain falls on 22/10/2026. That is nine days before the banks file the plans naming the machines they intend to replace.
cite_ungrounded: Pairing the 22/10/2026 competition decision with the 31/10/2026 supervisory filing is our own juxtaposition; no source connects the two events.

The reading that the Cyber Resilience Act captures cash machines, point-of-sale terminals, kiosks, recyclers and hardware security modules — and that it places Printec in an importer or distributor role — is explicitly flagged as an interpretation that no cited source states.

That ageing machines on unsupported operating systems fall inside the ECB's 'legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies' wording is a reading of the letter's language, not a category the ECB names.
No count of how many machines in the footprint actually run unsupported software exists in any signal, so the scale of the refresh population is unquantified here.

outlooks.scope: Structured payment address data becomes mandatory across all seventeen markets in November
outlooks.summary:
A hard network deadline in November forces address and party data into a structured format across every market Printec operates in. Messages that do not conform are rejected.

The euro settlement platform's release goes into production on Saturday 14/11/2026. Its test window opens 25/09/2026 and closes 28/10/2026. That closing date is the real hard stop, because a bank that has not tested by then has no second chance ([Deutsche Bundesbank — T2 R2026.NOV release information](https://www.bundesbank.de/resource/blob/994978/e841962b2370d811340b0fa5e3f61080/472B63F073F071307366337C94F8C870/t2-r2026nov-information-on-release-data.pdf)).

The scheme-side cut-off reported for 15/11/2026 at 03:30 CET could not be checked at source this cycle. It must be flagged as unverified in every customer conversation.

The settlement core itself is not Printec's lane. The layer around it is. That work covers cleaning address and party data, plus re-tuning sanctions and financial-crime screening onto the structured fields. It also covers payment repair, monitoring rejects through the cutover weekend, and the field services to run it.

The programme budget window has already closed. So the sale between now and November is emergency remediation rather than a planned migration. The largest unclaimed opportunity is in the non-EU markets, where no local regulator forces the change but correspondent flows break anyway. Correspondent flows are payments routed through partner banks.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, but as a sharp, short spike rather than a lasting line, followed by a separately funded second wave.

The dated events run in order. The euro settlement release test window opens 25/09/2026 and closes 28/10/2026. Production deployment falls on Saturday 14/11/2026, alongside the annual standards-release weekend. The payment-scheme address cut-off is reported for 15/11/2026 at 03:30 CET. A second wave in November 2027 migrates seven core payment messages that stay on their 2019 version this year. So any vendor pitching a core schema migration in 2026 has the scope wrong.

Two corrections cap the honest scope. Only the structured town and country fields are needed for regulatory screening, so the data-cleaning job is narrower than it is usually sold as. But no end date has been set for the hybrid address format, so it must not be presented as permanent either.

Where to focus: banks in the ten European Union markets in the footprint that have not booked test slots in the 25/09–28/10/2026 window. There the work is data cleaning, repair and reject monitoring rather than platform change.

Next come the non-European Union markets: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo and Ukraine. No local regulator forces the change there, and correspondent traffic will reject regardless, which makes it the largest unclaimed opportunity.

The third group is any bank whose outsourced processing contract is ending. Worldline has told investors its bank-facing division carries a EUR 60m full-year drag from contract terminations and will not return to growth before the second half of 2027. That brings estates and payment operations back to market at exactly the moment they need hands-on remediation ([Worldline H1 2026 results presentation](https://investors.worldline.com/content/dam/investors-worldline-com/assets/documents/presentations/2026/20260730-worldline-h1-2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

Conclusion: sell survival of the test window and reject monitoring through October and November 2026. Keep the scope honest at town and country. Open the 2027 conversation on the second wave before the first one is finished.
drivers: The euro real-time settlement release goes into production on 14/11/2026. Testing is open from 25/09/2026 and closes 28/10/2026. Address removal reaches the core payment messages through a usage guideline rather than a schema change ([Deutsche Bundesbank — T2 R2026.NOV release information](https://www.bundesbank.de/resource/blob/994978/e841962b2370d811340b0fa5e3f61080/472B63F073F071307366337C94F8C870/t2-r2026nov-information-on-release-data.pdf)).

Scheme guidance reported to fix the end of the unstructured address format states that its use will no longer be allowed. Rejects will follow, on the inter-bank leg and on corporate file upload alike. But the publisher's site was unreachable by every route this cycle, so this is reported, not verified ([EPC153-22 v2.1 — Provision of Addresses under the EPC Payment Schemes](https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/sites/default/files/kb/file/2025-10/EPC153-22%20v2.1%20EPC%20guidance%20document%20-%20Provision%20of%20Addresses%20under%20the%20EPC%20Payment%20Schemes.pdf)).

A change request confirms that seven core payment messages stay on the 2019 version in November 2026 and are only probably migrated in November 2027. That splits the work into two separately funded waves ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The wider payments package that would extend Verification of Payee beyond instant payments has slipped. Verification of Payee is a check that the name on a transfer matches the account it is going to. The only forward date is an indicative plenary of 14/12/2026. So roadmaps must be reset, and no 2027 or 2028 compliance date should be quoted as fixed ([Council of the EU — ST 8221/26, Payment Services Regulation](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-8221-2026-INIT/en/pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
Two things make this the moment. First, the anchor date moved from vendor guidance to a central-bank release document. So the testing window of 25/09–28/10/2026 can be quoted to a customer as an operational fact, and that window opens within a month.

Second, the scoping errors can now be named. The seven core messages are not migrating this year, and only town and country are needed for screening. A bank that has not started has roughly five weeks to book testing. That is remediation work rather than programme work, and remediation is bought late, quickly and locally.
cite_ungrounded: The European Payments Council site was blocked to every route this cycle, so none of the five scheme dates carried here is verified at primary source — including the 15/11/2026 03:30 CET address cut-off and the four rulebooks it is said to span. Quote them to customers as reported-but-unverified.
The Verification-of-Payee rulebook version 1.1 becoming binding at 20/09/2026 03:30 CET is unverified this cycle for the same reason and does not appear in any cited signal.
Bulgaria's 01/01/2027 instant-payments date and the 09/01/2027 date for Czechia, Hungary and Romania are carried from briefing context and appear in none of the cited signals.
The claim of a network-level rejection mechanic at the messaging network is recorded as unverified in the underlying research and should not be asserted to a bank.
