No signal quantifies how many footprint banks have yet to book a test slot, so the size of the remediation population is asserted from the shape of the deadline, not measured.

outlooks.scope: Ten months to the money-laundering regulation, with the technical rulebook still unpublished
outlooks.summary:
Every bank across the ten European Union markets in the footprint is now scoping financial-crime programmes against draft rules. The Anti-Money-Laundering Regulation applies directly on 10/07/2027, and the accompanying directive must be written into national law the same day.

A search of the European Union's own publications database on 27/08/2026 returned not a single binding technical text. Roughly nineteen mandates that were due on 10/07/2026 are overdue. They include the customer-due-diligence standards that say which sources may be used to verify identity ([AMLA — Regulatory Instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

That gap is the commercial argument. What banks can safely buy this autumn is a configurable rules layer that can be re-pointed when the official text lands, not a hard-coded onboarding or monitoring flow.

A second, larger programme runs alongside it and is bought centrally. The new anti-money-laundering authority is drawing up the list of cross-border groups it will supervise directly from 2028. Budget for both is committed in the 2027 planning round now open, from September to November 2026.
outlooks.projected:
Growth, spread across two different buying centres.

On the per-country side, two consultations close on 03/09 and 20/09. Two more close on 27/09 and 06/10/2026. The first of them is the ongoing-monitoring guidelines, which are in effect the functional specification for transaction monitoring. A European Banking Authority reporting release also carries the new risk-assessment and eligibility taxonomy, applying to reports as of December 2026.

Transposition means writing the directive into national law, and it is uneven in a way that creates a specific window. Croatia has reported no measures against the July-2025 tranche, and Slovakia only partial ones. Infringement proceedings are pending against Croatia, Cyprus, Greece and Slovakia. So those banks get national rules late while the July-2027 date does not move. Historically, that is the pattern that produces rushed, vendor-led remediation ([European Commission — AMLD6 transposition monitoring](https://finance.ec.europa.eu/regulation-and-supervision/financial-services-legislation/enforcement-and-infringements-banking-and-finance-law/monitoring-banking-and-finance-directives/anti-money-laundering-and-terrorist-financing-directive-vi_en)).

On the group side, national supervisors filed their data by 15/08/2026. The provisional list of eligible entities is expected to be finalised at the end of September 2026. The first selection process must begin by 01/07/2027 and finish within six months, and direct supervision starts in 2028. The eligibility test is operating in at least six Member States including the home state ([AMLA — next step toward the 2027 selection of entities](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

What is really being tested there is whether customer-due-diligence and monitoring records are consistent across subsidiaries in eight to thirteen countries. That is a group-level data-lineage problem, bought centrally rather than country by country. Data lineage means tracing where each piece of data came from.

Underneath both runs the identity build. Every Member State must provide a digital identity wallet by 24/12/2026, and the register regime for the businesses that accept wallet presentations applies the same day. The bank-side duty to accept wallets is worked out, not printed, at 24/12/2027. Seven of the ten markets still had no public sandbox as of an April-2026 tracker, so those banks cannot test on their own ([European Commission — EUDI Architecture and Reference Framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

Where to focus: group compliance and data functions at the large cross-border groups, for the consistency and lineage work. Then Croatian and Slovak banks, for the late-rules remediation window.

The third target is the identity-verification build at banks in the seven markets without a sandbox. Sell it as a wallet-agnostic acceptance layer that keeps document-and-selfie proofing alongside it, because the portrait does not become mandatory wallet data until 2028 and may still be declined.

Conclusion: sell configurability and say so openly in bids. Get into the 2027 budget round before November. Treat the group-level data question as a separate and larger sale than the per-country compliance work.
drivers: Not one delegated or implementing regulation under the three anti-money-laundering instruments has reached the Official Journal. The two instruments that matter most to banks remain at 'consultation closed' with no final report. Their statutory delivery date of 10/07/2026 has been missed ([AMLA — Regulatory Instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

The new authority's provisional list of eligible obliged entities is expected at end-September 2026. The first selection starts by 01/07/2027 and direct supervision runs from 2028. The eligibility test is operating in at least six Member States including the home state ([AMLA — next step toward the 2027 selection of entities](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

Member State wallet issuance and the relying-party register regime both apply from 24/12/2026. An amending implementing regulation in force from 11/08/2026 adds a biometric warning and an explicit confirmation step whenever a portrait is requested. It also adds a wallet trust mark and mandatory cryptographic mechanisms ([European Commission — EUDI Architecture and Reference Framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

The crypto-asset transitional period ended on 01/07/2026. Unauthorised providers must wind down while keeping full customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening and suspicious-activity reporting in place throughout. That gives two modest but real pulses of demand in identity verification and monitoring as client books move ([ESMA — public statement on the end of the MiCA transitional period](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-06/ESMA75-113276571-1710_Public_Statement_MiCA_transitional_period_ends.pdf)).

The real artificial-intelligence compliance deadline for financial-crime analytics moved to 02/12/2027, not December 2026. That buys about a year, and means any customer being told otherwise is being mis-sold ([Official Journal — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744](http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj)).
outlooks.rationale:
The reason to act now is a gap, not an event. Ten months before a directly applicable regulation, the binding detail does not exist. So every bank in the footprint is designing against drafts and knows it. That makes configurability a purchasing criterion this autumn rather than a feature claim.

At the same time, the group-level supervision list is being finalised at the end of September 2026, and the identity supply side goes live on 24/12/2026. Three separate timetables therefore meet in the same 2027 budget round, which opens now and closes in November.
cite_ungrounded: The inference that Erste, Raiffeisen Bank International, UniCredit, OTP, NLB and Intesa Sanpaolo all clear the six-Member-State eligibility test is Printec's own; the authority names no individual institution, and no group is identified as selected here for that reason.

Linking the overdue customer-due-diligence standards to the digital identity wallet is our reading: the standards are recorded as specifying the attributes electronic identification must carry, but no cited source names the EU wallet as the vehicle.
The bank-side wallet acceptance date of 24/12/2027 is derived from a 36-month clock in the legal text and is not printed anywhere; it must be presented to customers as derived.
The 'seven of ten markets without a public sandbox' figure comes from an April-2026 tracker and may have moved since.

outlooks.scope: Digital euro: funded terminal work now, and no funding for cash machines
outlooks.summary:
The digital euro is real and has dates. But the part of it that touches cash machines is explicitly not funded, and that distinction is the most useful thing a sales force can carry this year.

The draft scheme rulebook of 02/07/2026 does contain a full section covering cash funding, cash defunding and balance enquiry at a machine, with flows started by card and by code. The same annex states word for word that those use cases are deprioritised and will be addressed later ([ECB — draft digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91, Annex D1](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/timeline/profuse/shared/pdf/ecb.derdgpr260702_Digital_euro_scheme_rulebook_v0.91_-_Annex_D1_-_Front-end_implementation_specifications_4_Acceptance_device.en.pdf)).

What is funded is the pilot. Thirty-six payment service providers test four use cases, with no machine and no hardware terminal case. Development runs from Q3-2026, and operation runs for twelve months from the second half of 2027.

So the warm sale is terminal firmware, contactless and offline readiness, and remote update capability at the named pilot banks. The honest machine offer is a readiness assessment and a survey of gaps in code capability. Hardware should never be sold against a deadline that does not exist.

The first market discussion of rollout strategy is 13/10/2026. The sentence to watch is the deprioritisation sentence: if it changes in a later rulebook version, the whole euro-area machine estate becomes a buy signal.
outlooks.projected:
Mixed by design: growth on terminals, flat on machines, with the machine side depending on one sentence in the rulebook.

The dated triggers start with the 21st Euro Retail Payments Board technical session on 13/10/2026, the first time rollout strategy is discussed with the market. The pilot development phase is already running from Q3-2026. The twelve-month operating phase starts in the second half of 2027, which obliges the named banks to have terminal readiness in place well before it begins.

Parliament confirmed its negotiating mandate on 09/07/2026 by 416 votes to 169 with 22 abstentions. The central bank is formalising a memorandum of understanding with the payments-scheme body. That body's named candidate standards include a code-based payment standard described as potentially covering machine transactions. That point is reported, but could not be checked at source this cycle.

Two related cash files sit behind it. The legal-tender file entered trilogue on 08/07/2026, with political agreement targeted around end-2026. Trilogue means three-way talks between Parliament, Council and Commission. The draft names density of cash access points relative to population as a monitoring indicator, and geographical access requirements would follow if that indicator fails.

If that survives adoption, it is the largest single machine signal anywhere in the regulatory book. But nothing is adopted, and the indicator is not verified in the mandate articles. So a gap analysis of estate density may be sold today only as scenario planning.

The euro banknote redesign has a public survey closing 21/09/2026 and a design decision expected around end-2026. The manufacturer Glory guides related equipment demand from around 2029 ([ECB — ECB reveals shortlisted designs for new banknotes](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260723~c2d43f9170.en.html)). A series change is a recurring stream of recognition-template, sensor and re-testing work rather than a machine replacement. That favours a field organisation over a pure manufacturer. The condition is that the budget lines are shaped in the 2027 and 2028 planning rounds, instead of arriving as a single manufacturer package.

Where to focus: the named pilot banks, on terminal and terminal-management readiness for the second half of 2027. They are BAWAG P.S.K. and Raiffeisen Bank International in Austria, Bank of Cyprus with JCC Payment Systems, and three Greek banks including Piraeus. The list also includes Tatra banka with the Slovak central bank, NLB in Slovenia, Raiffeisenbank Austria in Croatia and UniCredit.

Offer the same accounts a readiness assessment for the machine estate, priced as an assessment. Offer euro-area central banks and large branch networks banknote-redesign service planning for 2027-2028 budgets.

Conclusion: sell terminal readiness where the obligation is real. Do not sell machine hardware against a deprioritised use case. Watch the rulebook version for the sentence that would change that.
drivers: The pilot tests four use cases only, with no machine and no hardware terminal case. It runs from Q3-2026 into a twelve-month operating phase from the second half of 2027. Bulgaria is not among the nineteen participating central banks, despite having joined the euro on 01/01/2026 ([ECB — press release naming the 36 pilot payment service providers](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260714~8cd07d9d45.en.html)).

The rulebook's machine annex says plainly that those use cases are deprioritised and will be addressed at a later stage. Version 0.91 was still the latest when re-checked on 27/08/2026. So there is no certification duty and no trigger for capital spending on the machine estate ([ECB — draft digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91, Annex D1](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/timeline/profuse/shared/pdf/ecb.derdgpr260702_Digital_euro_scheme_rulebook_v0.91_-_Annex_D1_-_Front-end_implementation_specifications_4_Acceptance_device.en.pdf)).

Worldline is positioning itself as digital-euro infrastructure through PAYONE in Germany and Austria, as both acquirer and technical service provider. Meanwhile its bank-facing division shrank 7.1% organically in the first half of 2026 and will not return to growth before the second half of 2027 ([Worldline H1 2026 results presentation](https://investors.worldline.com/content/dam/investors-worldline-com/assets/documents/presentations/2026/20260730-worldline-h1-2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

The euro legal-tender file moved into trilogue after the plenary confirmed the mandate on 08/07/2026. The duty only bites through a Commission implementing act that defines the indicators, so the first half of 2027 is the earliest it could matter ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Accessibility rules already require self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 to be replaced or retrofitted by 28/06/2030. The pending payments package would forbid making authentication depend on owning a smartphone. Those are two independent reasons the attended and self-service estate stays in scope ([Council of the EU — ST 8221/26, Payment Services Regulation](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-8221-2026-INIT/en/pdf)).
outlooks.rationale:
The reason to make this call now is protective as much as commercial. The pilot list published on 14/07/2026 created named banks with a contractual duty and a readiness date in the second half of 2027. That is a concrete terminal build to sell this autumn.

In the same fortnight the rulebook confirmed that the machine use cases are deprioritised, and a re-check on 27/08/2026 confirmed it again. Someone is likely to tell the market that the digital euro requires new machines. Separating the funded and unfunded halves before the 13/10/2026 rollout-strategy session keeps the terminal sale credible and stops the machine estate being mis-sold.
cite_ungrounded: Everything on the payments-scheme side — the memorandum of understanding with the European Payments Council and the code-based payment standard named as potentially covering machine transactions — is reported through secondary reading only, because the scheme body's site was blocked to every route this cycle and none of its dates is verified at primary.

The cash-access-point density indicator rests on a Parliament summary page last updated before the committee vote, so it describes a draft report rather than the adopted negotiating mandate, and is not verified in the mandate articles.
The banknote-redesign demand cycle from around 2029 rests on a single manufacturer's investor guidance and on one research unit; the regulation workstream filed no row on it at all.
The list of named pilot participants is assembled from several per-market rows rather than read off one published list, so treat the roster as compiled rather than authoritative.
